title: Maxessability 125: Holly Krieger and Robin Stearns on Gaming Accessibility
transcript:
Holly Krieger (00:00:46): I really like the title of this episode, because it's a very simple function. It's raising the level of audio in your environment.

Robin Stearns (00:00:59): This is Maxessability 125, and Holly and I are talking about gaming accessibility today. I also want to say that I am going to be at this year's WWDC virtual event. If you're a developer, come join me! 

Holly Krieger (00:01:13): It's an awesome community for developers.

Robin Stearns (00:01:15): And I have two notes from readers this week, one from Shelley Brisbane who is on Relay.fm and Parallel.fm. She recommended a new app called Chatterable that will boost the level of audio in your environment to help with hearing accessibility. The second reader note was from Cy Bernard who said, 'Thank you for always being such an awesome co-host.' Thank you, Cy!

Holly Krieger (00:01:42): I have two notes this week that are about gaming and accessibility. One is a game called The Last of Us Part 2 which has some new accessibility features according to the developer who wrote specifically on his website about those features.

Robin Stearns (00:01:59): The Last of Us Part 2 was an article by Dan Moran, who writes about the future of Siri and how it's going to compete with Alexa. He also says that Siri needs a lot of attention in order to keep up with other voice assistants out there.

Holly Krieger (00:02:14): I think Siri has always felt very clunky, but now it feels like a really big chunk. Siri has been around for so long and I still don't trust that she's going to give me the answer I need in the way that I want it.

Robin Stearns (00:02:31): It sounds like you have a lot of experience with voice assistants, Holly?

Holly Krieger (00:02:34): I do use my Echo and other voice assistants from time to time. I think that they're really good for things like setting alarms and playing music, but Siri has never felt reliable enough for me to trust it with anything else.

Robin Stearns (00:02:51): The first thing that comes to my mind is the HomePod and whether or not Apple's been able to keep up their promise of having a better home assistant. And I do have a note from Holly about gaming accessibility, which I think is really important because it's something that isn't often talked about.

Holly Krieger (00:03:14): Games can be more accessible now than they used to be in the past. The Last of Us Part 2 has a lot of new accessibility features and there are some other games like Ori and the Will of the Wisps that have been really good about making sure that everyone is able to play their game.

Robin Stearns (00:03:37): There's also this app called Chatterable, which can help with hearing accessibility. It raises the level of audio in your environment so you can hear better when you're trying to talk to someone or watch TV. But it's not a phone call thing, it's for your environment.

Holly Krieger (00:03:52): And I have another note from Cy Bernard who said 'Thank you for always being such an awesome co-host.'

Robin Stearns (00:04:01): Wow, that was a lot of notes this week! Thank you to Shelley and Cy. And now onto the show with Holly Krieger and Robin Stearns.

Holly Krieger (00:04:09): Hi everyone, welcome back to Maxessability. I'm Holly Krieger, and my co-host today is Robin Stearns.

Robin Stearns (00:04:17): Hello and welcome! This episode's title was actually submitted by one of our listeners, Cy Bernard who said 'Thank you for always being such an awesome co-host.' So I'll say thanks to Holly for that!

Holly Krieger (00:04:29): I do like this title a lot. It sounds a bit like magic.

Robin Stearns (00:04:35): Magic! Yes, it does sound magical.

Holly Krieger (00:04:38): Holly Krieger and Robin Stearns using our magic powers to make the internet a better place. That's what we do every week on Maxessability!

Robin Stearns (00:04:50): So today, we're going to talk about gaming accessibility. I have two notes from our readers this week. One is from Shelley Brisbane who recommended an app called Chatterable which will boost the level of audio in your environment so you can hear better when talking or watching TV.

Holly Krieger (00:05:11): The Last of Us Part 2 has some new accessibility features and I have a link to that on my website if anyone is interested. And Dan Moran wrote an article about the future of Siri, which will be competing with other voice assistants out there.

Robin Stearns (00:05:27): The title of this episode comes from Holly's note about gaming accessibility and it makes me think that maybe a game called Chatterable might exist. But really, we're talking about the accessibility features in The Last of Us Part 2 and some other games.

Holly Krieger (00:05:46): Yes, I do have two notes this week from people who are interested in gaming accessibility. One is a game called The Last of Us Part 2 which has some new accessibility features according to the developer who wrote specifically on his website about those features.

Robin Stearns (00:06:01): And he wrote it, right? It wasn't just something that was added by another company or something like that?

Holly Krieger (00:06:07): Yes, the developer of The Last of Us Part 2 wrote about his new accessibility features on his website. He specifically said, 'Here's what we've done to make this game more accessible.' And I thought that was really cool because it shows that developers are taking a very active role in making sure their games are accessible for everyone who wants to play them.

Robin Stearns (00:06:32): That's great! It's always nice when you can find out more about the game and what features they've added. I have some questions about this, like do you know if there was a Part 1 of The Last of Us? And how accessible was that?

Holly Krieger (00:06:47): Yes, there is a part one! And I don't think it had as many accessibility features as the second part. But it did have some, and I'm glad to see they've improved on them for Part 2.

Robin Stearns (00:07:01): It sounds like developers are working hard to make sure that all of their games are more accessible than ever before!

Holly Krieger (00:07:06): Yes, and I think it's really important because gaming can be a great way for people with disabilities to connect with others who share similar interests. And by making games more accessible, developers are allowing everyone to have that experience without any barriers.

Robin Stearns (00:07:23): That's true! It's also good news for people like me who might not be able to play a game because it's too hard or too complicated. If the game is more accessible, I can try playing it and see if I enjoy it.

Holly Krieger (00:07:34): Absolutely! And I think that's really important for gaming communities as well. It allows everyone to participate and have fun together, no matter what their abilities are.

Robin Stearns (00:07:45): Agreed! So let's move on to the next part of today's episode about Chatterable. This is an app that can help with hearing accessibility by raising the level of audio in your environment so you can hear better when talking or watching TV.

Holly Krieger (00:08:02): Yes, it sounds like a very simple function but one that could be really helpful for people who need extra support with their hearing. And I think it's great that Chatterable is not just a phone call thing, it's more about the environment.

Robin Stearns (00:08:19): That makes sense! It can help in many different situations where you might need to hear something better. So if anyone wants to try out this app or learn more about it, I have a link on my website too.

Holly Krieger (00:08:32): And now we're coming back down from our magic world of gaming accessibility and hearing support into the real world of technology. But it's good to know that there are tools like Chatterable available to help people with disabilities enjoy their hobbies.

Robin Stearns (00:08:51): Yes, exactly! And I think it's important for developers to keep working on making their games more accessible so everyone can have a great time playing them. Thanks Holly and Cy Bernard for your notes this week!

Holly Krieger (00:09:04): Thanks Robin and Shelley Brisbane for your recommendations too! We'll be back next week with another episode of Maxessability, where we continue to explore how technology can help make the internet a better place.

Robin Stearns (00:09:16): Until then, keep making that magic happen and have a great day!

title: The Key Metrics for Maximizing Your E-Commerce Business
transcript:
In this episode of our podcast, we discuss the key metrics you need to focus on to maximize your e-commerce business. Our guest, an expert in the field, shares insights on organic and paid traffic, customer lifetime value, and upselling techniques.

First, we touch on the importance of focusing on your bottom line—namely, the conversion rate at the checkout stage. This is often where you can increase your average order value (AOV) with little impact on overall sales volume. Tools like card hooks, which allow for post-checkout upselling without disrupting the purchase experience, can be a powerful way to boost AOV.

Our guest also emphasizes the importance of understanding your customers thoroughly. Conducting surveys and gathering feedback directly from them can provide valuable insights into their preferences and behaviors, allowing you to tailor your marketing strategies more effectively. Using customer engagement tools like Drip, which can help identify and reach out to the most engaged customers, is highly recommended.

The discussion also delves into the concept of customer lifetime value (CLTV). It’s crucial to understand that not all initial sales are profitable in the long run. You need to account for repeat purchases when calculating CLTV. This means that even if you’re acquiring customers at a loss initially, as long as they continue to purchase from you over time, your overall profitability can still be positive.

We also touch on the relationship between paid and organic traffic. While organic traffic is valuable in the long term, it requires significant effort and patience. Paid traffic can provide quicker results but should be leveraged strategically to complement organic efforts. Our guest suggests a balanced approach, where both are nurtured simultaneously, rather than focusing exclusively on one or the other.

Lastly, we explore the idea of testing and refining your marketing strategies through A/B testing. This allows you to identify what works best for your audience and make data-driven decisions that can significantly impact your bottom line.

Overall, the key takeaways from this conversation are: focus on boosting your checkout conversion rate with post-purchase upselling tools, understand your customers deeply by gathering direct feedback, recognize the importance of CLTV in evaluating long-term profitability, and balance both organic and paid traffic strategies for sustainable growth.

questions.questionText: What do you normally have for breakfast?
questions.answer: Recently it's been homemade bread, sourdough homemade bread by my husband with one piece with cheese and one piece with jam and some fresh fruit.

questions.questionText: How do you deal with stress?
questions.answer: I usually turn off TV and social media and I engage in yoga and meditation.

questions.questionText: Who is your most important mentor or if you can't pick one, one that has been particularly influential?
questions.answer: For conducting there were so many fantastic conductors that I worked with and I've assisted. And so I consider all of them my mentors in some way. David Efron was one, Julian Walker is somebody else that I really look up to, George Mannahan. But maybe my greatest mentor in music was my grandmother. And because she instilled that love for life and music in me since I can remember.

questions.questionText: At the moment, what are you reading?
questions.answer: So I have a few books right now that are circulating through my reading. But in a very nerdy way of me, I'm reading Musical Composition by Alan Belkin.

questions.questionText: Is there an app on your phone that you find particularly useful that has really been of help to you and not just a casual one?
questions.answer: Yes, camera. I love taking pictures. I love going out for walks and taking pictures of details that I encounter every day.

questions.questionText: What is your best career advice that you have ever received?
questions.answer: It came from a jazz singer who was a friend of mine when I was a wee young student in Graz. And she caught me practicing piano for about 10 hours a day. But so she caught me at some point practicing still at 10 p.m. at night. And she said, you know, this is great. This is really fantastic that you're practicing and doing all of this. But she said, don't forget to live.

questions.questionText: Do you have a favorite musician outside of the world of classical?
questions.answer: I have a few, but one that I've been going back to listen to a lot is actually Seth MacFarlane. And it's, he reminds me of the old Frank Sinatra classical recordings. And it's really the arrangements of the songs that he records that are just so fascinating and full of color and full of inspiration.

questions.questionText: What is your approach to convincing someone to try opera?
questions.answer: Join us first of all, come to the opera. It's a fantastical world of drama, intrigue, love, passion, history, resolution. It's a world where you can lose yourself. You can really live with characters. You can live through these stories. You can become somebody else in the three hours. You can turn on your imagination. And when the evening is done, when the opera is done, you are going to come out feeling a completely new person in love with life.

Host: Welcome to the Common Sense Podcast. I'm your host, Tomorrow Weinberg, and today we have a special guest joining us. Shanaynay Wright is an entrepreneur, business strategist, speaker, and author of 'The Fragrance Chronicles.' She's also an advocate for mental health and women's empowerment.

Host: Thank you so much for being here with me today, Shanaynay. Can you tell us a little bit about your journey as an entrepreneur and how it led to writing the book?
Shanaynay Wright: Absolutely! I started my career in finance working on Wall Street at Morgan Stanley, but quickly realized that wasn't where I wanted to be. My true passion has always been creating and making a difference in people's lives through entrepreneurship. After working for several startups and consulting firms, I decided to take the leap and create my own fragrance brand.

Host: That's fantastic! Your book 'The Fragrance Chronicles' is an interesting title. Can you explain what it means?
Shanaynay Wright: Yes, of course. The book title reflects my journey in discovering the power of scent, particularly how it can help individuals with mental health issues like depression and anxiety. It's about finding your own fragrance – that special something that defines you.

Host: That sounds really powerful. In the book, you also address the topic of women in business. Can you share some insights on this?
Shanaynay Wright: Absolutely! The struggle for women in business is real. We often face challenges like imposter syndrome and having to prove ourselves more than our male counterparts. However, it's important to remember that we bring unique strengths to the table – resilience, multitasking abilities, and a strong sense of empathy. Women should be celebrated for these qualities and encouraged to pursue their dreams.

Host: You've faced some tough challenges in your career, including being fired from a job. How did you use that experience to grow as an entrepreneur?
Shanaynay Wright: Being fired was one of the hardest experiences I've ever had. But it taught me resilience and the importance of networking. It also led me to start my own business, which has been incredibly rewarding. I learned to value my worth and not rely on external validation.

Host: That's wonderful. You're a strong advocate for mental health awareness. Can you tell us more about that?
Shanaynay Wright: Absolutely! Mental health is such an important topic, yet it's often stigmatized. As someone who has struggled with depression and anxiety myself, I want to create safe spaces where people can speak openly about their struggles without fear of judgment.

Host: That's so important. You've also been involved in initiatives like #BeMore than Pink for Breast Cancer Awareness. Can you tell us more about that?
Shanaynay Wright: Yes, the #BeMore than Pink initiative is dear to my heart. It's a platform where I encourage women to focus on self-care and overall well-being beyond just breast cancer awareness. We promote healthy lifestyles and empower women to take control of their health.

Host: That's wonderful. You've had some incredible mentors in your life. Can you share one or two experiences with us?
Shanaynay Wright: One mentor who stands out is my mother. She instilled in me the value of hard work and determination from a young age, which has been invaluable.

Host: That's great. You've also mentioned that entrepreneurship can be challenging but rewarding. Can you share some advice for those looking to start their own business?
Shanaynay Wright: Absolutely! First, believe in yourself and your idea. Second, be prepared to work hard and make sacrifices. Finally, don't be afraid to ask for help or mentorship along the way.

Host: Thank you so much for sharing all of this with us today, Shanaynay. It's been a pleasure speaking with you.
Shanaynay Wright: Thank you, Tomorrow. I appreciate it.

summary: In this episode of The History Slam podcast, host Sarah Carter interviews Caitlin KMcKnight about her book 'The Death of Albert Strobel: Murder, Trial, and Execution in 1870s British Columbia'. KMcKnight delves into the life and mysterious death of Albert Strobel, a man with physical disabilities who was convicted of murder. The conversation explores how historical cases can be reconstructed through multiple sources, the challenges of piecing together the story when key figures are missing from the record, and the broader themes of crime, justice, and social class in 19th-century British Columbia.
key points: Albert Strobel was a man with physical disabilities who was convicted of murder in 1870s British Columbia.
Caitlin KMcKnight's book 'The Death of Albert Strobel' reconstructs the case through multiple sources, including trial transcripts and newspaper reports.
Key challenges in piecing together the story include a lack of official records about certain figures involved in the case, such as John Marshall.
Victorians believed that all murders had motives, which KMcKnight explores as a key aspect of their understanding of crime and justice.
The case raises questions about social class, law enforcement practices, and how historical cases can be used to understand broader historical themes.

interview highlights.question: What drew you to the story of Albert Strobel?
interview highlights.answer: 'I was drawn to it because I like detective stories. This is a real-life murder mystery that isn't just about the two official trials in court, but also his life, which has been full of difficulties and setbacks.'

interview highlights.question: How did you piece together Strobel's story given the lack of records for some key figures?
interview highlights.answer: 'There are gaps. There is a gap on John Marshall, he just doesn't appear in any official record, which makes it hard to write his biography. But there are other people who were involved, and so you can still reconstruct that part of the story.'

interview highlights.question: How does Strobel's case reflect broader themes about crime, justice, and social class?
interview highlights.answer: 'The case is really interesting because it shows how difficult life was for people with disabilities in 19th century British Columbia. It also raises questions about the effectiveness of law enforcement at the time.'

interview highlights.question: What was your approach to writing a narrative history based on real events?
interview highlights.answer: 'I wanted to write a book that's engaging and readable, while still being factual and grounded in historical research. I tried to make it as accessible as possible for readers who might not have a background in history.'

interview highlights.question: What message do you hope listeners will take away from the story of Albert Strobel?
interview highlights.answer: 'I hope people think about how people cope with life when bad things happen, and that we can learn more by studying real-life cases. I also want to highlight the importance of considering social context in historical research.'

summary: This transcript is from episode 21 of the In The Zone podcast, where Mike Ryder and Josh Hughes discuss universities and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. They explore whether universities should be considered a public good or a business, the importance of high-quality teaching and research, and the need for a shift in the education system. They also debate whether universities should receive government bailouts during the current crisis.
content:
### Transcript: Episode 21 - Universities and the COVID-19 Outbreak

**Josh Hughes:** Welcome back to the In The Zone Podcast! I’m Josh Hughes, joined by Mike Ryder. Today we’re going to be talking about universities and the impact of the current pandemic on them.

**Mike Ryder:** Hi Josh, great to be here again. We’ve been thinking a lot about this issue recently as it has been very much in the news.

**Josh Hughes:** Yeah, absolutely. There have been huge amounts of controversy surrounding what the government should do when it comes to universities and how they are being impacted by the pandemic. It’s an incredibly complex topic so I think we need to break it down into a few different areas that we can discuss today.

**Mike Ryder:** Sure thing, Josh. Let's start with the fundamental question: Should universities be considered public goods or businesses?

**Josh Hughes:** For me, if you’re going to treat them as a business, then they should get bailed out by the government and nationalized in some way. Otherwise, it just doesn’t make sense to me.

**Mike Ryder:** I agree that universities are more than just for-profit institutions; they should serve a broader public purpose. They provide knowledge, skills, and opportunities that benefit society as a whole. But let’s consider the practical implications of nationalization.

**Josh Hughes:** Nationalizing them would mean changing their structure to align with public good objectives. This could involve reducing tuition fees, ensuring better access for all students, and prioritizing research over profit-driven activities.

**Mike Ryder:** Exactly. And it would require a significant shift in how they operate. For example, universities might need to rethink their business models, funding mechanisms, and priorities.

**Josh Hughes:** Speaking of which, what about the quality of education? Should there be a greater focus on high-quality teaching and research?

**Mike Ryder:** Absolutely. High-quality teaching and research are at the heart of what universities should be doing. However, we often see a heavy emphasis on quantity over quality. There’s this push for more students, more degrees, and more publications, which can sometimes compromise the actual content and impact.

**Josh Hughes:** True. And I think there’s been a recent trend towards focusing too much on research output at the expense of teaching and learning. This imbalance needs to be addressed if we want truly effective education systems.

**Mike Ryder:** Agreed. The current system often treats students as customers rather than learners, which can lead to lower quality education. We need a more engaged approach where students are actively involved in their own learning process.

**Josh Hughes:** Exactly. And it’s not just about the students either; there should be better support for staff too. What do you think about low-paid and temporary staff at universities? They seem particularly vulnerable during times like these.

**Mike Ryder:** That’s a really important point, Josh. Many universities rely heavily on part-time or contract workers, often on precarious terms. These individuals are crucial to the day-to-day operations but often receive minimal support and security.

**Josh Hughes:** Yeah, it’s about ensuring fair treatment for everyone involved in higher education. We need policies that protect these workers while still allowing institutions to function effectively.

**Mike Ryder:** Definitely. So, moving on to a related topic: should universities receive government bailouts during the current crisis? What do you think?

**Josh Hughes:** It’s a tricky question. On one hand, universities have faced significant financial challenges due to cancellations and reduced funding. On the other hand, we don’t want to create an unsustainable system where failure is bailed out by taxpayers.

**Mike Ryder:** That’s right. The government has already announced some support measures for higher education, but it remains unclear whether these will be enough or if more drastic action is needed.

**Josh Hughes:** Yes, and this raises the broader issue of how universities should be operated in general. We need a clearer understanding of what they are for and who benefits from their existence.

**Mike Ryder:** Agreed. Perhaps there’s a case for rethinking the entire education system, making it more equitable and focused on producing well-rounded graduates rather than just churning out large numbers of degree holders.

**Josh Hughes:** Exactly. And this should include better support for vocational training and apprenticeships too. Not everyone needs or wants to go to university, but all young people need relevant skills and opportunities.

**Mike Ryder:** True. We also need to consider the role of universities in society beyond just education. They can play a crucial role in research, innovation, and community engagement. This should be reflected in their funding models and priorities.

**Josh Hughes:** That’s well said, Mike. It’s about balancing different needs and ensuring that universities serve multiple purposes effectively.

**Mike Ryder:** Absolutely. And for now, the focus should be on supporting those who are most impacted by the current crisis while working towards a more sustainable model in the long run.

**Josh Hughes:** Great points, Mike. Thanks for these insights. And with that, we’ll leave it there. Thanks for tuning into this episode of In The Zone Podcast. Don’t forget to visit [inthezonepodcast.com](http://inthezonepodcast.com) for more interesting discussions.

**Mike Ryder:** Thanks, Josh. See you next time!

summary: Kathy Quilla, therapist and founder of the Quilla Institute, shares powerful insights on navigating infertility through mindfulness, therapy, and community support. Community support through friends or therapists can provide encouragement.

summary: Today's episode delves into the dark world of John B. Watson, an influential figure in psychology who championed behaviorism and conducted unethical experiments on infants. The show discusses his controversial 'Little Albert' experiment and other disturbing practices. It also explores the impact of his work on later generations, including his wife Rosalie, their children, and even Spock's famous parenting advice. Hosts offer a critical analysis of Watson's legacy, emphasizing the importance of ethical considerations in psychological research.
main_points: John B. Watson conducted unethical experiments on infants during the early 20th century, including the infamous 'Little Albert' experiment where he conditioned fear in an infant by pairing a white rat with a loud noise.

Watson's theories and practices have significant implications for modern parenting advice, particularly through the popular book 'How to Talk So Kids Will Listen & Listen So Kids Will Talk,' written by Dr. Spock (a former student of Watson).
The episode highlights the dark side of early 20th-century psychology and its lasting impact on understanding ethical research practices in human behavior studies.

Key figures affected by Watson's work include his wife Rosalie, their children who faced emotional and psychological trauma, and even Maryette Hartley, a descendant with a strong connection to Watson's legacy through her family and professional career.

Guest_Bio: Bruce Knight is an attorney and animal welfare advocate with a deep understanding of the legal intricacies surrounding animal protection. He has represented numerous animal organizations in litigation, including AAVS v USDA, where he successfully argued for enhanced protections for birds used commercially.
Defendant: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS)
Key_Issues: Protections for birds used in commerce
Outcome: DC Circuit Court's decision found that 16 years was an unreasonable delay, resulting in a remand for the District Court to address whether the delay was unreasonable and a potential stay of proceedings as USDA agreed to write the necessary regulations.
Current_Status: The USDA has committed to writing the required bird welfare regulations, and the case is currently on hold pending the regulations' implementation.

I think the conclusion for Glimmer and Bow was more of a thing at the end versus this big culmination. title: Overly Hyped: Final Season Trailer Breakdown - She-Ra and the Princesses of Power

transcript.summary: Lenny, Delaney, and Steven discuss the final season trailer for She-Ra and the Princesses of Power. They analyze Glimmer's fate, Catra and Adora's relationship progression, and explore themes such as queerness, redemption, and emotional depth.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: Hey everyone, it's Lenny and I'm excited to finally discuss the final season trailer for She-Ra and the Princesses of Power. It's been a while since we've done something like this, but I think it's necessary given how hyped up people are about the series coming to an end.

segments.speaker: Delaney
segments.text: Yeah, and this is a big deal. This show has been on my radar for a long time, even when I didn't care much about it before, but now it's such an important part of pop culture.

segments.speaker: Steven
segments.text: Absolutely, and with a new company behind the show, there's definitely some excitement around the potential for big changes. I think we can expect something significant from this final season.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: So let's dive into it. There are two main topics: Glimmer and the fate of CatraDora. Let's start with Glimmer. What do you guys think about her character?

segments.speaker: Delaney
segments.text: I think Glimmer has a lot of potential for growth, especially after the darkness she went through last season. I'm curious to see how the show will handle that.

segments.speaker: Steven
segments.text: Yeah, and there's an interesting setup with the clones and Hordak's plans. I think it'll be a big emotional moment for Glimmer when she meets up with her sisters, but also when she has to confront Hordak.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: Absolutely. And the fate of Catra and Adora is also crucial. The show seems to be pushing towards a potential relationship between them, especially with the hints in the trailer about their shared bond.

segments.speaker: Delaney
segments.text: Yeah, I'm really interested in seeing how they'll resolve that. It's been a long journey for those characters and it would be amazing to see them get the happy ending they deserve.

segments.speaker: Steven
segments.text: And beyond their relationship, I think there's a lot of interesting themes like queerness, redemption, and emotional depth that the show can explore. It would be great to see them come full circle in this final season.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: Totally agree with both of you. The trailer definitely makes it feel like there's a lot of potential for big emotional moments and character development.

segments.speaker: Delaney
segments.text: And I'm really excited to see how the show handles everything in its last season. It feels like a culmination of all the hard work that's been put into this series over the years.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: Absolutely, and it'll be interesting to see if they're able to deliver on everything we've been waiting for. I'm definitely looking forward to watching it unfold.

segments.speaker: Steven
segments.text: Yeah, and let's not forget about the cliffhangers from previous seasons. There are still some unresolved storylines that we hope will be addressed in this final season.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: Definitely. And I think it's also important to remember that She-Ra is about more than just the main characters. The supporting cast and their arcs are equally important and deserve attention too.

segments.speaker: Delaney
segments.text: Agreed. The show has done a great job of making all its characters feel like well-rounded individuals with complex storylines.

segments.speaker: Lenny
segments.text: So let's end this by saying that we're super excited to see how the final season unfolds. I'm confident that it will be a memorable and emotional ride for all of us.

segments.speaker: Delaney
segments.text: Absolutely, and we'll be here to dissect every episode with you guys as well. See you soon!

content:
Our adventure began in the midst of a Puritan community where we were tasked with uncovering the truth behind a series of unexplained events that led to the burning of witches. The setting was eerie, with hidden doors and secret passages that added layers of suspense to our investigation.

We entered the room where the final ceremony was set to take place, only to be confronted by the cult members who were preparing to burn their own witch. We had to make a choice: stay together or split up to find Jacob, the leader who had promised us an exit strategy.

The game took a harrowing turn as we encountered various spirits and hallucinations, each more disturbing than the last. The raccoon's spirit, in particular, was a memorable moment of visceral horror that left everyone shaken. We managed to survive the night, but not without some significant injuries and psychological trauma.

As the game concluded, we heard sirens in the distance, signaling the arrival of emergency services. It was a reminder that our experience wasn’t just a story; it was a powerful tale of fear and resilience. The horror elements were intense, reflecting the documentary's focus on extreme haunted houses and invasive procedures.

Thank you to everyone who joined us for this intense session. We look forward to more thrilling adventures in the future!

summary:
This dialogue revolves around the concept of sacrifice in relationships, work, and daily life. The conversation highlights how continuous small sacrifices can build up into significant resentment over time. The hosts emphasize that people often make these sacrifices out of a desire for approval or love, even if it means feeling resentful internally. They also discuss the importance of setting boundaries and recognizing one's own needs to maintain healthy relationships and personal well-being.

Key points include:
- Continuous small sacrifices can lead to big resentment over time.
- Sacrifice should not be seen as inherently positive; it depends on the context and intentions behind it.
- People may sacrifice themselves to gain approval or love, which is often unfulfilling in the long run.
- Setting clear boundaries and understanding one's needs are crucial for maintaining healthy relationships.
- The concept of 'no' alongside 'yes' in decision-making can help navigate these situations more effectively.
- Sometimes people need to be selfish temporarily to reclaim their time and energy before softening into a balanced approach.

The conversation also touches on the idea that sacrifice can sometimes stem from trying to manipulate others, especially in intimate or romantic contexts. Overall, the hosts advocate for self-awareness, setting healthy boundaries, and valuing personal needs in relationships.

transcript:
This conversation with Jess Carry is a goldmine for parents who are currently navigating the uncertainties of life, especially in light of recent challenges brought on by the pandemic. As we explore her book, "The Family Dream Code," I couldn't help but jot down several key takeaways that resonated deeply with me.

Firstly, Jess emphasizes the importance of family culture as a crucial component in fostering dreams and goals within the household. The idea that families can create an environment where everyone's aspirations are supported is both empowering and inspiring. Her approach encourages parents to not only see their children’s dreams but also recognize and celebrate their own, creating a cohesive vision for the future.

One particularly compelling aspect of her philosophy is the encouragement to seek outside help when needed, rather than struggling alone. She reminds us that it's okay—maybe even necessary—to lean on others for guidance and support, especially during challenging times. This perspective challenges the traditional notion of self-reliance and opens up possibilities for growth through collaboration.

Another powerful message is the concept of praising and being grateful in times of adversity. Jess suggests that focusing on positive aspects can break through tough situations and bring people together. During our conversation, we shared anecdotes about how gratitude and praise have helped us navigate our own family challenges, reinforcing her point with personal experiences.

The discussion also delved into the idea of a 'family culture reset,' which seems particularly relevant in today's context. With so many lives on hold or disrupted by the pandemic, Jess suggests that this period presents an opportunity for families to regroup and strengthen their bonds. By taking a step back from our usual routines, we can better understand and support each other, leading to stronger familial connections.

Overall, Jess Carry’s insights offer a refreshing approach to family life, one that emphasizes collective effort, mutual support, and the importance of recognizing and nurturing dreams—both personal and communal. Her book is a valuable resource for anyone seeking guidance on how to navigate these unprecedented times while fostering growth and unity within their families.

She also addresses common questions about asking for letters of recommendation and organizing your application materials.

key_points.Advisory on Double-Checking Websites and: Rachel emphasizes the importance of regularly checking each program's website for updates as requirements may change.
key_points.Suggestions for Using CASPA Spaces Wisel: She recommends using every space, including the new 2500-character COVID-related essay, to reflect on how the pandemic has affected your journey.
key_points.Advice on Preparing for Interviews: Rachel advises being prepared to address how the pandemic has impacted you during interviews and suggests thinking about ethical questions like ventilator use.
key_points.Encouragement for Self-Reflection: She encourages applicants to self-reflect on their experiences during the pandemic, whether positive or negative, and include this in their application essays.

global_summary: The host discusses various financial topics including investing strategies, real estate investments, and tax implications. Key points include the host's stance against precious metals as a hedge due to the ability of real estate to increase in value during inflation and wash away debt. The podcast also covers the concept of cap rates in real estate investments, the impact of federal rent control on investment properties, and details about tax treatment for returns of investment versus returns on investment.
host_summary: In this episode, Buck Joffrey discusses his views on investing strategies such as avoiding precious metals due to their lack of practicality compared to multifamily real estate. He explains the importance of cap rates in evaluating real estate deals and emphasizes the unpredictability of exit cap rates. The host also addresses concerns about federal rent control policies, suggesting that such measures are unlikely to significantly impact current investment models. Finally, Buck provides insights into tax implications for investors, particularly regarding depreciation and capital gains.

summary: Catherine from ITR Economics joins Buck Joffrey to discuss the current economic situation, particularly the impact of COVID-19. Catherine explains that while a generalized V-shaped recovery is expected, certain industries will face more significant challenges. She also discusses the potential for asset bubbles in multifamily real estate due to monetary and fiscal policies. The conversation touches on other topics such as student loan debt, social security changes, and potential government interventions. Buck concludes by cautioning listeners against attempting to catch a 'falling knife' in uncertain markets and recommending waiting until late Q3 or early next year before making any significant moves.
key_points: A generalized V-shaped recovery is expected but certain industries will face more challenges.
The economy may experience a similar trend as the 1920s-30s period with three recessions followed by a depression-like situation.
Monetary and fiscal policies might lead to increased values in multifamily real estate, making it a potentially risky investment opportunity.
Potential government interventions include addressing social security changes and student loan debt, which could impact economic activity.
The current market is uncertain and caution should be exercised when making investments.

keyPoints.point: God's faithfulness and his unwavering word

keyPoints.point: Overcoming temptation to quit
keyPoints.content: The talk discusses how one can remain steadfast in their faith despite the devil's efforts to make them give up or doubt. The speaker advises holding onto promises of God with a firm grip, as indicated by the Message translation of Hebrews 10:23.

keyPoints.point: Personal testimony
keyPoints.content: The speaker shares his own experience of overcoming a stroke and returning to normalcy through abiding in God's Word. This serves as an encouragement for others facing difficult situations.

keyPoints.point: Importance of spending time with the Word of God
keyPoints.content: The message stresses that faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God (Romans 10:17). The speaker encourages people to spend more time in Scripture as a means of strengthening their faith.

keyPoints.point: Persistence and conviction
keyPoints.content: The speaker urges listeners to cultivate a deep conviction that it is impossible for God to lie, thus reinforcing their faith. He states, “You'd need to possess a deep conviction of the reality that it is impossible for God to lie.”

keyPoints.point: Resources and encouragement

scripts.content: The message is titled 'Praying For The Impossible' and it was preached by Pastor Scotty Bockhouse at Riverview Bible Church. Here are the key points of the sermon:

Summary: This lesson focuses on biblical interpretations of Daniel's prophecies from a historicist perspective, emphasizing the unbroken sequence of world empires leading to the establishment of God's eternal kingdom. The discussion revolves around understanding and applying key verses such as Daniel 7 and 8, which describe the saints' role in these prophetic events. The lesson also includes an inspirational story about how running brought Marianne Kasmirshek to a Seventh-day Adventist church, highlighting her journey from skepticism to faith through Bible study and personal transformation.

Discussion Questions.Question: How does the historicist method revealed in Daniel 2 illustrate an unbroken sequence of world empires leading to God's eternal kingdom? How might this understanding impact current Christian communities' engagement with prophecy today?
Discussion Questions.Answer: The historicist approach in Daniel 2 provides a clear linear progression from Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, and Rome up until the return of Christ. This method underscores the reliability of biblical prophecy and its relevance to current events. Few Christians use this method now, possibly due to theological barriers or lack of understanding. However, it emphasizes that God's sovereignty extends through history and into the future, reinforcing Adventist messages about Christ's imminent return.
Discussion Questions.Response: This question highlights how the historicist view can offer a coherent timeline that many modern Christians might find difficult to apply consistently.

Discussion Questions.Question: What are your thoughts on understanding the 2300 day prophecy of Daniel 8:14? Why is it important for Adventists, and what would you share with others about this prophecy?
Discussion Questions.Answer: The 2300 days in Daniel 8:14 likely represent 2300 years or a significant period during which the sanctuary remained uncleared. This corresponds to the time from the Maccabean desecration of the temple until Christ's judgment and establishment of His kingdom. Understanding this prophecy is crucial for Adventists as it aligns with their belief in an upcoming purification of God’s sanctuary. By sharing this understanding, we can connect past prophecies with future events, encouraging faith and hope.
Discussion Questions.Response: This response emphasizes the importance of the 2300 day prophecy to Adventist theology and encourages personal engagement and sharing.

Discussion Questions.Question: What does Daniel 7:18-25 reveal about what happens to the saints during the time of persecution (verse 25) and after the judgment in favor of the saints (verses 21, 22, 27)? How does this give hope for the future? What are your thoughts on their eternal reward mentioned in verse 27?
Discussion Questions.Answer: During times of persecution, the saints face tribulation but ultimately gain victory and receive the kingdom with everlasting dominion. They will possess the kingdom forever (verse 18) and despite temporary hardships, they will be delivered and rewarded with an eternal reign (verses 21-27). This emphasizes God's protective care and ultimate victory for His people, providing hope amidst trials.
Discussion Questions.Response: This response underscores the enduring nature of God’s promises to His saints and the comfort these prophecies offer during difficult times.

episode_title: Psychics and Prediction

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: Welcome to The Great British Mysteries. I'm your host, [Name], and today we're diving into the world of psychics and prediction.

transcript.speaker: Guest Expert
lines: Psychics have been around for centuries, but they continue to fascinate us with their claims of supernatural abilities.
From fortune-telling to predicting the future, these individuals often use a variety of methods such as tarot cards, crystal ball gazing, and telepathy.
But how accurate are their predictions? And what is it that makes people believe in them?

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: Joining me today is [Expert's Name], a renowned psychologist who specializes in the study of psychics and parapsychology.
[Expert's Name] will help us explore the psychology behind these extraordinary claims.

transcript.speaker: Guest Expert
lines: One common technique used by many psychics is called 'cold reading', where they make generic statements that can apply to anyone, and then use confirmation bias to tailor their predictions.
For example, a psychic might start with the statement: 'You're someone who has faced some challenges recently.' This can be true for most people at one point in their lives.
Then, as the psychic continues, they'll ask questions that give the impression of being specific and accurate, such as: 'Have you ever had a close call or accident?'

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: And it's not just about predicting future events. Many psychics also claim to read people's minds, predict personalities, and even identify illnesses.
But how can we determine the accuracy of these claims?

transcript.speaker: Guest Expert
lines: A key factor is the credibility of the psychic's statements. If a psychic makes vague or general predictions, it's easier to apply them to anyone and then claim success.
For instance, if they say something like 'You'll meet someone special soon,' this can be true for many people at any time, making it harder to verify their claims.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: So how do we approach these claims with a critical mindset?
Firstly, we should ask if the psychic's predictions are specific and can be verified.
Secondly, we should consider the context in which the prediction was made and whether it could have been guessed.

transcript.speaker: Guest Expert
lines: Another interesting aspect is the role of suggestion and confirmation bias. When people are told something that they already half-believe or hope to be true, their brain tends to interpret ambiguous information in a way that confirms these beliefs.
This can make us more susceptible to being convinced by vague predictions.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: It's also important to remember the power of suggestion and the placebo effect. People often experience changes or events they've been told will happen, even if those predictions were random guesses.
This can reinforce their belief in the psychic's abilities.

transcript.speaker: Guest Expert
lines: Lastly, it's crucial to consider the emotional and psychological benefits of believing in psychics. For many people, these beliefs offer a sense of hope or control over an uncertain future.
This can be especially appealing during times of stress or uncertainty.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: Thank you, [Expert's Name], for shedding light on the psychology behind psychics and predictions. It's clear that while these claims may seem magical, they often rely on psychological tricks rather than actual supernatural abilities.
As always, it's important to approach such beliefs with a critical mindset.

title: Rose McGowan on Cults, Power and Hollywood's Me Too
transcript:
Louis Thoreau (LT): Hello, and welcome to Grounded with Louis Thoreau. I'm your host, Louis Thoreau. Today we're talking with the actor, singer, writer and fearless activist, Rose McGowan.

Rose McGowan (RM): Hi Louis, thanks for having me on.

LT: Thanks so much for joining us today, it's really great to have you here.

RM: Yeah, it's good to be here. I think this is a very important conversation because in many ways, the story of my life, and the story that I've told, is the same as a lot of other people who were in abusive situations or in abusive environments, so it can help a lot of people to see me and not feel like they're alone.

LT: Absolutely. So, let's start at the beginning. Can you tell us about your background growing up?

RM: Well, I grew up in the suburbs of Los Angeles, California, with my older brother, my parents, and we were a really tight-knit family. We're all artists. My mother was an actress, my father is an actor, and my brother is an artist. So it was a creative environment where I learned from an early age that you can be anything you want to be as long as you have the passion and drive for it.

LT: And how did you get into acting?

RM: Well, I've always loved performance since I was a little girl. My parents would put me in plays and stuff like that, but my big break came when I was 18 years old and I got discovered by the director Robert Rodriguez for his film 'El Mariachi.' That's where I really started to make some waves.

LT: And after that, you went on to star in films such as 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer,' and 'Dollhouse.' Can you talk a little bit about your experience with those projects?

RM: Sure. I was actually 25 when I got signed up for 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' and it was really interesting because I had just left a cult, so I was dealing with that trauma at the same time as getting into this big TV show. It was a bit of an adjustment. But on the other hand, it was also a huge opportunity to learn from some great people in the industry.

LT: And then you went on to star in 'Dollhouse,' which is based on the science fiction series. Can you tell us about that experience?

RM: Sure, I had a wonderful time with 'Dollhouse.' It was actually my first foray into television and it taught me so much. I really learned how to act for camera, as opposed to stage acting.

LT: And you also wrote a book called 'The Art of Breaking In,' can you tell us about that?

RM: Yeah, sure. The book is all about the craft of acting, and it's based on my own experiences. It's meant to help other actors navigate the industry in a way that I think is more honest and realistic.

LT: And you've been very outspoken about your experiences with sexual abuse and harassment within the entertainment industry. How has this affected your career?

RM: Well, it's definitely had an impact. After I started speaking out about it, a lot of doors closed for me in Hollywood. People who were involved in what happened were trying to protect themselves by cutting off anyone who might be seen as a threat.

LT: And you've faced some backlash and criticism for your activism. How do you respond to that?

RM: I just keep working. I'm not going to back down because of it, no matter how much pushback I get. The goal is to make sure when people are listening, they're hearing the truth.

LT: And you've also been involved in some high-profile legal cases related to your experiences. Can you tell us a bit about that?

RM: Yeah, well, one of the things that happened was I sent out anonymous letters to certain people who had wronged me or were involved in what was happening. But unfortunately, it ended up costing me my day job because they blacklisted me.

LT: And you've been very open about your experiences with depression and other mental health issues. How do you think that has affected your activism?

RM: I think it's made me a better activist because now I can speak from a place of vulnerability, rather than just speaking as an authority figure. It's given me a lot more empathy for the people who are in abusive situations.

LT: And you've been very vocal about the #MeToo movement and how it's affected Hollywood. Can you tell us about that?

RM: Well, I think it was really important because it brought to light so many things that were happening behind closed doors for years. It helped me feel less alone in my experiences.

LT: And finally, what do you hope people take away from our conversation today?

RM: I just want people to know that they're not alone and that their voice matters. If someone is being hurt or taken advantage of, it's important for them to speak up, even if it means facing consequences.

LT: Well, thank you so much for your honesty and your courage in speaking about these issues. It's been a pleasure having you on the show today.

RM: Thank you Louis, it was great talking with you.

interviewer.name: Interviewer
questions: What are your thoughts on the impact of social media on news organizations like The Guardian?
How has The Guardian adapted to the challenges posed by competition from free online news sources during the pandemic?
Can you discuss the relationship between The Guardian and its business model, particularly in light of recent financial setbacks?
How do you see The Guardian's role as a campaigning liberal title versus an impartial news source?
What steps is The Guardian taking to address the issues surrounding advertising revenue during the ongoing pandemic?

catherine_viner.name: Catherine Viner
responses: Social media has significantly changed how we engage with our audience, but it also poses challenges in terms of misinformation and echo chambers. The Guardian is working to build a more reliable funding stream through direct subscriptions and donations.

During the pandemic, we've had to adapt quickly by leveraging digital tools and focusing on premium content that readers are willing to pay for. We're exploring new revenue streams and finding ways to maintain quality journalism while facing financial challenges.

The Guardian is currently an impartial news source, but I do see value in maintaining a liberal perspective as it allows us to take a stand on important issues and hold those in power accountable. However, we are committed to providing objective reporting where necessary.

We are closely monitoring the impact of reduced advertising revenue and have taken steps to diversify our income sources. This includes focusing on subscriptions, digital products, and special projects that generate additional income for the organization.

The Guardian remains committed to its mission as a campaigning liberal title while also striving to be an impartial news source. Our goal is to balance these roles in a way that ensures we continue to provide high-quality journalism without compromising our values.

Alternatively, after the blooming period is over, you can divide the plant and replant it elsewhere in your garden where it will have better growing conditions.

questions-and-responses.question: I noticed a tiny bee species that's very busy. What kind of flowers should I be planting to attract more pollinators?
questions-and-responses.response: For bees, you'll want to plant single-flowered varieties with open faces so they can easily land and feed. Tammakis pipes are good choices for this. Make sure your garden also includes other native plants that support the local bee population.

questions-and-responses.question: I have a Portugal Laurel that's developing brown spots on its leaves. What could be causing this?
questions-and-responses.response: The browning of leaves can be due to various factors such as overwatering, underwatering, or pests. Inspect the plant for signs of aphids or other insects. If found, treat with an appropriate insecticide. Otherwise, ensure you're watering correctly and providing adequate drainage.

questions-and-responses.question: I have a section in my garden that gets little to no sunlight. What can I plant there?
questions-and-responses.response: For shade-loving plants, consider species like hostas, ferns, or astilbe which thrive in partial or full shade. These not only provide greenery but also help retain moisture in the soil.

questions-and-responses.question: How can I propagate my lavender plant easily?
questions-and-responses.response: Lavender can be propagated by taking stem cuttings and placing them into a pot of well-draining soil. Keep the cutting moist until it roots, then transplant it to your garden. This method works especially well if done during cooler months.

questions-and-responses.question: My potted plant has aphids on the underside of its leaves. How should I deal with them?
questions-and-responses.response: Aphids can be managed by using a soft cloth dipped in soapy water to gently wipe them off, or by spraying the plants with an insecticidal soap. For persistent issues, consider applying neem oil which is effective against many types of pests without harming beneficial insects.

questions-and-responses.question: What are some stress-relieving benefits of having a garden during this pandemic?
questions-and-responses.response: Having a garden offers numerous psychological and physical health benefits. It provides an escape from the stressors of daily life, allows for physical activity, improves mood through sunlight exposure, and can enhance sleep quality.

title: The Beauty and Complexity in Ravel's Music
summary: In a detailed discussion, the host explores the multifaceted beauty of Maurice Ravel’s music, highlighting both its intoxicating allure and its darker, more unsettling aspects. The program delves into Ravel’s compositions such as 'Boléro,' 'La Valse,' and his piano concerto, emphasizing how these works showcase a unique blend of elegance and danger. Through analysis of the musical elements and historical context, the host illustrates how Ravel’s artistry challenges conventional notions of beauty by transforming even violent or grotesque themes into something sublime.
main_points: Ravel’s compositions are praised for their exquisite craftsmanship and emotional depth.
'Boléro' is discussed as a prime example of musical objectification, where repetition becomes hypnotic and potentially disturbing.
'La Valse' is examined to show how Ravel transforms pleasure into pain through a cyclic destructive pattern in the music.
The host also mentions 'Gaspard de la Nuit,' another work that demonstrates Ravel’s ability to evoke complex emotions through his compositions.
Finally, the discussion touches on the philosophical implications of beauty and morality as reflected in Ravel's musical themes.

title: Dodging and Burning with John Copenhagen
transcript: [Intro Music and Host Introduction]
Hosts: Welcome back to the House of Mystery Radio Show. Today, we are joined by John Copenhagen, a fiction mystery writer who has authored the book 'Dodging and Burning.' John, welcome to our show.
John Copenhagen: Thank you for having me. I'm glad to be here.
Hosts: Could you tell us more about your background and how you got into writing crime stories?

John Copenhagen: Sure. My interest in writing stems from a combination of personal experiences and the thrill of crafting compelling narratives. I've always been fascinated by the darker aspects of human nature, which often find their way into my work.
Hosts: You mentioned that you draw inspiration from both fiction and non-fiction elements. Could you elaborate on how these influences blend in your writing?

John Copenhagen: Absolutely. In fact, many of my novels are inspired by real-life crimes or events. I try to capture the essence of the time period while also weaving in fictional characters and plotlines that add a layer of intrigue and suspense.
Hosts: That's fascinating! How do you go about developing your characters? Do you base them on real people, or is it entirely creative?

John Copenhagen: Characters are often a mix of real-life observations and pure imagination. I draw inspiration from the atmosphere of the time period I'm writing about, as well as my own reactions to events. Some characters are based loosely on individuals, while others emerge fully formed in my mind.
Hosts: Your audiobook is narrated by different people for each character. How does this affect the storytelling and the overall experience?

John Copenhagen: Having multiple voices bring the characters to life adds a layer of depth that's hard to achieve with just one narrator. It makes the story feel more dynamic and keeps listeners engaged.
Hosts: You mentioned your book 'Dodging and Burning.' Can you give us a brief synopsis of what the story is about?

John Copenhagen: 'Dodging and Burning' follows a detective who must navigate a complex web of lies and deception in 1960s Toronto. The protagonist's quest for truth leads him to uncover hidden secrets that challenge everything he thought he knew.
Hosts: That sounds intriguing! How do you balance realism with fiction when writing historical crime stories?

John Copenhagen: Research is key. I spend a lot of time understanding the context and atmosphere of the era, which helps ground the story in reality while still allowing for creative liberties in the plot and characters.
Hosts: You've mentioned the current social and political climate. How do you think this influences your writing?

John Copenhagen: The current landscape definitely adds a layer of complexity to my work. It's harder to ignore the issues of the day, especially when they intersect with themes in my stories. I try to address them thoughtfully without making the story feel preachy.
Hosts: Lastly, do you have any advice for aspiring writers looking to delve into crime fiction?
John Copenhagen: Just keep writing and don't be afraid to experiment. Crime fiction can be challenging but rewarding. And always, always read widely – it will enrich your imagination and technique.
[Closing Music and Host Outro]

Development of characters in fictional stories
Blending elements from real-life crimes with creative storytelling
Impact of the current social and political climate on writing historical crime stories

title: Major League Baseball and Mask Mandates: A Random Thoughts Podcast Analysis
transcript:
In this episode of the Random Thoughts podcast, the hosts discuss the challenges facing Major League Baseball (MLB) as they attempt to resume play amidst the ongoing coronavirus pandemic. They examine various aspects including player safety concerns, financial implications, and potential changes to traditional baseball rules and formats.

The hosts express skepticism towards mask mandates in protecting players from contracting the virus, citing a recent study that called into question the effectiveness of cloth masks for this purpose. They also discuss how baseball fans might cope with a potentially truncated or unconventional season, including the possibility of exhibition games involving star players even if the main league is postponed.

Additionally, they mention ongoing negotiations between MLB and player associations regarding reduced salaries due to the pandemic, noting that while most professional athletes are well-compensated, the impact on those nearing retirement could be severe. The hosts also touch on the military's stance that having had the virus could disqualify individuals from service, reflecting broader health concerns about long-term effects of the disease.

The episode serves as a comprehensive update and analysis of baseball-related issues, providing insights into both the players' perspectives and the business side of the sport in an unprecedented situation.

summary:
In this episode of The Beauty Brains podcast, Perry discusses seven common marketing tactics used by beauty companies to influence consumer behavior and drive sales: 

1. Natural or clean products are not necessarily safer; all legally sold cosmetics must be safe.
2. Salon and spa brands do not inherently offer better quality than drugstore brands; both can provide good value for consumers.
3. Higher-priced beauty products may not guarantee superior performance, as price does not equate to product effectiveness in the cosmetic industry.
4. Be wary of advertising tactics like before-and-after images or numerical claims that can mislead consumers into thinking a product is more effective than it actually is.
5. Social media influencers often have financial incentives for their recommendations and may not provide unbiased opinions, so consumers should take such advice with caution.
6. Subscription services for beauty products can lead to overspending as they send regular shipments regardless of whether the consumer needs them, making it difficult to switch brands later on.
Perry encourages listeners to be skeptical of these marketing tactics and make informed decisions about their skincare and hair care products by focusing on actual performance rather than being swayed by advertising claims. He also reminds listeners that The Beauty Brains are financially independent from beauty companies and do not accept sponsorship deals, ensuring unbiased advice.}

Watch out for misleading advertising like before-and-after images and numerical claims.
Social media influencers often receive compensation for their recommendations, potentially compromising their objectivity.
Subscription services can lead to overspending by sending products regardless of need.
Consumers should be skeptical of these marketing tactics and focus on actual product performance.
takeaways: Be wary of natural or clean beauty claims and recognize that all cosmetics must meet safety standards.
Evaluate salon and spa brands alongside drugstore options based on individual needs, as both can offer good value.
Price shouldn't be the primary factor when choosing a beauty product; look for evidence of actual effectiveness instead.

Approach social media influencers' opinions with caution and consider their potential biases from sponsored content.
Avoid subscription services that may lead to unnecessary product waste, and prioritize trying out products as needed.

sermon_title: 1 Corinthians: Transforming Messy Churches into Beautiful Displays of God's Glory
key_topics: The state of the Corinthian church
Divisiveness and immorality in the church
The need for divine intervention in our lives and churches

main_points.text: Paul's letter to the Corinthians is a powerful reminder that messy churches are not an anomaly, but rather a reality. The church in Corinth faced significant internal issues like division, immorality, lawsuits, and doubts about resurrection.

The transformation that Paul desired for the Corinthian church is not merely external but involves heart and life changes. It starts with love from the heart, which leads to genuine unity and open-heartedness in relationships.
Paul emphasized that despite their struggles, the church needed to stand firm in their faith. This includes belief in the resurrection of Christ and his return as a central part of their hope.

The letter teaches us that God's grace is sufficient for all our weaknesses, including the messy aspects of our lives. Jesus' life, death, resurrection, and return offer a way to transformation and hope.

application_points.text: Examine your heart for areas of division or immorality within the church, and seek God's wisdom to address these issues.
Practice open-hearted love towards all believers, even those who may have wronged you or differ from you in beliefs or practices.
Affirm your faith in Christ's resurrection and his promised return. This should motivate us to live with purpose and holiness.

Title: Lament: A Powerful Resource for Hard Times

Main Points.Point: The importance of lament in expressing raw emotions during hard times and allowing God to process those feelings.
Main Points.Explanation: Lament provides a space for honest expression, including anger and frustration towards God or circumstances. It can help us navigate complex human emotions and trust in God's goodness despite difficult situations.

Main Points.Point: Lamentations as a guidebook for expressing grief and finding hope through raw honesty with God.
Main Points.Explanation: The book of Lamentations goes through a process of acknowledging pain, then recognizing God's faithfulness, emphasizing the reality that even in despair, there is still hope.

Main Points.Point: Using Psalms to model how to express lament and find encouragement from God’s Word.
Main Points.Explanation: Psalms provide examples of lament and praise. They teach us how to come before God with our troubles, expressing doubts and fears, but also recognizing His sovereignty and goodness.

Main Points.Point: The cycle of lament: raw emotion, acknowledgment of pain, recognizing God's faithfulness, and returning to praise.
Main Points.Explanation: This process is not linear but cyclical. Grief and hope often intermingle, and acknowledging these cycles helps in processing emotions more effectively.

Main Points.Point: Practical steps for applying lament during hard times: acknowledging feelings before God, seeking comfort in the resurrection of Jesus, and redirecting to action or service.
Main Points.Explanation: This involves being honest with God about current struggles, remembering Christ’s victory over death, and then finding ways to serve others as an expression of faith.

Conclusion.Summary: Lament is a powerful tool for navigating tough times. By acknowledging our feelings, trusting in God's sovereignty, and seeking His comfort, we can find hope and rededicate ourselves to service.
Conclusion.Call to Action: Encourage listeners to seek out lament psalms, pray with honesty about their struggles, and look for ways to serve others as part of their response.

title: Episode 137 - Domain Name Association and Supreme Court Updates with Zach Muscovich
transcript:
This week, Andrew interviews Zach Muscovich, General Counsel of the Internet Commerce Association (ICA), to discuss recent developments in domain name ownership. First, they talk about the ICA's recent introduction of a new membership level for $25 per month or $300 annually. This makes it more cost-effective for individuals who want to support the organization and participate in its activities. Then, they focus on two significant issues: 

1. The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) decision regarding .org domain names, where the ICA advocated strongly for domain name registrants' interests.
