title: The Outer Dark #48: Craig Lawrence Giddney on 'Nectar of Nightmare' and the Intersection of Weird Fiction with Social Justice Issues
summary: Scott Nikolay talks to author Craig Lawrence Giddney about his upcoming collection 'Nectar of Nightmare', the intersection of weird fiction with social justice issues, and how authors can use horror as a tool for engaging important societal topics.

transcript.text: Scott Nikolay: Hello, everyone. This is Scott Nikolay, your host for The Outer Dark podcast.
I'm very pleased to have with us today, author Craig Lawrence Giddney. Welcome, Craig.
Craig Lawrence Giddney: Thank you for having me, Scott.

Scott Nikolay: Yeah. So we're going to talk today about your upcoming collection 'Nectar of Nightmare', which is coming out this month very soon from Dim Shores Press. Can you tell us a little bit about the book and what readers can expect?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Sure, Scott. 'Nectar of Nightmare' is a collection that spans multiple genres, but primarily weird fiction, fantasy, horror, all with this kind of dark mythos aesthetic. The stories are all set in an alternate history and they're tied together by these strange and mysterious forces called the Vampyres. So you can expect a lot of monsters, both human and non-human, as well as some political intrigue and social commentary.

Scott Nikolay: That sounds like it will be really interesting to readers. And I understand that the book is also something of a love letter to your hometown, Washington D.C., which you've lived in for over 35 years. Can you tell us more about how that plays into the book?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Absolutely. I wanted 'Nectar of Nightmare' to be a celebration of my home, which has seen so much change and yet still retains this sense of mystery and magic that attracts me as both an author and a person who grew up here.

Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And I understand there are also some nods to literary history in the book, such as references to Mary Shelley's Frankenstein and Edgar Allan Poe. Can you tell us a little bit more about that?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm a big fan of literary history, so there are some references to that in the book, including one story called 'The House of Vampyres' which is set in a fictionalized version of Switzerland where Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein.

Scott Nikolay: That sounds like an exciting addition to the collection. And speaking of literary history, you're also known for your work with the Weird Fiction Review and the weird fiction community in general. Can you tell us a little bit about that?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Sure thing. I've been involved with the Weird Fiction Review since its inception, and it's been an incredible journey to see it grow from just a few people in a forum on a website into this vibrant community of writers, readers, and fans who are dedicated to exploring the weird and the wonderful.
Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And you've also published with other presses such as Zorion Yell Hurston Press. Can you tell us a little bit about your work with that press?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I have two stories coming out in the near future from Zorion Yell Hurston Press as part of their 'The Glow' anthology series, which explores how authors intersect with literary history.

Scott Nikolay: That's really exciting. And I understand that you're also involved in social justice issues and have written about those topics in your work as well. Can you tell us a little bit about how you approach these topics in your writing?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Absolutely, Scott. Horror can be a powerful tool for exploring and engaging with important societal issues like racism and police brutality. I try to use my work as a way to bring attention to these topics and spark conversations about them.

Scott Nikolay: That's really great to hear. And you're not alone in that approach, as we've seen more and more horror writers using their work to address social justice issues. Can you give us an example of how you've done this?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Sure thing. In one story called 'The House of Vampyres', I explore the idea of race and identity through the lens of vampires, who are often depicted as non-human in horror fiction. By making them human, I'm able to comment on the way society dehumanizes people of color.

Scott Nikolay: That's a really interesting approach. And you've also mentioned that you're involved with the Washington Horror Writers Association. Can you tell us a little bit about your work there and how it relates to your writing?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm president of the Washington Horror Writers Association, which is a great group of writers who are dedicated to supporting each other and promoting horror in all its forms. Being involved with that community has definitely influenced my writing and given me new ideas for stories.
Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And you're also working on a novel called 'A Cinnamon and Honey Heart'. Can you tell us a little bit about that?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm excited to be working on this novel right now. It's set in an alternate 1920s where vampires and werewolves live among humans, but the city is also under threat from a supernatural entity that wants to destroy it.
Scott Nikolay: That sounds really exciting. And you've mentioned before that you're working on another project called 'Chapel of Nectar'. Can you tell us more about that?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm currently working on a novella called 'Chapel of Nectar' which is set in an alternate 20th century where vampires and werewolves live among humans, but the city is also under threat from a supernatural entity that wants to destroy it.
Scott Nikolay: And you've mentioned before that you're involved with the Zorion Yell Hurston Press 'The Glow' series. Can you tell us more about that?
Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm one of several authors contributing to this anthology series which explores how writers intersect with literary history.
Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And you've also mentioned before that you're involved in the Weird Fiction Review. Can you tell us more about your work there?
Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm a co-founder and editor-in-chief of the Weird Fiction Review which is an online magazine dedicated to exploring the weird and wonderful in fiction.
Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And you're also involved with the Washington Horror Writers Association. Can you tell us more about your work there?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm president of the Washington Horror Writers Association which is a great group of writers who are dedicated to supporting each other and promoting horror in all its forms.
Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And you're also working on a novel called 'A Cinnamon and Honey Heart'. Can you tell us more about that?

Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm excited to be working on this novel right now. It's set in an alternate 1920s where vampires and werewolves live among humans, but the city is also under threat from a supernatural entity that wants to destroy it.
Scott Nikolay: That sounds really exciting. And you've mentioned before that you're involved with the Zorion Yell Hurston Press 'The Glow' series. Can you tell us more about that?
Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm one of several authors contributing to this anthology series which explores how writers intersect with literary history.
Scott Nikolay: That's really cool. And you've also mentioned before that you're involved in the Weird Fiction Review. Can you tell us more about your work there?
Craig Lawrence Giddney: Yes, Scott. I'm a co-founder and editor-in-chief of the Weird Fiction Review which is an online magazine dedicated to exploring the weird and wonderful in fiction.

title: Project Wildfire - Episode 15
introduction: Welcome to Project Wildfire, the podcast where we look at the science in old movies and see if it holds up. I'm your host Dr. Biology.

segments.title: Episode Overview
segments.description: Dr. Biology provides an overview of the episode focusing on the movie *The Andromeda Strain* and its analysis.

segments.title: Movie Analysis - The Andromeda Strain
segments.description: Dr. Biology delves into the scientific inaccuracies and inconsistencies present in *The Andromeda Strain*, including biological warfare, military protection suits, and more.

conclusion: For those interested in discussing this episode or any previous episodes, Dr. Biology encourages listeners to engage on social media through Project Wildfire's Facebook page and Twitter handle @DrBiology.
audio_files: Project Wildfire - Episode 15 - The Andromeda Strain.mp3
transcript:
00:02:48 - Dr. Biology: Welcome to Project Wildfire, the podcast where we look at the science in old movies and see if it holds up. I'm your host, Dr. Biology. October 2nd, 2020.

00:03:15 - Dr. Biology: In this episode, we will be looking at one of my favorite films from the '70s, The Andromeda Strain. It was written by Michael Wilson and Michael Weller. Directed by Robert Wise and released in 1971. If you're a fan of old movies like me, you've probably seen this movie many times. Maybe you first saw it on an early cable channel when you were younger or maybe you've just picked it up as one of those random movies that are available now through Netflix.

00:03:47 - Dr. Biology: In any case, you might be surprised to learn some of the scientific inaccuracies and inconsistencies in this film. For example, there was a germ warfare program in the U.S. military during the 1950s and '60s. But by the time this movie came out, that program had already started winding down.

00:04:03 - Dr. Biology: In fact, it's not until after that program was shut down that biological warfare research starts to ramp up again with a focus on incapacitation and non-lethal weapons instead of the lethality of the 1950s and '60s.

00:04:18 - Dr. Biology: Now, let's get started. Let me walk you through some of these inconsistencies that I have found as I watched this movie again for this episode. First, there are military protection suits shown in the film. These are clearly based on real protective gear used by troops at the time and later.

00:04:38 - Dr. Biology: But here's a question from one of my listeners that I want to share with you. If your 40 minutes are up, and you got to get back on the ship, are there more oxygen bottles there? Or is he just planning to fly you 50 miles with the doors open to blow all the stuff out of the helicopter?

00:04:53 - Dr. Biology: Well, according to my research, this movie was made in 1971, and Apollo 13 had happened a few years prior. So the technology for breathing apparatuses at that time would be pretty well developed.

00:05:06 - Dr. Biology: Another inconsistency is how they seem to have all of their equipment in one place on this ship, whereas realistically, you'd expect military equipment and supplies to be scattered throughout a variety of locations. This would allow for more flexibility and ensure that there's always something available when needed.

00:05:23 - Dr. Biology: Another problem is with the biology. For example, it seems unlikely they can take one of these samples from outer space or even from another continent away, and in 40 minutes, you've got a biological agent that's going to start growing exponentially and cause all kinds of problems. That doesn't really make sense.

00:05:39 - Dr. Biology: Also, the movie portrays a situation where there is no clear leadership or organizational structure among the characters involved in handling this crisis. There are several scientists with different expertise levels but they don't seem to be coordinating their efforts effectively. This lack of coordination and unclear command structure could lead to chaos and ineffective response.

00:06:02 - Dr. Biology: Another inconsistency is how the military protection suits seem to function in a way that's inconsistent with real-world protective gear used by troops. For instance, it would be more practical to have a mechanism for changing out parts of the suit when necessary rather than just wearing one piece until its service life expires.

00:06:23 - Dr. Biology: Finally, I found an interesting tidbit that the U.S. military did indeed conduct germ warfare research during this period, but it was moving away from lethal agents towards non-lethal incapacitants. This makes some sense in the context of the film's plot where a highly contagious and deadly pathogen is being studied.

00:06:42 - Dr. Biology: I hope you enjoyed this episode of Project Wildfire, and if you have any questions or comments about The Andromeda Strain or anything we've talked about here today, please visit us on our Facebook page at Project Wildfire or on Twitter @DrBiology.

00:06:57 - Dr. Biology: So stay safe out there, and we'll see you next time.

title: Andromeda Minute - The Andromeda Strain (1971) - Minute #24
description: In this episode, Jim and Chris discuss The Andromeda Strain (1971), focusing on a particularly impactful scene that closes out Minute #24. They explore the film's storytelling techniques, its connection to Michael Crichton's novel, and how it sets the stage for future horror elements in the movie.
transcript: Jim Vickers: Welcome back everyone. I'm Jim Vickers here with Chris Escalante on this edition of The Andromeda Minute. Today we're going to be talking about The Andromeda Strain, 1971's science fiction classic based on Michael Crichton's novel. We'll be focusing on a particular scene that closes out our Minute #24.
Chris Escalante: That's right Jim and as always I'm super excited to have you here. So tell us about this minute and what we're going to be looking at today.

Jim Vickers: Well, it's one of the few minutes where we really see how close to the book Crichton was in adapting his story into a film. The Andromeda Strain is a very book-like movie, especially as you mentioned Chris, with Michael Crichton's writing being lifted almost word for word.

Chris Escalante: That's right Jim and it's so different from the more sedate Day of the Triffids or Village of the Damned. Andromeda Strain has a much darker tone which really sets the stage for what's to come in this scene we're about to discuss.

Jim Vickers: Yeah, and as you mentioned earlier, Chris, it's a very unsettling angle that closes out this minute. We see the victim lying upside down with his head on one side. And then we get this close-up of him being approached by the vulture, which is pretty graphic considering it's an R-rated movie.

Chris Escalante: Yeah, and there's a lot of trauma and distress here. The world is literally upside-down because of what has happened to this poor soul. And I think that little bit of allegory there really adds to the horror and sense of dread in the scene.

Jim Vickers: Absolutely, and it's so shocking given how understated much of the film is up until this point. The vulture sitting right next to him on the side is also a powerful image that drives home just how horrific the situation is.

Chris Escalante: And let me tell you Jim, the use of the fisheye lens really distorts the scene in a way that's both visually striking and terrifying. It almost makes it feel like his head is sticking out into your lap, which is quite unnerving.

Jim Vickers: Absolutely, and from this point on, it's going to be a roller coaster ride with more horrific things to come. But for now, we need to focus on this impactful scene that really sets the tone for the rest of the movie.

Chris Escalante: For sure Jim, there's no doubt about it. And as always, if you have any questions or comments, head over to our social media accounts and join the conversation. You can find us at @AndromedaMinute on Twitter or Project Wildfire on Facebook. And for those of you who want to learn more about our work, check out our website and my Amazon author page.
Jim Vickers: That's right Chris. And as always, thank you for joining us today. We'll see you next time on The Andromeda Minute.

title: Lesson Recap: Jesus' Death and Burial

keyPoints.content: Jesus was arrested, tried by the Sanhedrin, and then handed over to Pilate for sentencing.
Pilate found no guilt in Jesus but caved to pressure from the crowd and sentenced him to crucifixion.
Jesus was whipped, had a crown of thorns placed on his head, and carried a cross before being crucified on Golgotha hill.
Jesus died by crucifixion, cried out to God, and declared 'it is finished' as the price for sin was paid.
The lesson ended with John 3:16, stating that Jesus died for everyone's sins and belief in Him provides everlasting life.

description: In this episode, Wayne Shepard and Michael Card continue their discussion on the life of Jesus, focusing on the Book of John. They discuss Peter's role in the book, the concept of living stones, and other teachings found within. The conversation includes stories from Corrado Primavera, a friend and pastor to Michael in Rome, about his experience with the apostle Peter and how it relates to understanding the scriptures.
transcript: Welcome back to Sea of Souls, today we're continuing our discussion on the life of Jesus focusing on the Book of John. We have Wayne Shepard here as always and joining us from the studio is Michael Card. Hi Michael
Hi
Thank you for being with us today and we are joined by Corrado Primavera who's a friend and pastor to Michael in Rome, welcome to the show Carado.
Thank you very much for having me here.
We have been looking forward to this conversation we're going to have now. It's great to hear your stories about Peter and how that relates to understanding the scriptures better.

Absolutely, it was a really wonderful experience walking with Peter through his home in Rome. I remember walking through that neighborhood and I wish I'd known then what you've just told us, that Peter had been thinking about his eventual death all those years ago and still serving God faithfully up until the day he died, it's quite inspiring.

Yes, it makes me want to go back into the scriptures again. It is so rich with these stories and teachings from Jesus, like how we are Peter in living stones as you mentioned before. I was thinking back to what you said with our guest Corrado about how Peter had been thinking about his eventual death all those years ago and still serving God faithfully up until the day he died, it's quite inspiring.

- It's emphasized that while God promises deliverance in eternity, He also provides His presence and steadfast love in this life through prayer and Scripture. 

- Practical applications are given for believers to pray like David, pouring out their feelings, making known their needs, and ending with a reminder of God's hesed.

- The speaker challenges the congregation to seek God's hesed during times of difficulty, such as anxiety, depression, or other life struggles. 

- Jim Elliot's quote 'The saint who advances on his knees never retreats' is referenced, encouraging believers to approach their prayers with honesty and vulnerability.}

summary:
In minute 108 of 'North by Northwest,' the conversation between Eve Kendall (Eve Marie Saint) and Roger Thornhill (Cary Grant) is filled with vulnerability as they navigate their relationship in the aftermath of misunderstandings. The scene begins with both characters walking towards each other, and the interplay of emotions is palpable. Roger's attempt at humor and awkwardness provides a contrast to his sincerity, while Eve's response conveys her desire for reconciliation despite the tension. The scene is rich with subtext, as each character tries to gauge the other’s feelings, leading to moments of both discomfort and connection.

The conversation touches on themes of trust, misunderstanding, and the willingness to confront past conflicts. Roger's words like 'I know,' which are filled with a mix of sincerity and embarrassment, highlight his internal struggle between what he wants to say and how it might be perceived. Eve’s response is equally layered, as she tries to reassure Roger that they can move forward despite their disagreements.

The scene serves as a turning point in the relationship between Thornhill and Kendall, setting the stage for further developments in their journey. The subtle yet powerful interactions between these two characters add depth to the narrative and engage the audience emotionally.
key_quotes: "I know." - Roger Thornhill (Cary Grant), expressing his understanding of the situation with a mix of sincerity and embarrassment.

"Well, I thought I was going to see you too, but that professor wouldn't let me. Well, it wasn't safe." - Eve Kendall (Eve Marie Saint), using humor to lighten the mood while also addressing the misunderstanding.
"Are we down?" - Roger Thornhill, asking if they can move forward despite their past conflicts.
impact_on_storyline: This scene marks a significant shift in the relationship between Roger and Eve, laying the groundwork for their future collaboration. It highlights the complexity of their dynamic and the challenges they face as they work together to overcome their differences.

Summary: The conversation revolves around Simon's journey from his early days as a farrier in Australia to his experiences working abroad, focusing on his time at Lizzie Park Stud in New Zealand. Key points include: the importance of being adaptable and open-minded when presented with opportunities; the challenges faced during travel by mail in the 1980s; the significance of mentorship and education; the impact of cross-cultural interactions on personal growth; and Simon's current lifestyle in a small farming community. Throughout his narrative, Simon emphasizes the value of humility and continuous learning.

Interview Highlights.Question: How did you end up moving from Australia to New Zealand?
Interview Highlights.Answer: I went there because of an opportunity that presented itself through Lizzie Park Stud, which was recommended by a mentor in the farrier community.

Interview Highlights.Question: What were some significant challenges during your early days as a farrier overseas?
Interview Highlights.Answer: The biggest challenge was just getting there, dealing with travel by mail and not being able to see people face-to-face. I also had to learn how to manage the horses differently from what I was used to in Australia.

Interview Highlights.Question: How did you establish yourself as a farrier in New Zealand?
Interview Highlights.Answer: I focused on educating myself, staying adaptable, and learning from experienced mentors like Scotty Simpson. I also worked hard at getting the work done effectively despite limited resources.

Interview Highlights.Question: What have been some of the key lessons you've learned from your experiences?
Interview Highlights.Answer: The most important lesson is to remain humble and recognize that there's always more to learn, especially when working in different cultural contexts. It's also crucial to be open-minded and willing to adapt to new situations.

Interview Highlights.Question: How do you see the future of your work?
Interview Highlights.Answer: I enjoy the lifestyle I have now, staying active, and still being involved with farriery through my role at the university. I focus on maintaining a balance between work and personal life.

title: Introduction and Personal Experiences of Being an Expat in Europe

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: Hey everyone, welcome to the first episode of You Expat. My name is Tiago, and I'm here with my friend João today.

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: Hi there, I’m João. Nice to meet you all!

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: We’re going to be talking about our experiences as expats living in Europe and sharing some of the stories behind it.

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: Yeah, so let's get started. We'll give you a bit of background on ourselves first.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: Sure, let me start with my story. I moved to Brussels, Belgium from Portugal 6 years ago for work and haven't looked back since. What about you, João?

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: I've lived in different countries within the European Union over the past decade — starting in Spain, then Germany, now I'm in Luxembourg. Each place has had its unique challenges and rewards.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: That's quite a journey you’ve been on! How do you see your experiences with different countries shaping who you are today?

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: Absolutely, every new place taught me something different. Whether it’s learning to adapt quickly in Spain or managing work-life balance in Germany, these experiences have definitely made me more versatile and open-minded.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: That's great! So today, we wanted to discuss what being an expat means to us. How do you define the term 'expat', João?

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: Well, it’s a broad term. For me, an expat is someone who moves away from their home country for personal or professional reasons and adapts to a new culture.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: I agree. And I think it's interesting how the concept of being an expat differs between countries. For example, in the U.S., moving to another city within the same state might not be considered as significant compared to moving abroad.

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: Exactly! In Europe, however, we can move freely across borders without many restrictions and that’s quite a unique experience. It's like living in different worlds with slightly different rules but still within the same union.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: Absolutely. I think this freedom to move around has been a huge advantage for our generation, especially those of us who grew up during the expansion of the European Union. It’s shaped how we view countries and borders differently from previous generations.

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: True, it's like we're all part of this big experiment where we get to live in multiple cultures. And I think this has made us more understanding of different perspectives and ways of living.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: Definitely. So today, we want our listeners to know that being an expat is much more than just a job or a relocation. It's about embracing new cultures, meeting interesting people, and finding your place in the world.

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: Yeah, we hope this podcast will become a platform for us to share our stories and experiences with others who are either considering becoming expats or already living it. We’ll cover everything from fashion trends in different cities to local events and even dive into some of the challenges.

transcript.speaker: Tiago
transcript.text: And we welcome anyone out there who has an interesting story or perspective on being an expat. Don’t hesitate to reach out, we’d love to hear from you.

transcript.speaker: João
transcript.text: That's all for today, folks! If you enjoyed this episode, please leave us a rating wherever you listen to podcasts and join us next time on You Expat. Until then, stay curious and keep exploring!

title: Cody's Journey: Navigating LGBTQ+ Identity in the LDS Church
guestDescription: A member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS) who identifies as LGBTQ+, sharing his journey with faith and identity.
keyTakeaways: It's important to validate the struggles and doubts that come along with navigating LGBTQ+ identity in the LDS church, acknowledging that it is okay to doubt or feel conflicted.

Cody advises those going through a faith crisis not to be too hasty, but instead give themselves time to work through their experiences and lean into the process of finding light at the end of the tunnel.
Cody emphasizes that God loves all individuals, regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity. He encourages listeners who are struggling to hold on and trust in a better future.
transcript: Host: Today we have Cody with us, a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS) who identifies as LGBTQ+, sharing his journey with faith and identity.
Guest: Thank you for having me on the show. I'm really excited to be here today.
Host: To start, can you tell us your name and a bit about yourself?
Guest: Sure. My name is Cody and I've been an active member of the LDS church since I was 12 years old. I grew up in Utah and have always felt a strong connection to the gospel.
Host: Can you share with us how your identity as LGBTQ+ has impacted your relationship with the church?

Guest: It's definitely been a challenge at times, but I'm still committed to staying active in the church. The experience of coming out and figuring out my identity has made me more honest, authentic, and transparent about who I am. But there have also been moments where I've questioned certain doctrines or felt like an outsider.
Host: Can you tell us a bit about your journey with the church?

Guest: It's definitely been a faith crisis for me right now. There are some fundamental points of doctrine that I'm having doubts about and it can be really hard to reconcile those with my identity as LGBTQ+. But even though there are these doubts, I still feel like something pulls towards the gospel of Jesus Christ, even if it feels like a bonfire in the distance on a dark night.
Host: How do you navigate those challenges?

Guest: It's important for me to be honest and forthcoming about my struggles. For example, I've been open with my Bishop, who has been incredibly supportive and understanding. And it can also help to have a close-knit group of friends or other members in the church who understand what you're going through.
Host: What advice do you have for people who may be struggling with their faith as an LGBTQ+ member?

Guest: Validation is really important. It's okay to doubt and it's okay to feel conflicted about your faith. I encourage people not to be too hasty in making big decisions or thinking that they're out if they're having a faith crisis. Give yourself time, lean into the process, and know that there's light at the end of the tunnel.
Host: If you could press a button to be straight, would you?

Guest: In a heartbeat, in a heartbeat. But I also want people to understand that this is part of who I am and God loves me regardless of my sexual orientation or gender identity. And it's important for me to encourage listeners who are struggling to hold on and know that they're going to be okay.
Host: Thank you, Cody, for sharing your story with us today. It means a lot to our listeners to hear about someone navigating these challenges so authentically and openly.

title: Throw Away the Veil
transcript:
This sermon emphasizes the importance of embracing the presence of God fully, rather than putting up small barriers or veils. The speaker uses several key points to make this argument:

1. **God's Presence is Omnipresent**: God is everywhere at all times, and His presence is overwhelming but necessary.
2. **Face Masks as a Metaphor for Veil Control**: Just as we wear face masks out of habit or necessity (even when they're not relevant), we might try to put up small veils in our lives to control how much God's presence impacts us.
3. **Jesus' Guarantee of Access to God**: Jesus has torn the veil, allowing us direct access to God's presence. This means we should not try to limit His influence or presence through small barriers.
4. **Resilient Discipleship**: The speaker outlines what resilient discipleship looks like - recognizing prayer as essential, yearning for God's presence, and leaving everything behind when following Jesus fully.
5. **God's Call to Unusual and Astonishing Things**: God might call us to roles or paths we never imagined, such as business leadership or family duties, emphasizing that His plans are not limited by our perceived limitations.
6. **Cost of Following Christ Fully**: The speaker mentions the cost of following Jesus fully is giving up complete control, which is hard but ultimately rewarding.
7. **Purpose and Mission from God**: True purpose and mission come from knowing and experiencing God's presence deeply.
8. **Encouragement for Action**: The sermon concludes with a call to action - throw away any small veils we might have put in place and fully embrace the presence of God.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: Hello, everyone. Today, we have an incredibly powerful guest joining us. Cassidy Jensen is a survivor of rape and she’s going to share her story with us. Cassidy, thank you so much for being here.

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: Thank you for having me. I’m honored to be here.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: You're very welcome. So, Cassidy, could you start by telling us a little bit about what happened and how that experience impacted your life?

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: Certainly. I was raped two years ago, which is a difficult thing to talk about. It’s been incredibly challenging to process and come to terms with it over the past couple of years. The impact has been profound on every aspect of my life—my mental health, relationships, career, and faith.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: That's really tough. How did you initially cope with those feelings?

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: Initially, I found it incredibly challenging to cope. There was a lot of anger and confusion. But over time, I began seeking support through therapy and connecting with other survivors. Support groups and counseling have been instrumental in helping me navigate these emotions.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: It's great that you found those resources. How did your faith play a role in your healing process?

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: Faith was a cornerstone for me. It provided me with comfort, strength, and a sense of purpose during my darkest moments. It helped me find solace and gave me the courage to keep moving forward despite the pain.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: That's wonderful. Speaking of moving forward, you wrote an incredibly powerful victim impact statement. Could you tell us more about that?

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: Yes, I did write a victim impact statement as part of the legal proceedings against my rapist. It was a cathartic process to put everything on paper and share it with others who had experienced similar trauma. Reading it out loud during the trial brought me a sense of closure and justice.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: That's powerful. What advice would you give to other survivors facing similar situations?

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: First, I would encourage them not to be ashamed of their experience. It's a brave step to come forward and share what happened. Secondly, seek support from loved ones or professionals. Lastly, remember that healing is a journey. You are in control of your own healing process.

transcript.speaker: Richard Oster
transcript.content: Thank you so much for sharing those insights with us today. It's been an honor to have you here.

transcript.speaker: Cassidy Jensen
transcript.content: Thank you, Richard. I appreciate the opportunity to share my story and raise awareness about this issue.

summary: In this episode, Tara Spann, Director of Product Development at MGMA, discusses integrated care teams with host Daniel Williams. They explore how practices can improve patient satisfaction, reduce burnout, and optimize workflow through better team collaboration. Key topics include implementing level loading to offload tasks from providers, streamlining the patient experience by bringing care to the patient rather than sending them through multiple channels, measuring success using KPIs such as total time spent in office, face-to-face provider time, documentation time, and job satisfaction, and engaging a team that is willing to change. Tara highlights the importance of ongoing support for sustaining these changes. The conversation concludes with practical advice on how practices can adopt this model.
key_points: Integrated care teams improve patient satisfaction and reduce burnout by optimizing workflow and task distribution.
Level loading helps offload tasks from providers, allowing them to focus on value-added activities like face-to-face time with patients.
Bringing care to the patient through streamlined processes can significantly reduce wait times and enhance the overall experience.
KPIs such as total office time, face-to-face provider time, documentation time, and job satisfaction should be monitored for success.
Engaging a team willing to change is critical for implementing integrated care models effectively.
Ongoing support from leadership is essential to sustain these changes in the long term.
quotes: "It is self-perpetuating almost." - Tara Spann, on how word of mouth spreads engagement within practices.

"We're not just making a difference in their lives at work. We're making a difference in their lives at home and that balance is truly what is necessary in order to prevent burnout out and lessen the demand." - Tara Spann
takeaways: Identify providers and staff who are willing to change and engage them in implementing integrated care teams.
Measure success using key performance indicators (KPIs) such as total office time, face-to-face provider time, documentation time, and job satisfaction.
Streamline patient flow by having providers and support staff work more closely together, reducing the need for patients to navigate multiple points of contact.
Provide ongoing support from leadership to maintain these changes and ensure they continue to benefit both providers and patients.

summary: Daniel Williams interviews Tony Stadahar, Kathy Cooperman, and Dr. Russ Livingston about the psychological impact of COVID-19 on healthcare providers, recruitment strategies, and coping mechanisms for stress. They discuss the challenges posed by the pandemic to mental health and offer advice for both current healthcare professionals and organizations seeking to hire new physicians.
transcript: Daniel Williams: We’re joined today by three guests. Tony Stadahar is CEO of the consulting firm Medstar Consulting, Kathy Cooperman is president at KRC Associates Inc., and Dr. Russ Livingston is a psychologist with over 30 years experience in medical practice.

Daniel Williams: Thanks for joining us today to discuss the psychological impact of the pandemic on healthcare providers and how it’s affecting recruitment efforts as well as retention strategies for current employees. So, let's start by addressing some of these conditions that are present right now and the impact psychologically that it has on people.

<Tony Stadahar>: The biggest challenge is burnout. Providers were already stretched thin before the pandemic hit, but then there was a massive surge in demand as more patients needed care. They have to work longer hours, see more patients, and deal with increased stress from personal concerns about their own health and family members.

<Kathy Cooperman>: There’s also an added layer of grief and loss for many healthcare workers who are seeing colleagues and patients pass away every day. It can be very difficult to cope with that kind of emotional strain on top of the physical demands of working in a pandemic environment.

Daniel Williams: That's really important, especially as we hear about shortages in critical supplies like PPE and ventilators. What are some strategies for dealing with this stress? I’ll start with you, Kathy?

<Kathy Cooperman>: Sure, one key strategy is to prioritize self-care and take breaks when possible. Providers need to make sure they’re getting enough rest and nutrition, engaging in physical activity, and spending time with loved ones if that’s feasible given their work schedules.

Daniel Williams: That's a good point about taking care of yourself physically as well as emotionally. Russ, what do you think are some ways healthcare organizations can help support their employees' mental health during this time?

<Dr. Russ Livingston>: Organizations need to create a culture that values mental health and provides resources like counseling services or employee assistance programs. They should also offer flexible scheduling options so providers can manage their workload more effectively and give them opportunities to connect with colleagues in a non-work context.

Daniel Williams: Those are great suggestions for both individual and organizational support. Tony, you've worked with many healthcare organizations on recruitment efforts. How has the pandemic changed those strategies?

<Tony Stadahar>: We’re seeing a greater emphasis on virtual interviews and remote orientation programs to reduce travel costs and minimize exposure risks for candidates. It’s also important to be transparent about the challenges of practicing medicine in this environment and highlight ways that organizations are supporting their employees' well-being.
Daniel Williams: That makes sense given how much has changed over the past year. Kathy, what would you recommend for healthcare providers who are considering a job change during this time?

<Kathy Cooperman>: Providers should look for organizations that prioritize work-life balance and have clear policies around burnout prevention. They can also talk to current employees at potential new workplaces to get an insider’s perspective on how the organization supports its staff.

Daniel Williams: Good advice, especially since many providers may be feeling overwhelmed and looking for a change of pace. Russ, any final thoughts about the psychological impact of the pandemic on healthcare workers?

<Dr. Russ Livingston>: It's crucial that we continue to provide mental health resources and support systems for healthcare professionals who are risking their lives every day. We need to acknowledge the trauma they're experiencing and offer them tools and strategies to cope with it in a healthy way.

Daniel Williams: Beautifully said, Russ. Tony, Kathy, Ross, this has been a great discussion. Really plumb the depths of what's going on right now and offered some great solutions. So thanks so much for joining us today and sharing these thoughts.

今晚的娱乐节目我们来聊聊流行文化、明星八卦和新闻等。首先，让我们来看一下近期的娱乐新闻。

美国说唱歌手Sushant Singh Rajput在34岁时去世，死因疑似自杀。Rajput出演过Netflix的动作片《驱魔人》，还参演了宝莱坞电影《拉克什米·洛塔》和《吉普赛女孩》等作品。他的突然离世让许多人感到震惊。

此外，还有多位名人去世或确诊感染新冠病毒。70岁的演员Jack Turnball因新冠肺炎去世；70岁的动画师Pratt Brimer也因病去世。81岁的传奇漫画书编辑Denny O’Neill、67岁的著名公关人Nancy Ryder、以及34岁的宝莱坞男星Sushant Singh Rajput等多位名人也都离开了我们。

现在让我们来说说一些明星八卦新闻。好莱坞知名演员Mel Winkler在67岁时因肌萎缩性侧索硬化症（ALS）去世，他最著名的角色是在电影《魔鬼穿蓝色晚礼服》中饰演的撒旦一角；而他的弟弟John Greece则出演了2004年的经典喜剧电影《 Napoleon Dynamite》，今年已经63岁了。同时还有其他一些知名演员也到了花甲之年：60岁的Thomas Hayden Church、57岁的Greg Keneer、54岁的Will Forte等。

接下来是今天要介绍的明星生日名单，首先是1944年的资深演员Mark Lynn Baker，在《完美陌生人》中饰演了一位关键人物；63岁的John Greece是《Napoleon Dynamite》的主演；还有62岁的Bobby Farrelly导演和38岁的Arthur Darville。

接下来让我们来聊一聊娱乐节目的新闻。今天晚上录制节目前，由于有人被检测出新冠病毒阳性，制作组取消了节目录制并让大家进行检测。此前在WWE“暴怒”比赛上，Edge与Randy Orton的对决也因为Edge受伤而告一段落，现在还不清楚这是否会影响Christian在擂台上的未来。

接下来是今天的结束语：今晚的娱乐节目是由我们优秀的团队共同制作完成的，再次感谢Chachi McFly，他是80年代的代表人物。当然还有其他一些成员也是不可或缺的力量。最后祝大家晚上好，晚安。

trans: 本期节目我们依然继续《曼达洛人》第一季的讨论，今天我们来到了第四集。我必须得承认，在观看这个节目前，我对于它到底能不能成为一部好剧其实还是有些疑虑的，毕竟现在类似的科幻题材美剧实在是太多了。不过看完之后，我对自己的怀疑感到惭愧了。这部剧无论是从剧情、人物设定，还是特效制作方面都做得相当不错。而且我个人很喜欢它的叙事风格，每集的故事都非常紧凑，同时又带有一些西部片的色彩，这对我来说是很难得的一点。“曼达洛人”是《星球大战》系列中的一个角色，这个角色最早出现于原力觉醒当中，然后在后续的剧集中也有所提及。这部剧中讲述的是曼达洛人的故事，所以虽然从某种意义上来说，它属于‘外传’性质的作品，但其实对于了解整个星战宇宙的历史和文化，还是很有帮助的。此外，本集我们还聊到了《星球大战》系列中的一些武器装备等设定问题，以及在《曼达洛人》第二季里可能会出现的新角色等等。

title: Star Warsport | Mandalorian Roundup
summary: Riley and Scott discuss the latest rumors about the Disney+ series 'The Mandalorian' including casting news for Boba Fett and Ahsoka Tano, as well as other potential characters and plot developments.
transcript: Riley: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to another episode of Star Warsport, the only podcast where we talk about the latest in Star Wars news and rumors. I'm your host, Riley, and with me is my co-host, Scott Reif.
Scott: Good morning, Riley. And good morning to our listeners who are tuning in for this Mandalorian Roundup episode.

Riley: Yes, today we're diving into the latest rumors about The Mandalorian. Specifically, there's been some casting news that caught my attention. For those of you who have been following the series, you know that Boba Fett has been a fan favorite since he first appeared in Season 2. And now, there's talk that Timothy Olyphant, best known for his role as Sheriff Ed McCone in Deadwood and The Longmire, might be playing Jango Fett in the second season of The Mandalorian.

Scott: That is indeed a big deal, Riley. Timothy Olyphant has been quite active recently, appearing in Aquaman and Moana's dad in Moana, as well as voicing various characters for Disney projects. It makes sense that he would be considered for such a legendary role.

Riley: Absolutely. And while we don't have any official confirmation yet, it does seem like his casting could help bring some credibility to the character. Additionally, there's been some speculation about Katie Sackhoff potentially playing Ahsoka Tano in the series. She starred in The Title Star and has a new Netflix series she’s currently in, which could explain why they might be interested in her for this role.

Scott: That does make sense considering her recent projects. And it would certainly bring some excitement to fans who have longed to see Ahsoka return. However, we should also consider that there are no guarantees when it comes to casting decisions.

Riley: True, and I think the reason why people get upset about these rumors is because they can be inconsistent sometimes. Ashley Eckstein has a strong connection with the Star Wars community, but it's still a creative decision. We just don't know if her inclusion will be well-received or not.

Scott: Yes, exactly. And I think it’s important to keep an open mind and avoid jumping to conclusions until we have more information. That being said, let's move on to some other potential plot developments for the series. There are rumors that Rosario Dawson might appear as Ahsoka Tano, which could be a bold choice considering her role in The Mandalorian Season 2.

Riley: Oh, this is interesting. If true, it would certainly shake things up. It's also worth noting that while all these casting and plot developments are exciting, we should keep in mind that many of them might not come to fruition.
Scott: Agreed. But even if they don't materialize, the speculation can still provide a lot of entertainment for fans like us.

Riley: Exactly. And I guess that's it for today's Mandalorian Roundup. We've covered some of the latest rumors and speculations surrounding The Mandalorian. If you have any thoughts or other news you'd like to share, feel free to hit us up on social media. You can find me at @therileyguy and Scott at @ScottReif.
Scott: And make sure to tune in for our next episode where we'll be discussing more Star Wars news and rumors. Until then, may the Force be with you.

title: The Poker Presence Podcast - Episode 169 | Daniel Saper on Poker Presence & Writing a Book
transcript: [Intro Music]

Host: Welcome back, listeners! Today we have Daniel Saper joining us to discuss his new book, 'Poker Presence,' as well as the writing process and insights gained from self-publishing. So without further ado, let's get started!
Interviewer: Hello, everyone. I'm [Interviewer's Name], and today we're thrilled to have Daniel Saper with us on The Poker Presence Podcast. Welcome, Daniel.
Daniel: Thank you for having me. I'm excited to be here.
Interviewer: So, Daniel, can you start by telling our listeners a bit about your background in poker and what led you to write 'Poker Presence'?

Daniel: Sure! I've been playing poker professionally since 2013. My journey started with online play but eventually moved into live tournaments. Over the years, I found myself struggling with consistency and dealing with stress during big events. That's when I realized that my emotional management wasn't up to par. So, I began focusing on developing presence—a term I use in my book—and it became a game-changer for me. I decided to write this book because I wanted to share these concepts with others who might be experiencing similar challenges.
Interviewer: That's great! Can you explain what 'Poker Presence' means and why it’s important in poker?

Daniel: Sure, 'Poker Presence' refers to the ability to stay focused, calm, and objective during a hand or tournament. It involves being fully present and engaged without getting swayed by emotions like fear, anger, or frustration. Being present helps you make better decisions, read your opponents accurately, and maintain confidence. In poker, where decisions are made under pressure, presence is crucial for long-term success.
Interviewer: That makes sense. Now, let's dive into the writing process. How did you approach self-publishing 'Poker Presence'?

Daniel: Well, I initially thought about traditional publishing but ultimately decided to go with self-publishing because it allowed me more control over the content and timing. I had a clear vision for the book from start to finish, which made the process smoother. However, it did require a lot of time and effort to handle tasks like editing, formatting, and marketing.
Interviewer: What were some challenges you faced during the writing and publishing process?

Daniel: There were definitely some hurdles. Managing my time effectively was one challenge since I had a full-time poker career. Additionally, learning how to self-publish was steep—there's a lot of technical stuff involved that isn't immediately intuitive. But overall, it gave me a sense of satisfaction and control over the final product.
Interviewer: That sounds like quite an undertaking! What advice would you give to other poker players who might be considering writing their own book?

Daniel: My biggest piece of advice is to have a clear vision for your project. Know what you want to say and why it's important. Also, don't underestimate the time commitment—it will take much more than you initially expect. And finally, embrace the process; even if parts of the book aren't perfect, they can still be valuable.
Interviewer: That's great advice. Now that 'Poker Presence' is out, what do you hope readers gain from it?

Daniel: My main goal is to help poker players become more present and confident in their gameplay. I want them to understand the importance of emotional control and learn practical strategies for achieving presence. Ultimately, I hope this book will improve their overall performance at the tables.
Interviewer: That's fantastic! Thanks again for joining us today, Daniel. It was great talking about your journey and 'Poker Presence'. Best of luck with future projects!
Daniel: Thank you so much, [Interviewer's Name]. I appreciate it, and I'm looking forward to seeing how the book impacts the poker community.
outro music

Charles: Let’s jump right into today’s topic. Today we are going to talk about online teaching and how you have managed your transition from in-person teaching to online. Tony, as a teacher who has been working for many years now, can you tell us a little bit more about the challenges that you faced while making this transition? 
Tony: Sure! I think there were a few major challenges. One of them was trying to replicate the classroom experience virtually. You know, there's something about being in person with your students and having that personal connection. Another challenge was managing the technical aspects of teaching online. Setting up Zoom meetings, using breakout rooms, and so on. There’s also the issue of keeping students engaged for an extended period. But I think what has been most challenging is trying to keep a balance between making sure my students are learning effectively while also taking care of my own well-being. Charles: Exactly! And it's not just about the technicalities; it's also about adapting your teaching style and methods. For example, using breakout rooms can be really effective for group work, but how do you manage these groups online? Do you have any specific strategies or tips to share on this topic?
Tony: Yes, I use a lot of breakout rooms in my classes. One strategy that has worked well is assigning roles within the breakout room. For example, one student can be the facilitator who keeps everyone on track and ensures that all group members are participating. Another role could be note-taker or speaker, who will summarize the discussion when we reconvene as a whole class. This way, students get a chance to take ownership of their learning.
Charles: That's a great idea! I also use breakout rooms frequently and find them very useful. However, I often struggle with managing time during these sessions. How do you manage your time effectively while using breakout rooms?
Tony: Well, one tip is to set clear objectives for each session. For example, if we're doing a group activity in the breakout room, make sure everyone understands what they need to achieve before breaking out. This helps ensure that all students are on track and can stay focused during their time in the breakout rooms.
Charles: I agree! Another challenge is finding the right tools and resources for online teaching. Are there any specific tools or apps that you have found particularly useful in your online classes?
Tony: Yes, definitely. One tool that has been really helpful is Zoom's ShareScreen function. It allows me to share my screen with students while still being able to use my whiteboard marker. I can also highlight important points and write notes directly on the shared screen. This makes it easier for students to follow along during class.
Charles: That sounds like a great tool! Do you find that using technology helps you engage your students more effectively?
Tony: Absolutely! Using tools like Zoom's ShareScreen or an iPad with a whiteboard app can make the online classroom experience feel more dynamic and interactive. It allows me to show examples, work through problems step-by-step, and give immediate feedback on student questions.
Charles: I couldn't agree more. Another thing that has helped me is using different modalities for teaching. For instance, if you are explaining a concept, it's helpful to provide both verbal explanations as well as visual aids like diagrams or screenshots.
Tony: Yes, that’s true. By combining oral and visual input, we can cater to different learning preferences among our students. It also makes the content more accessible for those who may have difficulty with one form of communication over another.
Charles: Exactly! And you mentioned something about taking a break from technology at some point. Do you mean giving your students or yourself time without technology during class?
Tony: Yes, that’s right. Taking regular breaks can be beneficial both for the teacher and the students. It gives everyone a chance to rest their minds and come back refreshed.
Charles: That's a great point! I also find that using different tools like GoodNotes helps me maintain my energy levels during classes. Have you noticed any specific benefits from using such tools?
Tony: Yes, using GoodNotes has definitely helped me keep my notes organized and make them more interactive. It’s easier to highlight key points and add comments, which makes the content more engaging for students.
Charles: That's a great tool! And it seems like the best time to start exploring new tech tools is now that you've got some experience under your belt. Do you think there are any other tools or strategies we should explore?
Tony: Absolutely, I suggest trying out different tools and strategies as long as they make teaching more effective for both you and your students. ShareScreen and GoodNotes are just two examples of the many useful tools available.
Charles: That's a great advice! It sounds like we've covered quite a bit today, but is there anything else that you would like to add before we wrap up?
Tony: Just one final thought – don't be afraid to experiment with new technologies and strategies. The transition to online teaching has been challenging, but it also presents an opportunity for growth and innovation in education.
Charles: Agreed! And thank you so much, Tony, for sharing your insights and tips with us today. This conversation was really helpful and informative.
Tony: Thanks Charles, I appreciate that. It's always nice to have a chat about teaching, even if it’s over the computer!

He discusses the importance of anonymous data sharing and leveraging different organizational capabilities for enhanced security.

global_summary: The episode discusses the concept of confidential computing and its importance for data security in various industries. Experts from Fortanix, Cosmina Madonna, and Pass discuss how this technology addresses challenges such as protecting data during use (in contrast to at rest or transit), implementing defense-in-depth strategies, and ensuring compliance with regulations like GDPR.
host_summary: Richard Kern introduces the topic by explaining the evolution of data security concerns in a world where devices generate vast amounts of data. He highlights how confidential computing has emerged as a solution to protect sensitive information while it's being processed or analyzed, particularly in cloud environments. The host also mentions the global nature of this problem and its relevance across different industries.
guest_summary: Pat from Fortanix explains the company’s background and how they identified opportunities related to data security. Christian from Cosmina Madonna discusses their approach to solving data protection challenges in various domains, including healthcare and retail. The guests emphasize the need for secure execution environments (like Intel SGX) and attestation mechanisms to ensure trust and compliance.

global_summary: The podcast discusses privacy and security concerns related to COVID-19 information, particularly addressing misconceptions about HIPAA's application in non-healthcare sectors. It highlights the need for businesses to protect collected data securely, considering state-specific laws and federal regulations like the FTC jurisdiction. The episode also covers issues around testing results, especially regarding the types of tests (PCR vs antibody), their implications, and required authorizations for employers. Additionally, it explores privacy and security challenges as businesses reopen, including contact tracing, remote work policies, media interactions, and social media use.

They discuss the importance of collecting only necessary information securely, understanding different types of COVID tests, and obtaining proper authorizations from labs.
guest_summary: Iliana Peters clarifies that HIPAA applies primarily to healthcare entities and their business associates. She explains how individuals can share their health information freely, while businesses must comply with state and federal laws depending on the type of data collected. The conversation also covers best practices for handling testing results, particularly around ensuring privacy through proper authorizations, and addresses broader concerns like contact tracing, remote work policies, media interactions, and social media use.

global_summary: The episode discusses the challenges and strategies for securing a permanent remote workforce. host_summary: Host Tom Field introduces the topic of securing a permanent remote workforce, emphasizing the initial risk acceptance to enable work continuity and the need to improve cyber hygiene through training and technology. He concludes by thanking his guest.

He details CyberMDX's involvement in assisting JSOF by identifying affected vendors and deploying solutions to mitigate the impact. The discussion touches on levels of expertise among various roles within football, including coaches, players, media, and fans. Additionally, it highlights the importance of respecting player biology in training to prevent injuries, advocating for a balanced approach that includes proper recovery methods. The episode concludes with an announcement about a new Masterclass program aimed at helping parents navigate American youth soccer effectively.
key_points: Knowledge vs Expertise: Knowledge can be acquired through research and observation, but true expertise requires years of practical experience.
Practitioners vs Reporters: Actual players and coaches have insights that cannot be replicated by reporters or analysts who may not have the same level of experience on the field.
Levels of Understanding: There are varying levels of comprehension across different roles in soccer, including club executives, coaches, players, administrators, fans, advisors, and media members.
Respecting Player Biology: Proper training should include recovery methods to prevent injuries and ensure sustainable player development.
New 343 Masterclass for Parents: The podcast introduces a program designed to educate parents on how to mentor their soccer players effectively.
takeaways: Recognize the difference between knowledge and expertise when consuming soccer analysis or training advice.
Support balanced training practices that include recovery methods to avoid injuries among young athletes.
Seek out educational resources like the 343 Masterclass for guidance on how to best support your child's development in youth soccer.

title: Episode 250 - Mamie Donaldson: Empowering Your Voice and Elevating Your Speaking Presence
transcript:
Today, we are celebrating the milestone of our 250th episode by bringing back a very special guest, Mamie Donaldson. Mamie is an acclaimed speaker, voice coach, and author who has been making a significant impact in the community for many years. She shares her insights on empowering your voice and elevating your speaking presence.

[00:01:23] **Marsha:** Well welcome to all of you out there, especially my special guest Mamie Donaldson. Thank you so much for joining me today to celebrate the 250th episode. As you can see, I am wearing my chucks today because I love them so much and they are a good indicator that it's going to be a conversation that really gets down to business.

[00:01:43] **Mamie:** Thank you, Marsha. It is a pleasure to be here with you again on your show. I am looking forward to our conversation today and celebrating this special milestone.

[00:01:52] **Marsha:** Well, let's get started then. Mamie, can we start by having you tell us about the key factors that contribute to a powerful speaking presence?

[00:02:03] **Mamie:** Absolutely, Marsha. A powerful speaking presence is a combination of several key elements such as vocal variety, body language, and message delivery. Vocal variety includes using pitch, tone, and pace effectively, which helps to engage your audience and convey different emotions. Body language should be positive and confident, making eye contact with the audience and gesturing naturally to emphasize key points. Lastly, it's essential to deliver a clear, concise message that resonates with your listeners.

[00:02:43] **Marsha:** That makes sense. How do you suggest people improve their vocal variety?

[00:02:51] **Mamie:** One of the best ways to enhance vocal variety is through voice training exercises. I often recommend using a range of pitch, tone, and pace in your speech. For example, when introducing a topic, you might use a lower, slower voice to establish authority and set the tone for the presentation. As you move into specific points or arguments, you can increase your pitch and pace to emphasize key ideas. To practice this, record yourself speaking on various topics and analyze how well you are using vocal variety.

[00:03:41] **Marsha:** That's a great suggestion. So, Mamie, do you have any advice for someone who is nervous about public speaking?

[00:03:51] **Mamie:** Absolutely. One of the most effective strategies to overcome stage fright is through deep breathing exercises and visualization techniques. Deep breathing can help calm your nerves and reduce anxiety. Visualization involves imagining a successful presentation, focusing on positive outcomes, and visualizing yourself confidently delivering your speech. Additionally, practicing in front of a mirror or with a small group of trusted friends can boost your confidence before the big event.

[00:04:36] **Marsha:** Those are all great tips. Mamie, you have written several books on public speaking and voice coaching. Could you tell us about some of the key messages in these works?

[00:04:52] **Mamie:** Certainly. In my book 'Voice Power: Mastering Your Speaking Presence,' I emphasize the importance of mastering your voice to achieve a confident, impactful speaking presence. The book covers techniques for improving vocal variety, using breathing properly, and projecting your voice effectively. Another key message is that effective communication involves more than just what you say; it's also about how you say it. 'Speech Skills: A Guide to Mastering Your Public Speaking' focuses on developing the skills necessary to deliver compelling speeches and presentations, including storytelling techniques and handling questions from the audience.

[00:05:39] **Marsha:** Those are fantastic insights. Mamie, could you give us an example of how someone might use vocal variety in a real-life situation, like a business presentation?

[00:06:17] **Mamie:** Certainly. In a business presentation, vocal variety can be used to engage the audience and highlight key points. For instance, during your introduction, you could use a lower, slower voice to establish credibility and set the tone for the rest of the presentation. As you discuss different aspects of your topic, vary your pitch, tone, and pace to emphasize important information. You might also use pauses effectively to give the audience time to absorb key ideas or reflect on what has been said. By using these techniques, you can keep your listeners engaged throughout the presentation.

[00:07:12] **Marsha:** Those are some really practical tips. Mamie, could you explain how body language plays a role in public speaking?

[00:07:34] **Mamie:** Body language is crucial because it can convey confidence and authenticity to your audience. Positive gestures, such as open hand movements and appropriate facial expressions, can help reinforce your message and make it more relatable. Maintaining good posture and eye contact also helps establish a connection with your listeners. However, it's important not to overdo body language; natural, subtle movements are often the most effective.

[00:08:13] **Marsha:** That's great advice. Mamie, you have a unique approach to teaching public speaking and voice coaching. Could you tell us more about your methods?

[00:08:29] **Mamie:** My approach is rooted in the belief that everyone has the potential to become an effective speaker. I focus on helping individuals identify their personal strengths and weaknesses, and then work with them to develop strategies for improvement. For example, I might use role-playing exercises to help people practice different speaking scenarios, or conduct one-on-one coaching sessions to address specific challenges. My goal is always to empower my clients to become more confident and engaging speakers.

[00:09:18] **Marsha:** That's wonderful. Mamie, you are known for your humorous approach in public speaking and voice coaching. How do you balance humor with professional development?

[00:09:37] **Mamie:** Humor is a powerful tool that can help make my sessions more engaging and relatable. I believe it's important to find the right balance between entertaining and informative content. While laughter can break the ice and create a positive atmosphere, it's also crucial to ensure that the information being conveyed is relevant and valuable to the participants. Humor should enhance, not detract from, the learning experience.

[00:10:26] **Marsha:** That's great advice. Mamie, you have been a huge supporter of various causes throughout your career. Could you tell us about some of these initiatives?

[00:10:43] **Mamie:** I've had the privilege to work with several organizations that focus on empowering individuals through public speaking and leadership development. For example, I have partnered with Toastmasters International to help members refine their communication skills and build confidence in front of groups. Additionally, I have been involved with various local community events where I offer free workshops and talks aimed at helping people improve their speaking abilities.

[00:11:32] **Marsha:** That's wonderful work you're doing, Mamie. Finally, could you share some advice for someone who is thinking about becoming a public speaker or voice coach?

[00:12:06] **Mamie:** Absolutely. First and foremost, practice your craft through speaking opportunities as often as possible. Seek out local clubs like Toastmasters to gain experience in front of an audience. Additionally, consider enrolling in courses or workshops to learn from experienced professionals. Most importantly, be authentic and passionate about what you do; this will resonate with your listeners and make your message more compelling.

[00:12:46] **Marsha:** That's fantastic advice. Mamie, it has been such a pleasure speaking with you today. Thank you for sharing your insights on public speaking and voice coaching with our audience.

[00:13:05] **Mamie:** Thank you, Marsha. I enjoyed this conversation and look forward to staying in touch. Have a great week everyone, and remember to empower your voice and elevate your speaking presence wherever you go.

title: Key Insights into Sleep Disorders and the Importance of Sleep

introduction.quote: We still are a long way from answering the big questions about sleep, such as why we do it and why we dream. It's amazing that we spend a third of our lives doing something so mysterious.
introduction.speaker: Dr. Guy Leschsina

details.REM Sleep and Cataplexy: Cataplexy is exclusive to narcolepsy, a neurological disorder. It causes sudden muscle weakness due to the abnormal activation of REM sleep mechanisms during waking hours.
details.PTSD and Dreams: Dreams are not just meaningless garbage but can be related to traumatic experiences. This is evident in people with PTSD who often have recurring nightmares.

details.Deep Slow Wave Sleep vs REM Sleep: While deep slow wave sleep appears more crucial for cognitive function and physiological stability, both phases are important. The brain prioritizes non-REM sleep when sleep deprived.
details.Emotional Processing in Dreams: Dreams may play a role in emotional processing and memory consolidation, particularly in the context of PTSD.

details.Insights into Brain Functioning: Studying extreme sleep disorders provides insights into how the brain functions under normal conditions.
details.Potential for New Discoveries: Understanding what happens when parts of the brain are damaged can reveal more about the brain's normal processes.

details.Purpose of Sleep and Dreaming: Despite significant progress, we still don't fully understand why humans sleep or what happens during dreaming.
details.The Third of Our Lives: Sleep is a fundamental aspect of human life that remains as mysterious as eating or drinking.

sections.title: Key Messages on Sleep and Its Importance

details.Awareness of Sleep's Role: There is growing awareness of the importance of sleep for overall health, mood, cognitive function, and physiological stability.
details.Balance in Sleep Management: Finding a balance between adequate rest and daily responsibilities is crucial.

quotes: I started suffering the same sort of conditions, very teary, really worried about unnecessarily unwary some things and found it very hard to make decisions, hard decisions about bail and sentencing and things like that.

If you continually just put yourself in their shoes and really feel their pain, then I think that's a recipe or for me at least, that was a recipe for real mental affliction. On the other hand, if you're simply stepping back a bit and saying, 'Well, I really want this person not to be suffering,' there's a subtle but important difference in terms of what it does for the decision maker or for the listener.

podcastTitle: CyberWire Podcast 756: A Day in the Life of Cybersecurity

content.headline: Saudi Arabia and Qatar are engaged in an ongoing cyber war.
content.details: CyberWire reports that Saudi Arabia and Qatar are engaged in an ongoing cyber war, which is being fought primarily over social media. The conflict began last year after the Saudi prince was caught on video speaking out against Qatar’s leadership. Since then, both countries have been using their respective intelligence agencies to harass, threaten, and intimidate citizens of each other's country.

content.headline: The Saudi prince accused of ordering a hacking attack on a US citizen.
content.details: The Wall Street Journal reports that the US State Department is investigating an incident in which a Saudi prince allegedly ordered a cyber-attack to steal data from a private American corporation. It appears this prince may have been involved with the hacking of a Saudi-owned business in 2017, where he was accused of ordering the hacking as revenge against his own father for firing him.

content.headline: NIST's new cybersecurity guidance focuses on critical infrastructure.
content.details: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released a new set of draft guidelines to help organizations identify, prioritize, and protect critical cyber assets. The guidelines are meant for use by companies that provide utilities and other services that are vital to the nation's safety.

content.headline: A report on cyber attacks against banks in Russia.
content.details: Banks in Russia have reported an increase in phishing attacks over the past two months, according to a joint security bulletin from the Central Bank of the Russian Federation and the Federal Security Service (FSB). The FSB has issued a warning that hackers are using a new type of malware called the “Nazar” Trojan. The report also includes a list of specific cyber-attacks against banks in Russia.

content.headline: Vulnerability in Microsoft Windows 7 and 8.
content.details: Microsoft is addressing an important vulnerability in its older operating systems, Windows 7 and 8. The company has released a patch to address the issue, which could allow attackers to remotely execute code on affected devices.

content.headline: The importance of BGP and DNS in critical infrastructure.
content.details: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) and DNS (Domain Name System) are crucial components of the internet, but they can also be a target for attacks. Seth Finkelstein explains that these protocols are often overlooked because they operate out of sight, but they play a vital role in maintaining the stability and security of the global network.

content.headline: The impact of BGP hijacking on organizations.
content.details: Seth Finkelstein discusses the potential consequences of BGP hijacking, where an attacker can route traffic through their own IP addresses, potentially leading to data theft or denial-of-service attacks. He explains that this type of attack is particularly dangerous because it can affect entire regions and disrupt services for many organizations.

content.headline: The role of DNS in internet security.
content.details: Seth Finkelstein highlights the importance of DNS in ensuring the security of websites and online services. He notes that attacks on DNS servers, such as those using DDoS (Distributed Denial-of-Service) methods, can lead to service disruptions and allow attackers to redirect traffic to malicious sites.

content.headline: The challenges of securing BGP and DNS.
content.details: Mike McCabe discusses the difficulties of securing these protocols, including the decentralized nature of their management. He explains that while there have been efforts to improve security through initiatives like RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure), more work is needed to address vulnerabilities in BGP and DNS.

content.headline: The importance of collaboration between organizations.
content.details: Both Seth Finkelstein and Mike McCabe emphasize the need for cooperation among different stakeholders, such as ISPs, content providers, and government agencies. They stress that a coordinated effort is necessary to maintain the security and stability of critical infrastructure.

title: DevSecOps Days Recap with Ken Anderson and Greg Schofield

topics.details: Ken and Greg provide a recap of their experience at the conference, sharing insights on how to improve security in software development processes.

The hosts debate the pros and cons of each cloud service provider, concluding that Google Cloud Platform (GCP) might be the most intuitive but agreeing that Azure has become more user-friendly over time.
