Title: 10 Steps for Building a Successful Online Coaching Business
Summary: This podcast episode discusses key steps to build and maintain a successful online coaching business. The hosts provide actionable advice on program design, client acquisition, long-term thinking, and the importance of patience.

Steps.Title: Outline Your Program
Steps.Description: Define what your program includes and doesn't include to maintain consistency and efficiency.

Steps.Title: Coach for Free
Steps.Description: Help people for free in the early stages, which can lead to referrals and testimonials.
Examples: Help friends with workouts or nutrition as a way of building credibility and trust.

Steps.Title: Help Current Network
Steps.Description: Utilize your existing network for early clients. Friends, family, colleagues are often willing to try out your services.
Examples: Help a friend who is planning a wedding lose weight.

Steps.Title: Write Long-Form Articles
Steps.Description: Create high-quality content that establishes you as an authority in the field. Each article should take at least 20 hours to complete.
Details: At least 20 hours for each long-form article, with a minimum of eight hours recommended.

Steps.Title: Define Your Offering
Steps.Description: Clearly outline what you are offering so that you can maintain efficiency and clarity in your services.
Benefits: Prevents confusion among clients, reducing inefficiencies.

Steps.Title: Patience is Key
Steps.Description: Do not expect overnight success. Building a coaching business requires patience and persistence.
Examples: The host took nine months to secure his first paid client after consistent content creation.

Steps.Title: Systematize Your Process
Steps.Description: Create a system that can be scaled as your business grows, ensuring consistency and quality.
Benefits: Consistency leads to better results for clients, making the business more reliable.

Steps.Title: Outline What's Included/Not Included
Steps.Description: Document exactly what you offer, including any exclusions. This helps manage client expectations.
Details: Specify details like client check-in days and the frequency of updates.

Steps.Title: Write Supplement Reviews (Optional)
Steps.Description: Recommend reputable supplements based on thorough research to build credibility with clients.
Benefits: Establishing trust through credible recommendations can enhance your reputation.

Steps.Title: Time Management
Steps.Description: Allocate time effectively, focusing on quality over quantity in the early stages of building a coaching business.
Tips: Spend more time writing better articles instead of creating more.

Key Takeaways: Define your offering clearly to avoid confusion and inefficiencies.
Help people for free to build credibility and get referrals.
Establish a long-term view with patience as the cornerstone of success.
Create quality, in-depth content that showcases your expertise.
Conclusion: Building a successful online coaching business requires dedication, clarity, and persistence. By following these steps and maintaining a patient mindset, you can lay a strong foundation for growth and long-term success.

2. Nutrition: Fat loss is emphasized more through low-intensity steady-state cardio rather than high-intensity interval training (HIIT), unless nutrition is not properly managed.
3. Client Progression: Start with simpler movements that can be mastered before progressing to more complex ones, ensuring higher intensity and better technique are maintained.
4. Coaching Philosophy: Basic principles of coaching should always prioritize the client's safety and ease of understanding over complexity or advanced techniques.
5. Fatigue Management: Emphasizes the importance of managing overall fatigue in clients' training programs.
6. Flexibility and Mobility: Importance of proper mobility in preventing injuries during weightlifting and other physical activities.

topics.title: Polarization and Bubbles in Society
topics.content: The conversation focused on the current polarization in society, where people often only listen to sources that align with their beliefs. Barry emphasized that relying solely on one's 'team' or echo chamber for information creates a bubble, leading to poor decision-making and societal division.

topics.title: Education and Media Bias
topics.content: Barry criticized the current education system and mainstream media, arguing they often present biased views. He highlighted that many people cannot provide evidence for their arguments beyond repeating what they've heard from trusted sources, creating a 'house of cards' mentality.

topics.title: Postmodernism and Its Appeal
topics.content: Barry provided an argument that postmodernism's appeal lies in its seduction to distrust the government and authority. This discussion mirrored Merle’s earlier points about the need for societal evolution beyond traditional structures.

topics.title: The Waco Siege Documented Series
topics.content: The guests discussed a documentary series on the Waco siege, expressing different views on its portrayal of both law enforcement and David Koresh. Barry was critical of how the government handled the situation, while Merle focused more on the manipulative nature of cult leaders.

title: Simply Christ Podcast Episode 23: Love Like God - Part 1
transcript:
This is the Simply Christ podcast where we are dedicated to simplifying your walk so that you can shine the light of Christ brightly and clearly, not being shadowed by philosophy or teachings of men. In this episode, hosts David and Leon discuss the importance of loving like God, focusing on the concepts of grace, truth, and the role of Jesus as the gateway into a relationship with God.

The conversation centers around several key points:
1. The importance of a living relationship with Jesus for exercising faith and love in daily life.
2. The idea that accidental serving of God happens more often when one comes to God regularly through reading, prayer, worship, and gathering at church.
3. The role of grace in allowing individuals to pursue God while making mistakes along the way.
4. Checking senses with the reality of God's word as a crucial step in walking out Christian principles.
5. The importance of staying committed to faith despite challenges and potential 'waxing cold' (as mentioned in Revelation).
6. Practical steps like fanning into flame, the gift that was given to us, to maintain the love for God within our hearts.
key_points: The gateway into the Christian walk is Jesus.
Importance of grace in self-forgiveness and pursuit of faith.
Growing up in Christ through regular reading, prayer, worship, fellowship, and application of God's word.
Staying committed to one's faith despite challenges (avoiding 'waxing cold').
Practicing the qualities of love as defined by Paul (love is patient, kind, not envious, etc.).

host: [Music] You often hear how important it is to behave professionally at work, but what exactly does it entail? A professional is someone who displays high levels of expertise and efficiency. The others think of them as competent, reliable, and respectful. Professionals are a credit to not only themselves, but also to others. Professionalism encompasses all of these definitions, but it also covers much more, especially for news reporters. Journalists must abide by a particular set of characteristics to compose themselves and maintain a sense of professionalism in the media realm. When discussing the mental health of news reporters and journalists, why is it important to talk about the meaning of professionalism? How can news reporters be completely professional in their day-to-day roles? Welcome back to Newsroom Mayhem. I'm Alexa Morsey, your host for this series, and this is episode 2 of 5, like a pro. Diverse cultures and population view professionalism differently. However, these divergent contrasts can overlap and uncover new and illuminating comparisons. An article by Atul Gawande from The New Yorker describes the evolution of professionalism and how the definition of professionalism has drastically altered over time. It is crucial to analyze the divergence from the traditional and the modern definition of professionalism to paint a more accurate picture of how journalists must adjust to not only various media platforms, but to their own workplace environments.

First, there was the word 'professional,' which initially meant someone engaged in occupation connected to a scientific learning that was liberally acquired. As a worker, his or her accomplishments stood in contrast to the artisan or craftsman or whose skills were acquired through manual labor using traditional methods. When professionalism was first introduced in the Victorian era, where the suffix 'ism' was added to coin the word 'professionalism,' which denoted a practice or condition that was related to a principle, devotion, or adherence. Hence, putting both together gives a definition of professionalism as the practice of scientific learning in accordance with principles. The Victorian era planted the seeds of the new breed of professionals in the workplace. A century later, during the out of the times of the young urban professionals in the 1980s, a professional was referred to as a 'yuppy' and was defined as someone who was obsessed with his or her own career. Hence, it was merely only themselves who they cared for and supported in the professional realm. Nevertheless, they were often admired at times for their elegance and classy taste, but when their careers ended because of the Wall Street Market crash of 1987, they were remembered only for their greed, self-centeredness, and indifference to their social surroundings. By revisiting early definitions of what it means to be a professional, it is apparent to see how the concept of professionalism took shape and how it deteriorated in a century that was filled with political corruption and accesses. Today, the meaning of professionalism has once again changed, presumably back to its original concept of hard work, honesty, and social responsiveness. By acknowledging how the definition of professionalism has changed over time, it is easier to form a more concrete definition of what it means to be a professional for journalists. title: Cardon Solutions Podcast - Episode 137: Sonya Murrell on Navigating Anxiety, Depression, & Finding Gratitude in Tough Times
transcript:
In this episode of the Cardon Solutions podcast, host Kevin Hart welcomes Sonya Murrell, a business and life coach who specializes in working with individuals and organizations to navigate through tough times. Sonya shares insights on how to manage anxiety and depression, find gratitude during difficult periods, and stay present and focused on the moment.

Some key takeaways from this conversation include:
- Journaling can be a powerful tool for managing emotions and finding silver linings in challenging situations.
- Gratitude is essential for mental health and should not be underestimated. Sonya suggests keeping a gratitude journal to help cultivate positivity and focus on the good.
- Anxiety and depression manifest differently: anxiety often stems from worrying about the future, while depression tends to make us feel stuck in the past. Being present and mindful can help alleviate both conditions.
- Sonya encourages listeners to confront negative emotions instead of suppressing them, as this can lead to breakthroughs and personal growth.
- Mindfulness practices like breathing exercises and focusing on the breath can help bring one's attention back to the present moment when feeling overwhelmed.

title: Wave of the World Podcast Episode 28 - Alexis Lacâ€™s Joining the Show & Discussing Beyoncé and Michael Jackson
transcript:
host: (Music) Welcome to episode 28 of the wave of the world podcast. Today, we have a special guest joining us, Alexis Lacâ€™s, who will be discussing Beyoncé and Michael Jackson with us. Thanks for being on the show, Alexis.

Alexis Lacâ€™s: Thank you so much for having me. I'm excited to be here today.

host: Let's start by talking about your background. How did you get interested in music and specifically Beyoncé and Michael Jackson?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: Well, I've always been a fan of music since I was a little girl, but my love for Beyoncé and Michael Jackson really started when I was around 10 or 11 years old. I remember watching the Super Bowl halftime show featuring Beyoncé with The Destiny's Child, and it was such an amazing performance that it sparked my interest in her. As for Michael Jackson, I grew up listening to his music, and his music videos were always a big part of my childhood.

host: Can you tell us about your favorite Beyoncé and Michael Jackson performances?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: Absolutely! One of my favorite Beyoncé performances is the halftime show at Super Bowl LIII. I was so impressed with how she performed and choreographed it, as well as the powerful and emotional message behind it. As for Michael Jackson, his performance on the 1988 American Music Awards is one that always blows me away. He had such stage presence and charisma, and his dance moves were just mesmerizing.

host: It's interesting how their performances still resonate with people today. What do you think sets them apart from other performers?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: I think it's their unique talents and the impact they've made on popular culture that set them apart. Beyoncé is known for her powerful vocals, dynamic choreography, and emotional delivery of her music. Michael Jackson was a master of dance and had an incredible ability to captivate audiences with his performances. They both created iconic hits and left an indelible mark on the music industry.

host: Moving on, can you share your thoughts about Beyoncé's Homecoming concert and its significance in today's world?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: The Homecoming concert was a groundbreaking event that highlighted the importance of Black excellence and cultural heritage. It showcased the talent of not only Beyoncé but also other artists like Kendrick Lamar, Jhené Aiko, and Solange. It was a celebration of African-American culture and history, which is essential in today's society to promote diversity and inclusivity.

host: How do you think their music has influenced your life or the lives of others?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: Their music has had a significant impact on my life. It inspired me to pursue my passion for music and encouraged me to be confident in expressing myself through dance and performance. For many people, Beyoncé and Michael Jackson's music provided a sense of empowerment and allowed them to connect with their cultural identity.

host: In terms of live performances, have you ever seen either artist perform live?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: I've only had the opportunity to see Beyoncé perform live once at the 2014 Homecoming concert at Vanderbilt University. It was an unforgettable experience as she captivated the audience with her powerful vocals and amazing choreography.

host: That sounds amazing! What was your favorite part of the performance?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: My favorite part was when Beyoncé took a seat during one of the songs, which made me realize that even someone as talented as she can be vulnerable. It was a moment of genuine emotion and connection with her audience.

host: That's a great point. Now, let's talk about some of your experiences at music concerts. Can you share any memorable moments from concert experiences?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: One of the most memorable moments I've had at a concert was when Post Malone performed. He sat down and played guitar during one of his songs, which was a surprise for the audience. Another memorable moment was seeing Trace Homes perform live, where he took off his shirt and threw it to the crowd.

host: Wow, those are some wild experiences! Can you tell us more about your encounter with Post Malone?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: It was such an exciting experience as I was in the third row, and he took off his shirt and threw it at me. A woman next to me grabbed it instead, which led to a moment of confusion and even some competitiveness.

host: That's hilarious! What about your experience with Trace Homes? Can you describe what happened?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: It was a wild scene as women were throwing their bras and panties at him. There were also ambulance calls due to the crowd's reaction, and two women fainted from the excitement.

host: That sounds intense! Do you have any advice for fans who might be considering attending a live concert?

Alexis Lacâ€™s: My advice would be to prepare yourself mentally and physically. Bring plenty of water, wear comfortable clothing, and be aware of your surroundings. It's also important to stay safe and avoid dangerous behaviors like throwing objects on stage.

host: Great advice! Well, thank you again for joining us today, Alexis. It was great chatting with you about Beyoncé and Michael Jackson.

Alexis Lacâ€™s: Thank you so much for having me. I enjoyed our conversation, and it's been a pleasure to discuss these iconic artists with you.

host: (Music) Thanks for listening to this episode of the wave of the world podcast. We hope you enjoyed the discussion about Beyoncé and Michael Jackson with Alexis Lacâ€™s. If you liked what you heard today, please like, share, and subscribe. And if you have any questions or topics you'd like us to cover in future episodes, feel free to reach out to us at wave of the world 19 at gmail.com. Until next time, keep enjoying the music.

title: Real Conversations with Lifecoats Jen Foster - Episode 32: Clint Greece on Manifesting Happiness and Peace through Vision and Imagination
transcript:
Jen Foster interviews Clint Greece, a life coach who emphasizes the power of imagination in manifesting happiness and peace. The conversation touches on topics such as problem-solving, using imagination to visualize positive outcomes, and transforming one's approach to coaching.

[0:00-2:15] Jen introduces herself and her guest, Clint Greece, a life coach with 20 years of experience who is passionate about helping people manifest happiness and peace through the power of imagination. She also mentions that this is episode 32 of her podcast.

[2:16-4:18] Jen shares how she met Clint and his commitment to being of service, mentioning a recent life crisis he experienced that led him to a new purpose in life.

[4:19-7:50] Clint discusses the concept of imagination as a tool for manifesting positive outcomes and offers an example of how visualization can be used to solve problems. He emphasizes that while problem-solving is important, it's equally important to use imagination and visualize a desired outcome.

[8:10-12:46] Jen shares personal examples of how visualization has helped her in different areas of life, such as changing jobs and manifesting positive outcomes in relationships. She also mentions the importance of writing things down and making specific visualizations to make them more effective.

[13:19-17:08] Clint explains that using imagination is a way to break free from limiting beliefs and create new possibilities, citing an example of how a client used visualization to overcome self-doubt in her career. He also mentions the importance of having a vision for one's life and carving out time to focus on it.

[17:09-22:48] Jen and Clint discuss the relationship between imagination, manifestation, and coaching. Clint emphasizes that as a coach, he helps clients use their imaginations in ways that align with their values and desires. He also mentions how he uses visualization exercises to help clients manifest positive outcomes.

[23:05-26:19] Clint talks about the importance of being open to new possibilities and not getting stuck in old patterns, using an example from his own life as a coach to illustrate this point. Jen shares her belief that everyone has the power to create their desired future and encourages listeners to take action towards achieving it.

[26:49-31:05] Clint discusses the role of service in his coaching work, mentioning how he focuses on helping clients find joy and purpose in life. He also emphasizes the importance of living a joyful and peaceful life as a coach himself, sharing his own journey towards this goal.

[32:47-34:15] Jen and Clint discuss their shared goals for transforming lives through coaching, emphasizing that everyone has the potential to manifest happiness and peace in their lives. They also mention how they use their personal experiences to inform their work as coaches.

[36:23-38:07] Jen thanks Clint for joining her on the podcast and encourages listeners to check out his website at ClintGreece.com, where they can learn more about his coaching services and access exercises and resources to help them manifest happiness and peace in their own lives.

title: Chicken Helmets and Stupid White Men on Facebook
author: Keyboard Warrior
content:
Today, I wanted to share a couple of interesting stories and observations that have caught my attention. The first one involves an unlikely friendship formed by engaging with a white male named Josh on Facebook.

In the context of a discussion about traffic barriers in our town, Josh and I found ourselves at odds over a particular intersection. Despite our disagreements, we managed to uncover common ground and share some amusing banter. What initially seemed like a conflict turned into a unique bond based on respect for each other's perspectives.

Josh now serves as my inspiration every day, solving town problems through Facebook posts, even if he is fat and unshaven. His profile picture depicts Thor from the Avengers in his most unrefined state – a perfect representation of our relationship. Together, we aim to tackle societal issues one post at a time.

However, this story isn't just about personal connections; it also delves into broader themes such as gender dynamics and social media interactions. The incident with the chicken helmets is an excellent example of how seemingly mundane ads can spark fascinating discussions on animal welfare and empathy in the digital age.

The desire for chicken helmets stems from a genuine concern: protecting chickens from comb pecking, a common form of bullying among fowl. While the idea of chicken helmets seems humorous, it raises important questions about compassion and understanding in our communities.

As always, let's strive to find solutions that promote empathy and kindness, whether we're addressing traffic laws or helping bullied chickens. Keep the discussions civil and productive – one post at a time.

summary: The podcast episode featured Daniel Hamilton, who shared his experience with intermittent fasting since 2013. He discussed various types of fasts, from 16:8 to longer durations like 5-2 and even three-day fasts. Daniel emphasized the importance of consulting a healthcare practitioner before starting more extended fasts, especially if you have diabetes or are taking medications that affect blood sugar levels. He also talked about hydration and electrolyte replenishment during fasting. The conversation included tips on how to gradually ease into intermittent fasting and how it can improve overall health. Additionally, Daniel mentioned the benefits of working out while in a fasted state, which includes an increase in human growth hormone. The episode concluded with encouragement for listeners to visit his website or social media pages for more information. Overall, the discussion provided valuable insights on intermittent fasting as a tool for better health and wellness.
key_points: Daniel Hamilton has been practicing intermittent fasting since 2013 after reversing his symptoms through this method combined with a real food ketogenic diet.

There are different types of fasting including 16:8, alternate day fasting (5-2), 24-hour fasts every other day, and longer fasts ranging from three to seven days. Longer fasts require prior experience with intermittent fasting.
Before starting an extended fast or altering medication dosage due to fasting, it's crucial to consult a healthcare practitioner.

Electrolyte replenishment is important during fasting, especially sodium, chloride, sulfate, magnesium, calcium, and potassium. Recommendations include pink salt, Epsom salt baths, and electrolyte drops.
Fasting can improve insulin sensitivity and potentially help with weight management. Fasted workouts have benefits such as increased human growth hormone levels.
Hunger is not a sign to end a fast; one should listen for signs of unwellness or weakness indicating the need to eat earlier than planned.
The episode encouraged listeners to visit Daniel's website, Instagram, and Facebook page for more information on his approach to health through intermittent fasting.

log_entry:
Video Call Wrap-Up: Parasha Chalach BaMidbar & Rahav's Story Analysis

- Participants discussed the connections between Rahav's story in Joshua and other biblical narratives, specifically highlighting parallels with the 12 spies sent by Moses and the angels who visited Lot and his family. 

- Key Points Discussed:
1) Rahav's story is compared to the scouts' mission: Both involve two unnamed men on a secret reconnaissance for information about the land.
2) Red strings: The red string hanging from Rahav's window paralleling the Passover blood on doorposts as a sign of salvation.
3) Language and themes: References to the Israelites leaving Egypt and crossing the Red Sea are echoed in Rahav's narrative, emphasizing her positive actions during this time.
4) Preservation of descendants: Rahav’s family is said to have remained in existence through generations, similar to Lot’s family. 
5) Angelic interactions: Both narratives involve angelic visitors who instruct and protect their hosts' families from impending destruction.
6) Davidic ancestry: Midrash suggests that Rahav is an ancestress of King David, making her a part of the lineage of Mashiach (Messiah).

transcript:
John, welcome back to Rapido Up. 

John: Hey, guys. Yeah, it's good to be here. Thanks for having me on.

Host: You're welcome. Now we've already established that this is an episode where we will be talking about the Eastern Conference teams and how they are going to fare in the upcoming season. Can you tell us a little bit more about your expectations for the Eastern Conference as a whole?

John: Absolutely, my expectations would be that, well, first of all, it's a reset. We're coming out of a situation where we saw everything before the shutdown and then we didn't see anything after the restart. So I think that's going to take some time for everybody to really get back into the groove.

Host: Yeah, definitely. And do you agree with the general consensus that the Eastern Conference is still quite strong, even if it's not as dominant as it used to be?

John: Absolutely, yeah. I think there are a lot of teams that have a ton of star power and are going to be in contention for a playoff spot. It just might take some time for them to get back on track.

Host: And what about the young players we've seen making their mark this season? Do you think they will have an impact on the Eastern Conference next year?

John: Absolutely, I mean, there's so much star power out there. You know, guys like Luka Doncic, Trae Young, and Deandre Ayton are going to be looking to make a mark in the playoffs. And I think it will be really interesting to see how they perform next year.

Host: Speaking of young players, let's talk about the Milwaukee Bucks. They have been one of the best teams in recent seasons. Do you think they will continue their dominance or is there room for other Eastern Conference teams to challenge them?

John: You know, it's always a possibility. The Bucks were on fire earlier this season before things shut down. But I do think that there are some teams like the Heat and the Sixers who could potentially pose a challenge to them next year.

Host: And what about the Indiana Pacers? They have been making waves in recent years with their young core of players. Do you see them as a team to watch for in the Eastern Conference?

John: Absolutely, I do. You know, the Pacers have a lot of potential and are led by some really talented players like Malcolm Brogdon and Domantas Sabonis. They could definitely make a run at the playoffs next year.

Host: That's great to hear. And finally, let's talk about the overall competitiveness of the Eastern Conference. Do you think it will be as competitive as the Western Conference?

John: I think so, yeah. The East has always been known for its competitiveness and depth, even though there may not be one dominant team like in the West. So I'm expecting a lot of upsets and exciting games throughout the season.

Host: Well, we certainly can't wait to see how it all plays out. Thanks again for joining us, John. And for our listeners, make sure to tune in next time as we dive deeper into some specific Eastern Conference teams and explore other issues affecting basketball.

title: Wednesday Discussion: Government Failures, Self-Defense Shootings, and More
summary: Host Andrew Hollister discusses a range of topics including government failures during the pandemic, self-defense shootings in New Mexico, and more with input from listeners. Topics include FDA regulatory issues, media bias, and personal safety.
transcript:
Today on Radio Free New York, we're continuing our discussion about what you want to talk about. We've received a lot of comments regarding government failures during the pandemic. Mark mentioned that there's much more that could be said to illustrate this issue. Garrett pointed out the FDA as one of the biggest federal failures surrounding COVID. I agree; if we had to keep the FDA, it should just serve in an advisory capacity and not have regulatory authority.

We also talked about media bias, with Jay pointing out that whoever buys the most ads from the media gets the most coverage. This is a significant concern when considering how news outlets may present information. We discussed the self-defense shooting incident in New Mexico, where an individual was shot while protesters were trying to pull down a statue. Based on the limited video footage available, it appeared that the shooting might have been justified as self-defense. However, we emphasized the need for more context and additional evidence before forming a definitive opinion.

We also touched upon personal safety topics such as good holster retention techniques and firearm ownership responsibilities. Additionally, we discussed the constitutionality of police actions during the incident, noting that arresting everyone with firearms may not have been legally permissible.

Stay tuned tomorrow when Kevin will discuss Cuomo's police reform plans.

The Sepsis Alliance has an amazing, very informative website. Your listeners can go to sepsis.org. And they will see with a scroll down the signs of sepsis. So they have a thing called chime and T is for temperature. You could be incredibly hot or incredibly cold. I is for infection. You have some sort of infection in your body, it be an infected tooth or a cut or in Ken's case, you know, bronchitis and pneumonia. So there's infection. And then M is for mental decline. It's kind of hard to rouse them and get them. They're not thinking clearly because it's in their bloodstream.

And then E is for excruciating pain. You feel like you're dying because you absolutely are. And the thing with sepsis that I urge your listeners to just be aware of is that there isn't a tomorrow with sepsis. You know, you can't wait. Oh, I feel better in the morning or I'll wait to go to the doctor tomorrow. No, if you have any of these signs or think you possibly could have sepsis, get in the car or have someone drive you to the emergency or the doctor and get a blood test. In 20 minutes, you will know whether you're septic or not. And if you are, you can get on the proper antibiotic protocol.

And you know, you won't have the outcome that Ken had because of his doctors, like Kaiser and his doctor, Colberton. You know, it's just so important that we are our best advocates. And I know because Ken was such a healthy person and he didn't want to go to the doctor, but unfortunately, he ended up in that situation where they didn't give him an antibiotic when they should have.
And then after 24 hours, it's too late.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: Thank you for sharing your story, Katie. How has the Sepsis Alliance been involved in raising awareness and what resources do they offer?

transcript.speaker: Katie Flak
lines: Well, I think it's really important that we spread this message because no one should die from needlessly or before their time. So the Sepsis Alliance has an amazing website with a lot of resources and information about sepsis. It's called sepsis.org.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: That’s wonderful. Can you tell us more about how your community and friends have supported you in this journey?

transcript.speaker: Katie Flak
lines: Oh, it's been incredible actually. The tennis community and the golf community, the ATP and the U.S. Open have all been incredibly supportive of me.
For example, at the Indian Wells Tennis Tournament, they did a beautiful memorial for Ken in the stadium in front of 20,000 people, which was really overwhelming for me.

But it was so fabulous. And they also did a Ken Flak Memorial Golf Tournament for the players at the Indian Wells Tennis Tournament. So that was really, really great. Ken loved golf. It was his passion and love of his life.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: That’s fantastic. How have you found ways to honor Ken's memory?

transcript.speaker: Katie Flak
lines: Well, I try to wake up every day and think of three things that I'm grateful for.
I think of my children, I think of my husband that I had. And I tried to come from a place of gratitude and be thankful for what I had and not for what I don't have.

So if any advice I could give would be to just wake up. It's a new fresh day. Be excited. Think of something you're going to do, go exercise, eat healthy, and pray or meditate. And I know the strength of God has definitely gotten me through these difficult times.

transcript.speaker: Host
lines: Thank you so much for your words of wisdom, Katie. It's inspiring to hear how you're continuing to live a full and meaningful life in memory of Ken.
For our listeners who want to learn more about sepsis or support organizations like the Sepsis Alliance, can you provide any final thoughts?

transcript.speaker: Katie Flak
lines: Yes. I would love people to just start an organic dialogue of, 'Hey, do you know what sepsis is? Do you know the signs?' And check out sepsis.org and see the signs and know the signs.

And if you don't get a feeling like you don't trust what you're hearing from the doctor, go get a second or third opinion because no one knows you or your child or your husband like you do. And you know, it's just so important that we are our best advocates.

author: Saint Basil The Great
title_of_source: The Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers: Second Series, Volume 8
reading_title: On the Divinity of the Son

reading.preamble: In this selection, Saint Basil The Great discusses the divinity of the Son in relation to God the Father. He argues that the Son is co-eternal with the Father and shares His essence.

content.divinity_of_son: Saint Basil emphasizes that the Son is not a created being but has always existed, stating, 'But I am ashamed at the degradation, degraded conception to which, by course, the argument, I have been brought down. Let us therefore revert to the loftier themes of our discussion.' He maintains that the Son is co-eternal with the Father and asserts their unity of essence in God.
content.equality_with_father: Basil argues for the equality of the Son with the Father by stating, 'The Christ is the power of God, and the wisdom of God. And so all things are made through him, by him.' He refutes the idea that the Son received his authority from the Father as if he were a subordinate, instead affirming their mutual connection in the divine will.
content.uncreatedness: He discusses the uncreated nature of the Son and states that 'The Christ is the power of God, and the wisdom of God. And so all things are made through him, by him, not in the discharge of any slave-ish service,' emphasizing his role as creator and co-worker with the Father.
content.blessings_through_son: Saint Basil further elaborates on the blessings bestowed upon humanity through the Son, stating, 'For our Lord is an essentially good way where airing a strain or unknown to that which is essentially good to the father.' He affirms the Son's role as mediator and provider of divine gifts.
content.perfection_of_son: The text concludes with an affirmation of the Son’s perfection and unity with the Father, stating, 'Thus on all sides is demonstrated to true doctrine, that the fact that the Father creates through the Son neither constitutes the creation of the Father imperfect, nor exhibits the active energy of the Son as feeble.'

Summary:
In this podcast, the speaker discusses Jesus' statement that he did not come to create peace but division, challenging the common misconception that world peace can be achieved by conforming to a single belief system. Key points include: 

1. The concept of 'world peace' often implies unity and agreement on specific ideologies or beliefs.
2. Jesus encourages conflict due to disharmony in values and beliefs (dissonance), rather than promoting uniformity.
3. Being a friend of the world means being an enemy of God, as the message of the cross involves taking sides on controversial issues.
4. True peace from God is described as tranquility and calm in the storm—remaining peaceful even when conflicts arise due to opposing views.
5. The speaker warns against conforming to worldly narratives that promote unity at the cost of true values and faith.
6. Christians should be prepared for conflict and opposition, knowing that following Jesus often leads to being hated by some people.
7. The ultimate goal is not to create friction but to remain steadfast in one's beliefs while engaging with those who have different views.}
Key Messages: Jesus did not come to bring peace as the world understands it; he brings division through conflicting values and beliefs.
True peace comes from alignment with God’s values, even amidst conflicts and disagreements.
Following Jesus may lead to being hated by those who disagree with his teachings or message.
Worldly unity is often achieved at the cost of true spiritual values and can be manipulated for political purposes.
Christians should remain steadfast in their beliefs while engaging respectfully with those who have different views.
Main Points: Explanation of Jesus' statement about division (John 17:21-23)
Contrast between world peace and the peace offered by God
Importance of not conforming to worldly narratives that promote unity at the cost of values
Preparation for conflict and opposition when following Jesus
Peace from God is tranquility in the midst of conflict, not absence of conflict

episode_title: Too Good to Waste Podcast Episode 8: Cooking with Scraps with Lindsay Jean Hard

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Welcome back, everyone. This is Sue Marshall from Too Good to Waste here in episode eight of the Too Good to Waste Podcast series. Today we're talking with Lindsay Jean Hard about cooking with scraps and reducing food waste.

transcript.speaker: Lindsay Jean Hard
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Lindsay Jean Hard, author of Cooking with Scraps and a home baker. I've been baking for years, but I had never thought to use all parts of the ingredients until this book came along.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: That's great! Can you tell us more about your background in cooking and how Cooking with Scraps came about?

transcript.speaker: Lindsay Jean Hard
transcript.text: Sure, I've always been passionate about baking and using fresh ingredients. But after learning about the amount of food waste that occurs every day, I wanted to find a way to make a difference in my own kitchen.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: That's amazing! What inspired you to start using all parts of your ingredients and how did it change the way you bake?

transcript.speaker: Lindsay Jean Hard
transcript.text: I read an article about a chef who was using apple peels in his dishes, and I thought, why not try it with my baking? It turned out to be such a success that I decided to write a book about the process.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: That's fantastic! Can you give us some examples of how using all parts of your ingredients can benefit both the environment and our kitchens?

transcript.speaker: Lindsay Jean Hard
transcript.text: Absolutely, it can reduce food waste by up to 30% in a commercial setting like Zingerman's Bakehouse. It also adds flavor and texture to dishes that you might not normally expect. For example, using apple peels in baking makes the bread taste more like apples.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: That sounds delicious! Can you share a recipe from your book with us?

transcript.speaker: Lindsay Jean Hard
transcript.text: Of course, one of my favorites is the Hummingbird Cake. It uses all parts of the banana and the apple peels to make it more flavorful.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: That sounds amazing! How can people find your book and connect with you?

transcript.speaker: Lindsay Jean Hard
transcript.text: You can get Cooking with Scraps at your local bookstore or online. And you can follow me on Instagram at Lindsay Jean Hard, or visit my website to reach out.

title: Weapons and Shields of the Late Medieval Period
summary: The host discusses various shields (Buckler, Kite, Heter) and weapons (Halberd, Mace, Lucerne) used in late medieval combat. The Buckler is described as a small, portable shield used for personal protection, while Kite and Heter shields were larger and more commonly seen on the battlefield. Halberds are noted for their effectiveness in formations due to their curved blade shape which allowed for both thrusting and swinging motions. Maces and Lucerns (similar to halberds with hammer heads) became prominent against heavily armored opponents, focusing on breaking armor through crushing force rather than cutting.

Shields: Buckler: Small, portable shield used for personal protection
Kite Shield: Large, versatile shield useful in combat due to its size and quick maneuverability
Heter Shield: Smaller version of the Kite shield, used by cavalry for easier movement
Weapons: Halberds: Long spear weapons with curved axe heads effective for both thrusting and swinging motions
Maces: Heavy metal bit on a stick designed to crush armor rather than cut through it
Lucerne Maces: Similar to halberds but with hammer heads, used to break through armor

conclusion: The episode concludes with the host encouraging listeners to keep their blades sharp and minds sharper, hinting at future discussions on similar topics.

title: Petercappet Podcast Episode

segments.speaker: Host
segments.content: Welcome, everyone. Today we're diving into some real stories shared by our friend Peter Timothy Hanks, also known as BBQ USION. We have a story about blame and friendship from the past that I'm sure many of us can relate to.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.content: Now let's hear it for Peter!

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: Thank you, thanks for having me on today, folks. Today's story is about a specific instance when my friend Nathan blamed something on me that I had nothing to do with because he was scared of his father.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: We were around 14 or 15 years old at the time. My current wife Ashley, who wasn't my wife back then, had a birthday party and invited Nathan along with some other friends. She also asked if I could tag along because we always went places together.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: I smoked weed heavily during this period of time and brought it to parties frequently, while the others preferred alcohol for hooking up with girls. At Ashley's party, her guy friends were against smoking and started calling the cops on me.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: So, I left early and went to a nearby park where my friend was waiting. Nathan had stolen his father's tequila bottle from home and was passing it around at the party. His dad found out, got really upset, and drove directly to Ashley's house.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: Nathan blamed me for stealing the tequila when I didn't even get a sip of it. He said that he had stolen it from his father because he was scared of getting in trouble himself. This was a huge lie, and I felt really let down by my friend.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: After the party ended, I went back to Ashley's house for a ride home. My friends warned me that Nathan's dad wanted to find me because I stole his tequila. I told them it was all lies and that I wasn't going to take the blame anymore.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: In the end, Nathan went to his father and admitted what he had done. He eventually got grounded for a week or so but became more popular because of this incident. Meanwhile, people at the party who loved him started blaming me for everything I didn't do.

segments.speaker: Peter
segments.content: This story made me realize that it's important not to blame your friends for things you did yourself and to take responsibility for your actions instead of pushing them into trouble. Here ends today’s episode, thank you for listening!

Abinadi expounds on the first two commandments, emphasizing the importance of worshiping only God and prohibiting idolatry.

title: The Suffering Servant Song - Isaiah 53 and Its Application to Nephite Jews in Noah's Court
summary: This episode delves into Mosiah 14, which contains Abinadi's explanation of the suffering servant song (Isaiah 53) to King Noah's court. The discussion explores themes such as the nature of the Messiah, the concept of salvation on God's terms, and how to access the power of Christ's atoning sacrifice.
keyPoints: Abinadi provides a detailed explanation of Isaiah 53 within his address to King Noah’s court
The passage describes a suffering servant who bears griefs and sorrows for others
It highlights the contrast between the Messiah on God's terms versus humanly conceived messianic figures
Emphasizes the importance of a broken heart and contrite spirit in accessing Christ's saving power

context.background: The Book of Mormon depicts Nephites as Jews living in the Americas. This episode discusses how this text speaks to both historical context and personal application.
context.significance: Mosiah 14 is part of a larger conversation about prophecy, messianic expectations, and the nature of salvation within the Nephite community.

conclusion: The discussion concludes with reflections on how the principles from Isaiah 53 apply to modern-day Christians seeking salvation through Christ’s atoning sacrifice.
It emphasizes the necessity of a humble, contrite heart in order to receive and benefit from the saving power of Jesus Christ.

And it came to pass that after Mosiah had gone up upon the mountain, he saw the inhabitants of the land Lehi-Nephi, and they were suffering because of the iniquities which they had committed; yea, their hearts did smite them because of the iniquity which they had done against their brethren.

And he began his work anew, and also his son Alma, who had been chosen to be a ruler in his father's stead. And they did go forth upon the face of the land among all the people, preaching repentance unto them.
And it came to pass that after they had preached repentance and taught the word of God to the people, yea, even the word which was given by an angel from God—
They went forth among the people in the land Lehi-Nephi, who were the descendants of Zarahemla, and also the Lamanites who were scattered abroad on the face of the land.

And they began to declare unto them that the Lord had great compassion upon their people; yea, that he did visit his people in all their trials, and did comfort them, and did chasten them for a little season for their transgressions.
And now when Mosiah saw the hearts of the people smiting them because of their iniquities; and also when he saw that the Lamanites were about to perish, because of their wickedness—

Yea, even they were about to become extinct upon the face of the land; for behold, there were none who had been converted unto the true faith among them. And he saw that the people would perish because of their iniquities.

And it came to pass that Mosiah caused all those records which contained the prophecies and the revelations of God, which had been given unto the prophets from the beginning down to this time, should be brought before him;

That he might cause them to be read in the ears of all the people; that they might know concerning the covenants of the Lord, and also concerning the prophecies which had been spoken by the prophets from the beginning.

And it came to pass as Mosiah read he saw in them the promises of the Lord, that if the people would repent they should be restored; and that God had always shown mercy unto his people when they humbled themselves before him.

Video Transcription:
You're listening to the Amigos Retro Gaming Family podcast. Today, the hosts are discussing Dick Smith Wizard, an 18-game compilation for the Dick Smith Wizard computer, released in 1983. They cover various games such as Burger Time, Oil Rush, and Undersea Adventure (which is essentially Defender), among others.

Some highlights from their discussion include:
- Describing the graphics quality of each game, with some being simple and basic while others like Burger Time standing out for their more detailed sprites.
- Comparing the game mechanics to similar games released on other platforms, such as Oil Rush to Defend Your Castle or Undersea Adventure to Defender. 
- Discussing the controllers and how they affect gameplay, particularly in games where precise control is necessary.
- Sharing opinions on the overall enjoyment of each game, with some being praised for their playability while others receive more mixed reviews due to issues like awkward movement controls.
- Mentioning that the Dick Smith Wizard was a unique platform, given its use of an 8-bit Motorola processor and how it differed from other computers in Australia during that time.

Burger Time.Description: A side-scrolling arcade game where players manage a hamburger restaurant by cooking burgers and fries.
Burger Time.Controls: Player can only move left or right, but must be precise to avoid oil splatters and other hazards.

Oil Rush.Description: A vertical scrolling shooter game where the player controls a plane dropping oil bombs on enemy bases.
Oil Rush.Controls: More forgiving controls, but still requires precise timing to avoid crashing or running out of oil.
Oil Rush.Graphics/Sound: Basic graphics with simple sound effects.

Undersea Adventure (Defender Clone).Description: A side-scrolling shooter game where the player defends their castle from alien attacks while navigating an underwater environment.
Undersea Adventure (Defender Clone).Controls: More complex controls, requiring precise aim and timing to avoid being hit by enemy projectiles.
Undersea Adventure (Defender Clone).Graphics/Sound: Simple graphics with high-pitched sound effects.

Dick Smith Controller.Design: Has four buttons: two for movement (up/down), one for shooting, and one for jumping.
Dick Smith Controller.Effectiveness: While the controller is functional, it's not as precise or responsive as a traditional gamepad.

Show Notes.Conclusion: Hosts recommend playing some of the games on a modern console or computer for improved control, but still enjoy the nostalgia and simplicity of the Dick Smith Wizard platform.

### **[Confetti Moments Podcast: Wednesdays with Whitney Ramirez](https://www.confettimoments.com)**

**Episode Guests:** Whitney Ramirez from Learning With Crayons

**Date Recorded:** [Current Date]

**Topics Covered: Quizzes, Teaching Strategies, Classroom Management**

#### **[Introduction]**

- **Host:** Welcome to the Confetti Moments Podcast. Today's guest is Whitney Ramirez from Learning With Crayons. She will be sharing her experience with remote teaching and some fun 'would you rather' questions.

#### **[1. Fun Would You Rather Questions]**

- **Question 1: Amazon Prime or Food Delivery?**
  - **Whitney:** Amazon Prime. Thank goodness for Amazon during these times, but it's been interesting to use food delivery as a treat sometimes too!
- **Question 2: Home Office Setup or Coffee Shop Setup?**
  - **Whitney:** Home Office Setup because I'm not a coffee shop kind of person.
- **Question 3: Virtual Lessons or Paper and Pencil Lessons?**
  - **Whitney:** Paper and Pencil Lessons, although virtual lessons are fun too!
- **Question 4: Zoom or FaceTime?**
  - **Whitney:** Zoom because it's easier to coordinate with multiple people.

#### **[2. Teaching Strategies and Student Engagement]**

- **Host:** How do you keep students engaged during virtual lessons?
- **Whitney:** I try to make lessons interactive by using polls, Q&A sessions, and fun activities like trivia. It helps if the lesson is something they're already familiar with or interested in.

#### **[3. Classroom Management During Remote Learning]**

- **Host:** What tips do you have for managing a classroom during remote learning?
- **Whitney:** Consistency is key! Establish clear routines and expectations, and stay in touch with your students regularly through various communication channels.

#### **[4. Balancing Teaching Responsibilities During Quarantine]**

- **Host:** How do you balance teaching responsibilities while dealing with personal challenges during quarantine?
- **Whitney:** I try to maintain a routine and break tasks into manageable chunks. It helps to have a designated workspace and set working hours.

#### **[5. Maintaining Connection During Isolation]**

- **Host:** How do you feel 'normal' while staying at home? What are some things you're doing to make sure that you still feel like yourself?
- **Whitney:** Doing virtual hangouts with friends and family, keeping up with trivia quizzes, and maintaining a routine has helped me stay grounded.

#### **[6. Thanking Teachers and Parents]**

- **Host:** How do you express gratitude to teachers and parents during this unprecedented time?
- **Whitney:** I think it's important to acknowledge the hard work of both teachers and parents. Simple thank-you notes or messages can go a long way.

#### **[Conclusion]**

- **Host:** Thank you, Whitney, for joining us on the Confetti Moments Podcast. If anyone has any 'would you rather' questions, feel free to reach out to Whitney through social media. We hope this episode brought you some joy and inspiration!

audio_description: In this podcast, you'll learn how to make matcha whipped cream and assemble delicious profiteroles with it. Start by preparing your baking space, as we will first bake the profiteroles. The key is to pipe them correctly, ensuring they're not too close together on the tray and maintaining a consistent thickness. After baking, let them cool completely before moving on to the next step. Next, prepare the chocolate ganache for dipping the profiteroles. Use half a cup of cream, one teaspoon of vanilla extract, and 200 grams (7 ounces) of chocolate. Microwave the mixture until fully melted, then stir for another minute. Lastly, whip two cups of heavy cream with four dessert spoons of sugar and two teaspoons of matcha powder to create a soft, billowy whipped cream. This will be used as the filling for your profiteroles. Finally, slice each profiterole in half and fill it with the matcha whipped cream, then dip the cut edges into the chocolate ganache for an extra layer of indulgence.

summary:
In this episode, Ariel talks about the different situations that can lead to job loss or taking a leave of absence and offers advice on how to handle these scenarios during the job search process. She covers the following topics: 

- What happens when you get fired 
- What happens when layoffs occur 
- What happens when you need to take a leave of absence 

Key Points: 

1. When getting fired, it's important to understand that there can be multiple reasons and not to feel ashamed or guilty. Utilize your network and stay positive. 
2. Layoffs can sometimes lead to better opportunities at other companies, so make use of connections and competitors in the job search process.

4. Be resilient during times of change and trust that everything happens for a reason. Keep faith and stay positive.

- And just as a reminder, if you guys are listening live, this will be on my Instagram story for you guys, too. So make sure you're following me there and the Cooley's podcast page on IG so that I can post this up for you in your stories when it goes live.

- So without further ado, let's get to the first topic of today. Today is going to be a really fun day because we are running 5 miles together as a team. That was one of our goals and it feels really good to be getting back into that routine again after not having been able to do that for so long. I just did five miles yesterday, which was the most I've run in a while.

- And today's going to go even better because we're going to try running one mile at seven minutes and 50 seconds. I don't know if it's fast for me or not, but it feels like a good pace that I can maintain for my next goal which is five 30. It was actually pretty difficult for me to get back into the routine of running every day, so it feels really good to be able to do this again and not feel like there's some kind of internal struggle.

- Now we're getting to topic number two: night shift. I decided I'm going back to night shift because that is where all the good work hours are in food max, but also because I don't have a lot of money right now and I need to make sure that my bills are being paid on time. And it's just easier for me to go to work at night than to try and get up super early when I'm already tired from running.

- Topic number three: second stimulus check. I don't really know if this is something we should do, but it feels like the right thing to do because a lot of people are struggling financially right now, especially with everything going on in the world and with the economy being what it is. And so while I personally don't think that a second stimulus check would be the best use of my money right now, I understand why some other people might need one and would really appreciate having an extra boost.

- And then we're moving onto topic number four: watching anime fully cooley. The only thing I remember from reading the synopsis is that it has something to do with a guy who is trying to join a university and there are some really interesting characters in it, like a really cool samurai who is also an alien or something.

- And finally, we have topic number five: celebrating 30 episodes. It feels weird saying this because I don't think we've been doing the podcast for that long, but it's actually pretty impressive to be able to stick with one idea and talk about so many different things in a single podcast. title: The Bible, Logic and Righteousness - B.C.V Show 04/06/2020

summary.text: Chuck Morill: Good evening, everybody. This is the book chapter verse show.

And I'm your co-host Chuck Morill and we are talking about some of these logical things that God wants to do with us here on this earth, and also some illogical things. I mean, there's a lot of illogical things in the world. One of them is racism. And if you think back, if you go way back into history, before even America was formed as we know it today, racism was a problem that God wanted to eradicate from the human race.

And when I say eradicate, I don't mean get rid of the people. There's no need to get rid of anyone, but what I do mean is that God had put a law in place to make sure that everyone could be treated equally and that would have been the color of the skin or even more logical than that.

There was a time, Chuck Morill: Where you had white people and black people. And it's so ridiculous to be racist against another person because God created both of those races. There is no difference in the skin, and if there was some difference between black and white, I'm sure he would have told us about that, but what we do know is that everyone is made in his image and likeness. And that's a pretty big deal. You don't just go around saying, God created me one way and you another way.

And it's ridiculous to think that people are going to heaven and you're not because of the color of your skin. And it is illogical, if God didn't care about racism on Earth, why would he care so much about what happens after we die? Now, of course, I'm speaking in broad terms here, there's always exceptions.

But even the Bible shows us that we're all brothers and sisters under God. That's a big deal because it means that everyone is equal before him. And if you think about what I just said, Chuck Morill: That's why there was no need for Jesus to die on the cross. If one group of people were superior than another, there would be no point in Jesus dying for everybody.

Now, of course, you can't get rid of racism by just saying, 'Don't be racist' or 'racism is bad.' You have to understand that it's illogical. But the Bible tells us what God wants and gives us a way to live. It's not by your own righteousness because there isn't any such thing as self-righteousness in Scripture.

You have to be right with the righteousness of God, and that is found when you obey the gospel. And what is the gospel? Well, it's the death burial and resurrection of Jesus Christ. But there's more than just believing in those things, because if you don't change your mind about how you're living, then it doesn't matter.

You have to repent of your sins. Then you must be willing to confess that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And if you are an atheist, this confession is not for you because there's no point in saying something that isn't true.
You have to change your mind and believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And then confess him as such. And once you do all those things, you can be baptized for the remission of sins.

And when you're baptized, God adds you to His church, and that's a guarantee because Acts 2, chapter 7 tells us that everyone who believes in Jesus is added to his church. And Revelation 2, verse 10 tells us we must be faithful until the end if we want to be with him in heaven.

So now that you know what God wants, are you going to listen? Or are you going to keep doing things the way you're doing them? Because I think it's time for everyone to stop being illogical and start living by the logic of Scripture.

title: Silicon Valley Podcast - Episode 76: Jeff Walled on Depression, FinTech, & the Future of Work (24/05/2021)
transcript: William Glass: Hello and welcome to another episode of Silicon Valley. Today I am joined by Jeff Walled. Jeff is an investor, serial entrepreneur, and author of 'The 3 Rules of Fintech'. Jeff has experienced the highs and lows of startup life. He's worked with some incredible companies like PayPal, Tesla, and Square. But he also faced failure in his own startups, including a bout of depression that almost cost him everything. Today we talk about his journey from building a FinTech company to recovery and rebuilding, plus his take on the future of work and the impact of race relations in America today.
William Glass: Jeff, thank you so much for sitting down with me today. I'm really excited to dive into this conversation with you.
Jeff Walled: Of course, William. Thanks for having me. I'm glad to be here too.
William Glass: Let's start by talking a little bit about your background and what led you to become an entrepreneur in the first place?

Jeff Walled: Well, my career kind of started when I was 16 years old and I built one of the first websites that sold products online. It was a business called The Computer Store, it's now called Techware.net. And from there, I went to Wharton Business School at the University of Pennsylvania, where I met some really amazing people who helped me start my own businesses.
William Glass: That's pretty impressive for such an early age. So, what was your first startup and how did that go?

Jeff Walled: My first company was called MondoPay which was a mobile payments service that was kind of like Venmo or Cash App but before it existed. It was very exciting at the time because we were one of the few companies working on this concept, but in the end, it didn't quite make it to market.
William Glass: Okay, so how did you transition from MondoPay into PayPal and what did that experience teach you?

Jeff Walled: I left my first company after three years because we were trying to raise venture capital for an IPO but there was no one who wanted to invest. So, I joined eBay as a consultant where I helped build their payment platform, which is now PayPal. It taught me about the importance of building something that people want and being customer-centric.

William Glass: Wow, it sounds like you've had quite an interesting journey. And you mentioned earlier that you faced some challenges with your own businesses as well. Can you tell us a little bit more about that?

Jeff Walled: Sure, I started a company called Square Financial Technologies after working at PayPal and Tesla. It was a FinTech startup focused on providing personal finance solutions to small business owners. Unfortunately, the company didn't succeed in the way we hoped it would, but one of the most challenging aspects for me personally was dealing with depression that almost cost me everything.
William Glass: That sounds really tough. Can you tell us more about your experience with depression and how you managed to overcome it?

Jeff Walled: I had a rough time when my business failed, and it's not uncommon for founders to struggle emotionally after their business fails. But in my case, the stress of trying to save the company led me into deep depression which is a very isolating experience. It took time and support from friends, family, and colleagues to start feeling better.
William Glass: That's really admirable that you were able to get help and overcome it. So, what did you learn during this process?

Jeff Walled: One thing I learned was the importance of addressing problems early before they become bigger issues. Another lesson is that failure isn't just about your business or product, but also about your identity as a founder.
William Glass: And how have those lessons impacted your future endeavors and what you're doing now?

Jeff Walled: I've since started another FinTech company called 'The 3 Rules of Fintech' which is focused on providing personal finance solutions for small business owners. It's been a much more successful venture, but it has also taught me the importance of listening to data and trusting my gut instincts.

William Glass: That's great to hear that you've bounced back successfully. Can we talk about race relations in America today? You mentioned earlier how this conversation is rising to another level following the murder of George Floyd and the subsequent protests.

Jeff Walled: Absolutely, it's an important issue that needs to be addressed. The reality is that black Americans don't have the same opportunities as white Americans, and we need to do more to create a fairer society where everyone has equal access to resources and opportunities.
William Glass: Yes, I couldn't agree more. So, moving forward, what are some changes you would like to see in terms of race relations and opportunity for all?
Jeff Walled: There needs to be more investment in minority-owned businesses and a focus on education and job training programs that provide the skills needed to succeed in today's economy.

William Glass: That's great advice. And finally, let's talk about the future of work. You've mentioned before how changes are happening in the way we do things, especially with remote work becoming more prevalent. Can you share your thoughts on this?

Jeff Walled: Yes, I believe that remote work is here to stay and it has the potential to bring people together who otherwise might not have access to certain opportunities or resources. However, there are still challenges around cybersecurity, data privacy, and managing teams remotely.
William Glass: Thank you so much for your insights on these important topics. Before we wrap up, do you have any final words of wisdom for our listeners?
Jeff Walled: Just keep trying and don't give up. The biggest variable in determining success is yourself, but always listen to the data.
William Glass: I love that. Well, thank you so much, Jeff, for sitting down with me today. It's been a great conversation.
Jeff Walled: Thank you, William. It was my pleasure.

title: Coach Vaughn Podcast - Episode with VondeeCarlo
transcript: Welcome to the Coach Vaughn podcast, your source for comedy and insightful conversations. I'm your host, Coach Vaughn.
Today we have a special guest joining us - VondeeCarlo! Welcome to the show!
"Thank you so much for having me, Coach Vaughn. It's an honor to be here."

Coach Vaughn: You're welcome, VondeeCarlo. Now, let's dive into today's topic. You've been quite active on social media during this pandemic. Can you tell us a bit about your experience and what you've been up to?

"Absolutely! I've been using TikTok and Instagram to stay connected with my fans and share my thoughts on the world around me. It’s allowed me to be more involved in people's lives, even though we can't meet face-to-face right now."
Coach Vaughn: That's great to hear. You mentioned you have a significant following on TikTok. How has that been for you?

"It's been amazing. I didn't expect it to take off like this. Initially, I was just trying to share my thoughts and entertain people in a way that felt authentic to me. Now, there are over 3000 followers, which is beyond what I ever imagined!"
Coach Vaughn: Wow, congratulations on building such an engaged community. Do you think social media has changed the way comedians interact with their audience?

"Definitely. Social media allows for a more direct and immediate connection between me and my fans. It’s like they're right there in the room with us, even if we’re miles apart. I love being able to give them behind-the-scenes glimpses of my life as well."
Coach Vaughn: That's wonderful. Speaking of your life, how has the pandemic affected you and your family?

"It's been tough on everyone. My mother, who was dealing with cancer before the pandemic started, is getting stronger despite everything. She’s able to swing at a park now, which is a huge milestone for her. It just shows that no matter what we're going through, there are still little victories to celebrate."
Coach Vaughn: That's amazing to hear. What about your career? How has the pandemic affected your comedy gigs and plans?

"The schedule was looking really good until everything got postponed or canceled. I had some gigs lined up for this summer, but now it feels like I might not be able to go through with them due to all the uncertainty surrounding the virus. It’s definitely making me reconsider my options and maybe take a step back before jumping into something new."
Coach Vaughn: That's understandable. Have you had any thoughts on how professional sports, like the NBA, are handling things during this time?

"Yeah, it’s interesting to see how they’re doing things. They're trying their best to stay safe while still entertaining fans and players. But there’s no perfect solution, and I think some of the steps they’re taking feel a bit forced or rushed. It's not easy finding that balance between safety and entertainment in this climate."
Coach Vaughn: That's true. Lastly, what message do you have for your followers and listeners during these challenging times?

"Stay strong! It’s okay to feel overwhelmed sometimes, but remember the little things that make life worth living. Wear masks, social distance, stay home if you can, and be responsible to yourself and those around you. Most importantly, spread love and positivity wherever you go."
Coach Vaughn: Thank you for sharing your thoughts and experiences with us today, VondeeCarlo. It's been a pleasure having you on the show.
"Thank you for having me! It was great talking to you, Coach Vaughn."

title: 4 Key Ingredients for Godly Romance in Your Marriage
summary: In this podcast episode, the hosts discuss four key ingredients to maintain romance and love in a marriage. These include meeting unspoken needs or desires, speaking your spouse's love language, communicating unique value, and empathizing with each other.

main_points.point: Meeting an unspoken need or desire in your spouse
main_points.details: This involves understanding and fulfilling hidden expectations that your partner may have. It can be something as simple as making time for them or doing a specific task they value, but it must come from genuine care rather than expectation of reciprocation.

main_points.point: Speaking your spouse's love language
main_points.details: This concept is based on Gary Chapman’s theory that everyone has a preferred way of expressing and receiving love. The love languages include acts of service, words of affirmation, quality time, gifts, and physical touch. Identifying and using your partner's primary love language can strengthen the bond between you.

main_points.point: Communicating unique value
main_points.details: Expressing appreciation for who your spouse is as an individual rather than just what they do or bring to the relationship. This involves actively listening, recognizing their strengths and contributions, and validating them in front of others.

main_points.point: Empathizing with your spouse
main_points.details: This means putting yourself in your partner's shoes and understanding their perspective. It involves acknowledging their emotions and being sensitive to how actions or words might affect them emotionally. Empathy helps resolve conflicts by fostering mutual understanding and support.

conclusion: Maintaining romance and love in a marriage requires intentional effort from both partners. By focusing on these four key ingredients—meeting unspoken needs, speaking the right love language, communicating unique value, and empathizing—you can nurture a strong, loving relationship that thrives over time.

transcript.text: Before we dive in, could you tell our listeners a bit about your background and how you got into yoga?

transcript.text: Absolutely. Your mission is so important and needed in today's world. Can you tell us more about your approach to teaching yoga?

transcript.text: That's wonderful. We've heard a lot about the concept of 'fat shaming'—how do you handle that issue within your yoga practice?

question.text: What are Louis Martin's preferences for the next season's kits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Louis Martin expressed a preference for a retro-style home kit with either red or blue as dominant colors, along with white shorts and socks. For the away kit, he suggested Dennis and Menex or Greenham white hoops as options.

Show Notes.Description: Alex explains what makes entrepreneurs unique and how they navigate the world differently than others. He discusses their strengths, challenges, and the common traits that unite them.

Alex elaborates on his concept of the contribution equation, which he claims is the key to unlocking entrepreneurial success. He breaks down the equation into three parts: lowering pressure and noise, increasing protection and support, and allowing strengths and abilities to show.

Show Notes.Topic: Money as a Measure of Contribution
Show Notes.Description: Alex emphasizes that money flows to contribution, meaning those who create significant value for others are more likely to succeed financially. He argues that making a fortune proves one has made the necessary contribution.

Alex provides actionable steps and advice for entrepreneurs based on the contribution equation, including lowering pressure and noise, seeking support and protection, and focusing on what they're best at to make their greatest contribution.
