You're listening to the True Wealth Investors Podcast, where we focus on helping real estate investors build their wealth and achieve financial freedom. I'm your host, Brandon Cornett.

In today's episode, we have a special guest joining us: Brandon Ingram. Brandon is an Ohio-based real estate investor who has taken his financial journey to the next level in just three years. He's built up a six-figure income from real estate and now aims to reach the one million dollar mark by age 30. Let's dive into this interview!

Host: Welcome to the True Wealth Investors Podcast, Brandon! Can you tell us a bit about yourself and your journey in real estate investing?

Brandon Ingram: Thanks for having me on, Brandon! I've always been interested in real estate. In law enforcement, I would see it used as an investment tool to get people out of neighborhoods that weren't safe. But when my wife and I became pregnant with our third child, we started looking at how we could build a six-figure income from passive investments. That's where real estate came into play for us.

Host: That was a great trigger moment. How did you get your start in real estate?

Brandon Ingram: We started with some small flips, and then we transitioned to wholesaling. After that, we moved into rental properties. That's when things really took off for us. We now own 23 multifamily properties and three single family homes in Dayton, Ohio.

Host: That's quite a jump from just flipping houses! How do you manage such a diverse real estate portfolio?

Brandon Ingram: It requires a lot of attention and dedication. We have a team that helps us with the day-to-day operations, but we also bring in experts for tax, accounting, and legal advice when needed.

Host: Speaking of managing a team, you mentioned bringing on experts early on. Can you share any tips for small business owners or entrepreneurs who are just starting out?

Brandon Ingram: Absolutely! One key tip is to have a strong 'why.' What's your ultimate goal? If it's about lifestyle, then going solo might work. But if you're after impact and making more significant changes, then bring on people who can help scale the business.

Host: That makes sense. How do you handle bookkeeping and tax issues when running a real estate portfolio?

Brandon Ingram: We have an accountant who helps us with that, which is crucial for staying organized and avoiding any potential audits or legal troubles.

Host: Great advice. What's the biggest lesson you've learned from your journey in real estate investing?

Brandon Ingram: The most important lesson is that it takes a lot of work, but once you have the right team and community around you, building wealth through real estate can be very rewarding. And the lifestyle benefits—being able to spend time with family and being your own boss—are priceless.

Host: That's absolutely true. Finally, what's next for Brandon Ingram and his team?

Brandon Ingram: We're focused on growing our business, but also making a positive impact in the community. Specifically, we want to see more people own their homes through programs like the Neighborhood Homeowner Program. This not only benefits individuals but helps stabilize neighborhoods.

Host: That's a fantastic goal! Thanks for sharing your journey and insights with us today, Brandon!

Brandon Ingram: Thank you for having me, Brandon. It was great talking to you!

Host: For more information on Brandon's insurance agency, visit insuredbyingram.com. Be sure to check out his YouTube channel for more tips and strategies.

That wraps up today's episode. If you enjoyed this conversation with Brandon Ingram, please leave us a review on Apple Podcasts or Spotify. And don't forget to subscribe so you never miss an episode!

Thanks for listening to the True Wealth Investors Podcast! Until next time, keep investing and building your wealth.

title: Trawcast Episode 75: Interview with Christopher Brown of Stillborn Condition
transcript:
Sean Matthews (Host): Welcome to Trawcast, the show where we bring in a guest and we talk about music, writing, and anything else interesting. I'm Sean Matthews.

Seth Matthews (Guest Host): And I'm Seth Matthews. Joining us today is Christopher Brown from Stillborn Condition. Chris, welcome to the show!

Christopher Brown: Thank you for having me, man. It's been a pleasure.

Sean Matthews: So, let's dive right in. Tell us about your band and what kind of music you play.

Christopher Brown: Sure thing! Well, Stillborn Condition is an old-school death metal outfit from Ohio. We've got a new album out called 'God Eater,' which came out on the 30th of October this year. It's our second full-length release, and we're really proud of it. The style is classic death metal with some thrash influence here and there.

Seth Matthews: That sounds awesome. And I know you have a podcast as well. Can you tell us about that?

Christopher Brown: Absolutely! The podcast is called 'I Fucking Knew It,' and we talk about psychic mediumship, paranormal activity, and more. We also do some lighter stuff like pop culture references and comedy.

Sean Matthews: That's great. And we have links to both the band and the podcast in our notes section, so listeners can check those out if they're interested.

Seth Matthews: So, you've got a new album coming out soon. Can you tell us more about it?

Christopher Brown: Yeah, definitely! 'God Eater' is an 11-song death metal album that's pretty intense and dark. The themes are about the death of the gods and the end of times. We tried to capture the essence of classic old-school death metal with a bit of modern production.

Seth Matthews: That sounds like it will be a great listen. And you're also doing some house projects right now, correct?

Christopher Brown: Yeah, I've been working on some landscaping and building steps around my property to make things more functional and aesthetically pleasing.

Sean Matthews: Nice! So, let's talk about the paranormal aspect of your podcast. Do you believe in psychic abilities yourself?

Christopher Brown: Personally, I don't have any extraordinary powers or anything like that. However, I do find it fascinating to explore these topics with guests and audiences who might be more inclined to believe in them.

Seth Matthews: That's interesting. And do you think the podcast has influenced your approach as a musician or medium?

Christopher Brown: It has, actually. The experience of talking about paranormal phenomena can sometimes inspire me creatively when writing lyrics for our songs. I find that blending the supernatural with metal can create a unique and compelling atmosphere.

Sean Matthews: That's great to hear. Is there anything else you'd like to share with our listeners today?

Christopher Brown: Just that 'God Eater' is out now, so feel free to check it out if you're into death metal or just looking for some intense music. And don't hesitate to reach out through my social media or the podcast site for more information.

Seth Matthews: Thank you again, Chris, for joining us today and sharing your music and insights with our audience. It was great talking to you!

Christopher Brown: Thanks for having me, guys. Take care!

Summary: This video provides a detailed history and analysis of Honda's CR250R motorcycle from its inception to its eventual retirement in 2007. The CR250R played a significant role in the development and popularization of motocross, having first appeared on the market in 1984. It underwent several design changes over the years but faced challenges with its case-read engine, which struggled to match the performance of competitors' two-stroke motors. Despite these issues, the CR250R remained a favorite among enthusiasts for its handling and suspension quality. The video concludes by discussing the broader context of two-stroke motorcycle development in the late 20th and early 21st centuries, including industry trends towards four-strokes due to environmental concerns and changing consumer preferences.

title: 1998 Yamaha YZ400F: The Machine That Transformed Motocross
author: Tony Blaser

content.text: The 1998 Yamaha YZ400F marked a pivotal moment in motocross history, transforming the perception of four-strokes from niche cult machines to mainstream performers. This article delves into its development, performance, and impact on the sport.

In 1998, Yamaha unveiled the YZ400F as part of their response to the four-stroke revolution in motocross. The bike was a leap forward from previous Japanese four-strokes and featured innovative technologies such as the FCR throttle body and a sophisticated decompression system.

The YZ400F boasted impressive handling, power delivery, and reliability. Its 400cc single-cylinder engine provided smooth, powerful acceleration and excellent traction thanks to its prodigious weight. The bike's plush suspension worked well on small terrain but struggled with larger obstacles.

The YZ400F's introduction forced other manufacturers like Kawasaki and Honda to accelerate their four-stroke development programs, leading to a significant shift in motocross technology by the early 2000s. The YZ400F remains an iconic symbol of this era.

Despite some initial criticisms, the YZ400F is now recognized as a groundbreaking machine that paved the way for modern motocross four-strokes. Its influence can still be seen in contemporary four-stroke designs.

The 1998 Yamaha YZ400F was not without its flaws, but it undeniably changed the landscape of motocross by making four-strokes more accessible and performant. Its legacy is a testament to innovation in motorcycle design.

/Director: David Zucker, Jim Abrahams, Jerry Zucker
/Cast: John Vernon (Joe Grotowski), Jennifer Jason Leigh (Lily), Robert Vaughn (Don Ho), John Ratzenberger (Ralph), Tom Kane (Rodney), Bob Holt (Vlad Bianco)
/Plot Summary: The film follows Joe Grotowski, a middle-aged man who is unemployed and living in an abandoned lot. He befriends a group of talking roaches that help him build a garden on the vacant land. The roaches eventually inspire Lily, a young woman, to start planting community gardens around her neighborhood, much to the displeasure of Don Ho, a local developer who wants to build a prison on the lot. Don Ho and his associates threaten violence against Joe, but the roaches protect him, leading to a series of comedic confrontations. In the end, Lily falls in love with Joe, but he is still living in her apartment with the help of the roaches.
/Conclusion: The movie 'Parasite' (1982) was enjoyable and nostalgic for its creators due to it being a film from their childhood that their father enjoyed. However, the ending feels somewhat unsatisfying as Joe continues to live in Lily's apartment with the help of the roaches, which is seen as an appropriate metaphor for parasitism. The movie features a mix of stop-motion animation and live-action elements, resulting in a unique visual style.

Title: Morning in the Mountains - Frank & Kira Show (Alcatraz East) [Transcript]
Summary: This is a transcript of the Morning in the Mountains show featuring Frank and Kira discussing Alcatraz East. The segment covers various topics including the reopening of attractions, credit card usage, social media, and a brief mention of true crime fans.
Key Points: Alcatraz East is back open for business after a shutdown due to the pandemic.
Credit card usage at attractions has been discussed, with plans for future implementation.
Social media platforms like Twitter and Facebook are encouraged as ways to share the show.
True crime fans were mentioned, with one host noting that true crime enthusiasts might not be on social media.
Transcript: {Introduction and welcome}
Frank: You're listening to Morning in the Mountains. I'm Frank, and this is our co-host Kira.

Kira: Good morning, everyone. Welcome back to the Frank and Kira show on Mountain Fun Life. Today we have a very interesting guest with us who will be discussing an attraction that's finally reopened for business after the shutdown. So welcome to the show, Brian Holland.
Brian: Thank you so much for having me, Frank and Kira. I'm really excited to chat about Alcatraz East.
Frank: Absolutely. Alcatraz East is one of those attractions we've missed during this pandemic time. Can you give us a brief overview of what it is?

Brian: Of course. Alcatraz East is an attraction based on the famous prison, Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay. It's not just about the prison; there are interactive exhibits that transport visitors back to the 1930s when the federal penitentiary operated.
Kira: That sounds fascinating! So, what have you been doing since its reopening?

Brian: Well, we've implemented several new safety protocols such as contactless ticketing and frequent sanitization. We're also encouraging the use of credit cards for purchases to minimize physical touch points.
Frank: Credit card usage seems like a smart step during these times. Have you noticed an increase in visitors using that method?

Brian: Yes, definitely. People are becoming more comfortable with digital payments as well. It’s convenient and it helps reduce the risk of transmission. We're also exploring other technologies to make our visitation process smoother.

Kira: That's great to hear. Moving on to a lighter topic, we've noticed you have some unique methods of communication. For instance, your flip phone. Is that something you prefer or is it due to personal reasons?
Frank: It’s more about personal preference, Kira. Dr. Bass and I still use our old flip phones because we don’t want too much contact with the digital world.

Kira: That's interesting. You know, in this day and age, social media is almost essential for any business or attraction. Do you think true crime fans like yourself could be hesitant to embrace all these new technologies?

Brian: Absolutely. True crime enthusiasts might prefer a more traditional approach. They might not want as much contact with the digital world, preferring instead to have a flip phone and perhaps an old-school way of communication.
Frank: That's fair. But I guess it’s about finding what works best for each individual. Thank you so much for sharing your insights with us today, Brian.
Brian: You're very welcome. It was great talking to both of you. And thanks for all the support from your fans. Keep up the good work!
{Conclusion and outro}

Host: This is the Daily Diddy and we are talking about some heavy topics today. Let's get into it.

First, let's talk about the Black Lives Matter movement and how it has impacted Long Beach. How do you think the city of Long Beach has responded to this movement?

Guest 1 (Sue Bird): I think there have been a lot of positive changes in terms of the dialogue around race and equity. However, there is still much work to be done.

Host: What are some of those specific steps that need to be taken?

Guest 2 (PPG Monty): We need to address systemic issues like housing and education disparities. Additionally, it's important for local businesses and organizations to invest in underrepresented communities.

Host: Speaking of Long Beach, how do you think the city has changed over the years? 

Guest 1: There has been progress, but there is still a lot of work to be done with regards to addressing homelessness and social issues. Some neighborhoods have undergone gentrification which can sometimes push out long-term residents.

Host: How does Long Beach compare to other cities in terms of its representation of artists from the streets? 

Guest 2: I think there are definitely parallels between Long Beach and other cities, but each city has its unique challenges. Long Beach is known for its diversity and rich musical history, which often gets overshadowed by bigger cities like Los Angeles.

Host: Can you give an example of how Long Beach's history and culture have influenced the city's artistic community? 

Guest 1: Long Beach has a vibrant music scene with artists like MC Eiht and Murs who came up in the local underground. Their success has helped to showcase the talent from the streets on a larger scale.

Host: How do you think the current political climate affects the way artists are portrayed or represented? 

Guest 2: The current administration's rhetoric can sometimes alienate certain groups, which can impact how they're perceived and supported by the community. However, it also provides opportunities for artists to advocate for change through their work.

Host: What advice do you have for aspiring artists in Long Beach who are looking to make a name for themselves? 

Guest 1: Stay true to your roots and continue to create high-quality work that resonates with your community. Networking within the local scene can also be beneficial.

Host: Lastly, what's next on your respective projects?

Guest 2: I'm currently working on a new project that explores themes of identity and social justice. It will feature collaborations with both local and national artists.

Guest 1: I have some tracks coming out soon that focus on personal experiences and reflections. We'll keep you updated!

Title: Interview with Ross Murray - A World Class Athlete
Description: In today's podcast, we have the pleasure of speaking to Ross Murray, a world-class athlete who has achieved significant success in long-distance running. He shares his insights and advice on training for endurance events such as marathons. From understanding the importance of listening to your body, to the value of consistent training, Ross provides practical tips for anyone looking to take their fitness journey to the next level. Plus, he offers valuable wisdom on how to maintain focus and set goals that can drive personal growth.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: You're listening to Body Power Mind with your host, Adam Robinson. Today, we have an incredible guest who has achieved world-class success in long-distance running - Ross Murray!

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: So, Ross, thank you for joining us today. Can you tell our audience a little bit about yourself and your background in the sport of long-distance running?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: Of course, Adam. I've been involved with long-distance running since 2013 when I was diagnosed with a heart condition that limited my physical activity. The doctor encouraged me to take up an alternative form of exercise and running became the perfect fit.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: That's fascinating! And how did you transition from amateur to professional runner?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: I took a leap of faith, enrolled in a local running club, and started to participate in races. As my performance improved, I began taking part in larger events and eventually secured sponsorship opportunities that allowed me to focus on training and competing at the professional level.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: That's amazing! In your experience, what do you think are the most important factors for someone starting out in long-distance running?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: First and foremost, it's crucial to listen to your body. Building a solid base through consistent training is key, but it's also essential to recognize when rest and recovery are necessary.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: Absolutely! How do you stay motivated to keep pushing yourself during challenging times?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: Setting clear goals helps a lot. Whether it's qualifying for the Olympics or running your first marathon, having something specific to work towards gives me the drive and focus I need to persevere.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: That makes sense. Can you share any practical tips for someone looking to start training for endurance events like marathons?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: Start small, increase gradually, and don't forget to incorporate strength training and cross-training into your routine. Flexibility and core stability are also vital for injury prevention.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: That's great advice. Are there any common mistakes runners make that you've seen throughout your career?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: Overtraining is a big one - listening to the signs of fatigue and allowing sufficient recovery time can prevent burnout and injury.

Transcript.Speaker: Host
Transcript.Text: Thank you for sharing those insights. As we wrap up, could you tell our listeners about your upcoming plans and any advice you have for them moving forward?

Transcript.Speaker: Ross Murray
Transcript.Text: Currently, I'm focusing on qualifying for the Tokyo Olympics next summer. For anyone looking to take their fitness journey further, invest in yourself by setting realistic goals and making a commitment to consistent training.

   - Jesus commands His disciples to keep His commandments if they love Him, promising the Comforter (Holy Spirit) would assist them in doing so.

   - Jesus affirms that He will return to the Father but will send the Holy Spirit to remain with His disciples. He also reminds them of His upcoming crucifixion, resurrection, and ascension, emphasizing His commitment to fulfilling God's will.
3. **Key Themes**: Love for Christ, obedience to His commandments, the role of the Holy Spirit in guiding believers, and the certainty of Jesus' return despite current challenges.
application: The study encourages listeners to embrace humility and reverence towards God, seek wisdom by fearing Him, and live out love through obedience to Christ's commands. It also highlights the importance of relying on the Holy Spirit for guidance and peace in challenging times.

title: Developing Creativity and Human Skills in Children with Stephen Hallam
description: In this episode, we talk to Stephen Hallam about the importance of creativity and human skills development. He explains how machines will replace most algorithmic tasks, leaving humans with a unique advantage in creativity and communication. We discuss his app that aims to teach children how to ask questions and think critically.

introduction.speaker: host
introduction.text: Hi everyone! Welcome back to the Ed Futurist podcast.

guest_interview.speaker: host
guest_interview.text: Today, we're talking about developing creativity and human skills in children. Joining us is Stephen Hallam from the 'What Ifs' app.

guest_interview.speaker: Stephen Hallam
guest_interview.text: Hello, thanks for having me! It's great to be here.

guest_interview.speaker: host
guest_interview.text: So, Steve, can you tell us a bit about your work with the 'What Ifs' app?

guest_interview.speaker: Stephen Hallam
guest_interview.text: Certainly. The 'What Ifs' app is designed to help children and adults develop their critical thinking skills by encouraging them to ask more questions and explore different scenarios.

guest_interview.speaker: host
guest_interview.text: That sounds really interesting! Can you give us an example of how the app works?

guest_interview.speaker: Stephen Hallam
guest_interview.text: Sure, for instance, one question might be 'How could we use a fire to solve a problem?' This is not necessarily an ethical question, but it helps develop their ability to think creatively and critically.

key_points.speaker: host
key_points.text: Steve, you mentioned that as machines do more for us, the human ability to be creative will arguably become our single biggest strength. Can you elaborate on this idea?

key_points.speaker: Stephen Hallam
key_points.text: Absolutely! As technology advances and machines take over repetitive tasks, humans will need to rely more on their creativity and ability to think outside the box to differentiate themselves.

questions.speaker: host
questions.text: Moving on to parents who want to use this app with their children. How do they go about doing it successfully?

questions.speaker: Stephen Hallam
questions.text: Parents can download the app, open a question and encourage their children to think deeply about different scenarios. The prompts provided in the app are there to support them if needed.

conclusion.speaker: host
conclusion.text: Thanks so much for your time today, Steve! We really appreciate you sharing this with us.

conclusion.speaker: Stephen Hallam
conclusion.text: Thank you very much. It was great talking to you!

title: Normalizing Conversations with Maria Fawzia Ahmed
summary: In this episode of the Dope Muslim Woman podcast, host Dr. Khoroush chats with author and founder of Buddy Speaks, Maria Fawzia Ahmed, about her children's book that aims to make conversations around sexual abuse normal and fun for kids. Maria discusses why it’s important to talk to kids about these topics early on and shares insights on the challenges she faced in creating this groundbreaking work.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: Welcome back, Dope Muslim Women! Today, we have an amazing guest with us. Maria Fawzia Ahmed is joining us from Atlanta, Georgia to discuss her children's book called Buddy Speaks. Maria, thank you so much for being here.

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: Thank you so much for having me! I'm excited to be here and share this important work with everyone.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: Before we dive in, can you tell us a little bit about yourself and why you decided to write Buddy Speaks?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: Sure! I'm an author and educator who has dedicated my life to working with children, especially those facing trauma. My goal is to make conversations around sexual abuse normal and fun for kids. Buddy Speaks was born out of the need to address this topic in a way that's accessible and engaging for young children.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: That’s wonderful! Can you walk us through the process of creating Buddy Speaks? What challenges did you face along the way?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: Absolutely! One of the biggest challenges was making sure that the book wasn't just another dry, boring text. I wanted it to be something kids would actually enjoy reading. Another challenge was ensuring that the language and concepts were appropriate for their age group without oversimplifying or trivializing the topic.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: How did you ensure that Buddy Speaks was not only fun but also educational?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: I worked closely with child psychologists and educators to make sure that the book provided accurate information while still being engaging. I also incorporated colorful illustrations and relatable scenarios to help kids understand complex concepts in a simple way.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: That's amazing! Can you share some key messages or lessons from Buddy Speaks that parents and educators should know?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: Of course! One of the main messages is that it's okay to talk about private parts, and that children have the right to say no if someone makes them feel uncomfortable. The book also emphasizes the importance of trust and seeking help from trusted adults when needed.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: How do you hope Buddy Speaks will impact the Muslim community?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: I hope it encourages open, honest conversations about sensitive topics within our communities. By normalizing these discussions, we can empower children and create a safer environment for everyone.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: Absolutely! So, how can people support Buddy Speaks?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: People can purchase the book directly from my website or through Amazon. Additionally, spreading the word and sharing the importance of this conversation on social media is also very helpful.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: That’s great advice! Where can people find you online?

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: You can visit my website at www.buddyspeaks.com, or follow me on Instagram and Facebook @buddy_underscorespeaks. I'd love to connect with you there.

content.speaker: Host
content.text: Thank you so much for sharing your insights and the importance of Buddy Speaks with us today. It's been a pleasure having you, Maria!

content.speaker: Maria
content.text: Thank you for having me! I appreciate the opportunity to speak about this important topic.

title: Fin Settings Optimization for Ski Tuning
summary: The discussion revolves around optimizing fin settings on water ski bindings, focusing on key measurements like leading edge (LE), depth from tail (DFT), and fin surface area. The experts emphasize the importance of understanding how these factors interrelate and how they can be adjusted to suit individual skiers based on their weight, technique, and personal preferences.
key_points: Leading Edge (LE) is a critical measurement that indicates where the fins start from in relation to the ski's binding. It influences balance and turn radius.
Depth from Tail (DFT) determines how far back the fin starts on the ski, impacting width control and turning performance.
Fin Surface Area combines length and depth measurements, crucial for tail hold and leverage. Adjusting this area can significantly affect the skier's ability to maintain balance and maneuverability.
For heavier skiers, it is recommended to move boots forward to utilize more of the wider part of the ski’s tail for support.
Lighter skiers generally require less depth in their fin settings because they have an easier time rolling over due to lower edge pressure.
Balancing these factors (LE, DFT, and surface area) allows skiers to find a setting that provides optimal feedback and performance based on personal preferences and physical attributes.
quotes: Fin Surface Area is not the mathematical approach, but it seems to have worked over time. So I just stick with it.
You are going to be able to be stronger behind the boat, but you also are going to have a harder time turning now that we did that.
speaker_notes: This conversation provides valuable insights for water skiers looking to optimize their fin settings. It highlights the importance of individualized adjustments based on weight and technique.
The emphasis on surface area as a balance factor is particularly useful, as it ties together length and depth in a practical way.

summary: This week on Finding Our Tribe, Joey and Fabian discuss various teaching-related topics such as student engagement, interactive lessons, and the importance of relationships. They also share their experiences with virtual classrooms and reflect on the challenges teachers face during the school year.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Hey, hey there are you Fabian?

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: I'm here. I'm ready to talk about teaching.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, good. I think this is a great time to be talking about teaching because we're at the end of the school year, and so we have some thoughts on what we've learned, what's been important, and how to kind of get back into it next year.

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Yeah, I think that's a really good idea. I mean, we're all looking for a little bit of inspiration before summer starts and also like some perspective on the teaching in general because teaching is hard work. But it can be really rewarding.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. And so what have you learned this year? I mean, we've been kind of focused on the numbers and percentages. You know like how many percent of your students are engaged in virtual classrooms or whatever, but it's not just about that.

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. It's all about the relationships you build with your kids. And if they don't feel comfortable talking to you, then it doesn't matter how much technology you throw at them because they're not going to participate in any way.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. And so what are some of the things that you've done this year to try and build those relationships?

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Well, we tried a lot of different things like peer editing, which is something I haven't done before. And it's been really interesting because I have to go on camera for that. But uh, you know, it makes me feel uncomfortable because I don't want to look silly.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. It's like a lot of teachers just don't even go on video in these meetings and stuff. And so what do you think is the best way to get them more comfortable with it? Like how can we build those relationships?

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Well, I think it's all about being genuine and showing your students that you care about them. You know, like if you're in a virtual classroom and they start talking, you should respond to their comments. And maybe even share something personal with them.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. And so what are some of the other things that you've done this year to try and engage your students?

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Well, we've tried a lot of different things like flocabulary, which is really good for teaching vocabulary. But uh, you know, I'm trying to think about how I can integrate all these cool live webcams that Fabian got during his field trip with the writing lessons.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. And so what are some of your thoughts on ending the year? Like do you have any plans for signing yearbooks or leaving notes for your students?

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Well, I bought a yearbook because I just think it's going to be my first year and I want to look back at this year as like that year that you met me. And so yeah, I'm definitely going to sign the yearbook.

transcript.speaker: Joey
transcript.text: Yeah, exactly. And so how can we help other teachers feel less alone during the school year? Like what are some of your thoughts on that?

transcript.speaker: Fabian
transcript.text: Well, I think it's all about finding a community. You know, like if you have friends who are also teachers or people in your department, then you can reach out to them and share your struggles and your successes.

title: Chief Seeds Podcast - Episode 126: Major League Baseball Scout Darrell Milney | Player Development, Minor League Impact of Coronavirus
transcript:
Darrell Milney is a long time Major League Baseball scout and former coach. He spent years working with the San Diego Padres, Boston Red Sox and Philadelphia Phillies. Darrell shares his experiences in player development as well as his insights on how the coronavirus will affect minor league baseball and college baseball.

In this episode of the Chief Seeds Podcast, we talk to Darrell about:

- His time as a scout for the San Diego Padres, Boston Red Sox, and Philadelphia Phillies 
- The importance of command in fastball development 
- The shift towards analytics and statistics in baseball 
- How the coronavirus pandemic will affect the 2020 MLB draft 
- The potential impact on independent leagues and minor league teams 

We hope you enjoy this episode and if you have any questions or comments, please reach out to us at ChiefSeedsPodcast@gmail.com.

[Music]

Host: Welcome back to the Chief Seeds Podcast. I’m your host, [Your Name], and today we’re joined by a long-time Major League Baseball scout and former coach named Darrell Milney. Darrell spent years working with the San Diego Padres, Boston Red Sox, and Philadelphia Phillies, and he shares his experiences in player development as well as his insights on how the coronavirus will affect minor league baseball and college baseball.

Darrell, welcome to the Chief Seeds Podcast!

Darrell: Thank you for having me. I’m excited to be here with you today.

Host: So let’s start by talking about your time as a scout. What was it like working for the San Diego Padres, Boston Red Sox, and Philadelphia Phillies?

Darrell: It was an incredible experience. As a scout, my job was to travel around the country and evaluate players at different levels of baseball. I would attend high school games, college games, summer leagues, and try to identify talent that could eventually make it to the major leagues. Each organization had its own unique approach to scouting, but all of them shared a passion for discovering new players who could contribute to their team.

Host: And how did you go about evaluating players? What were some key factors you considered when making your assessments?

Darrell: There are many things I looked at when evaluating players. One of the most important was their physical tools, such as velocity, arm strength, and bat speed. But I also took into account their makeup, including their work ethic, mental toughness, and attitude. It’s important to remember that a player’s skills can improve with training, but their character is something that cannot be coached.

Host: Speaking of which, you’ve mentioned the importance of command in fastball development. Can you elaborate on this?

Darrell: Absolutely! A player who has command of his fastball can throw strikes consistently and keep hitters off balance. This is especially important for pitchers, as it allows them to mix in other pitches and keep batters guessing. In contrast, a pitcher who cannot command his fastball will struggle to make contact with the strike zone and be less effective on the mound.

Host: That’s really interesting. How did you go about developing a player’s command?

Darrell: It starts with basic mechanics. A pitcher needs to have proper arm action, release point, and follow through in order to throw strikes consistently. From there, we would work on things like grip variations and pitch sequences to help players develop different types of fastballs.

Host: And how did the shift towards analytics and statistics impact your role as a scout?

Darrell: The rise of sabermetrics has changed the way teams approach scouting and player development. While I still place a lot of importance on traditional scouting techniques, data analysis can provide valuable insights that might not be immediately apparent to the human eye. For example, we could use pitch tracking data to see which pitches were most effective against certain hitters or how often players were able to throw their secondary pitches for strikes.

Host: Finally, let’s talk about the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on minor league baseball and college baseball. With the 2020 MLB draft being cut down to five rounds, what do you think this will mean for these levels of the game?

Darrell: The reduction in the number of rounds in the MLB draft is going to have a significant impact on both professional and collegiate baseball. For minor league teams, it means fewer players will be drafted overall, which could lead to budget cuts or even the elimination of some teams. At the same time, college seniors who were counting on playing their final year won’t get that opportunity, and incoming freshmen may find themselves competing for roster spots earlier than expected.

Host: That’s definitely a tough situation for many players and teams. Do you see any silver linings in this situation?

Darrell: While it’s unfortunate to see these changes happen, there are some potential positives. For example, the reduced number of rounds could make the draft process more streamlined and efficient. Additionally, if players do end up playing independently or for minor league teams, they may gain valuable experience that could help them in future seasons.

Host: Thank you so much for joining us today, Darrell. It was great talking to you about your experiences as a scout and coach.

Darrell: Thanks for having me! I enjoyed the conversation and look forward to staying connected with Chief Seeds Podcast.
summary: In this episode, Darrell Milney shares his experiences as a Major League Baseball scout and coach for the San Diego Padres, Boston Red Sox, and Philadelphia Phillies. He discusses the importance of command in fastball development and how analytics have impacted scouting techniques. Darrell also provides insights on how the coronavirus pandemic will affect minor league baseball and college baseball due to the shortened 2020 MLB draft.

title: Interview with Lindsey Elmore - Integrative Functional Medicine and Authentic Living
transcript: Host: Welcome to the Kill Candida Podcast. I'm your host, Lori Cieley. Today's episode is all about integrative functional medicine and living authentically with my guest Lindsey Elmore. We're going to dive into how she uses these principles in her own life and as a functional nutritionist.
Host: Thanks for joining me, Lindsey. Can you tell us a little bit about your background and what led you to become a functional nutritionist?

Guest: Thank you, Lori. I'm a functional nutritionist, but really, my background is in the arts. I studied painting and photography at school, which initially didn't seem like it would have anything to do with health and wellness. But after experiencing some struggles with Lyme disease and chronic fatigue syndrome, I decided to make a drastic change and study integrative medicine.
Host: That's interesting. Can you explain what functional nutrition is and how it differs from conventional nutrition?

Guest: Sure! Functional nutrition focuses on the relationship between food and our bodies at the cellular level, rather than just counting calories or focusing on isolated nutrients. It looks at the underlying causes of health issues and addresses imbalances in the body to support overall wellness.
Host: That makes a lot of sense. How do you integrate functional medicine into your work as a nutritionist?

Guest: I use my background in both art and science, blending creative visualization techniques with evidence-based approaches to help clients identify their unique health needs and create personalized plans. I also focus on lifestyle factors like stress management and sleep quality.
Host: That's fascinating. You mentioned Lyme disease earlier. Can you share your personal experience with this condition?

Guest: Absolutely. After a diagnosis of Lyme, my body went through some major changes. It was really difficult to find effective treatments, but eventually I discovered functional medicine and it helped me regain control over my health.

Host: That's amazing that you found success in functional medicine. You mentioned earlier that you've been studying functional medicine for about two years now. Can you tell us more about your studies?
Guest: Yes, I'm currently enrolled in the School of Applied Functional Medicine and focusing on a personalized approach to health and wellness.
Host: That's great! You also spoke about the importance of being authentic. Can you explain what that means in the context of living with chronic illness or conditions like Candida?

Guest: Being authentic is about embracing your true self without apology. It involves recognizing your unique needs and values, and making health choices based on who you are rather than societal expectations.
Host: That's a powerful perspective. Do you have any tips for listeners who may be struggling with authenticity in their own lives?
Guest: Absolutely! One tip is to practice self-compassion and recognize that everyone has unique challenges. Another is to surround yourself with supportive people who accept you for who you are.
Host: Thank you, Lindsey. Your insights have been incredibly valuable. Where can our listeners find more information about your work?

Guest: They can visit my website at LindseyElmore.com or check out the free tools section on there. I also have a book called 'The Empowered Choice' that might be helpful for those struggling with authenticity in their health and wellness journey.
Host: Excellent, thank you so much for sharing your knowledge with us today, Lindsey.

summary: Congressman Rick Allen discusses the CARES Act and its impact on local businesses, addressing questions about the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL), unemployment benefits, and essential business status. He provides insights into applying for loans, managing payroll, and seeking financial advice during these unprecedented times.

key_points.Congressman's Role: Represents the 31st District of Georgia in Congress and is handling legislation related to the CARES Act.
key_points.PPP Loan Details: 25% of PPP funds can go towards non-payroll expenses such as rent, utilities, or mortgage interest. Up to 75% must be spent on payroll.
key_points.EIDL Application Process: Visit SBA.gov for EIDL loans; application process involves proving business necessity and potential impact of loan.
key_points.Unemployment Benefits: Eligibility varies by state but generally includes self-employed individuals and sole proprietors. Benefits can range from $300 to $600 per week.
key_points.SBA Support: Team up with SBA for PPP and EIDL applications; SBA also provides loan forgiveness for up to 6 months.
key_points.Next Steps: Contact financial advisors, tax professionals, or Congressman Allen's office for further guidance.

content.title: The Faithful Soldier - Hideo Onoda
content.text:
Let’s talk about a soldier named Hideo Onoda. Born in 1922, he was an intelligence officer during World War II stationed on the菲律宾的一个小岛。当战争在1945年8月结束时，他却没有收到撤退的命令。Onoda决定继续执行任务，而这一等就是29年！直到1974年，他的前指挥官亲自前往菲律宾找到他并告知战争已经结束了，他才放下武器投降。

Onoda的故事是关于坚持和忠诚的完美例证。即使在最困难的情况下，他也保持了对使命的坚定信念。

This story is a reminder that we too must remain faithful, even when it’s difficult. When tragedy strikes and we face challenges, it can be tempting to give up or lose faith. But Hideo Onoda didn’t. He kept going, trusting in the mission he believed in.

As Christians, our calling is to stand firm in our faith, regardless of what life throws at us.

Father God, we pray that you would strengthen and encourage your people during these difficult times. Help us not to falter or lose hope when things get tough. Teach us the value of perseverance and faithfulness in all circumstances. In Jesus' name, amen.

title: Conversations with a Health Warrior: A Closer Look at the Pandemic and Beyond
guest_bio: A health warrior who advocates for natural living, holistic healing, and critical thinking. He challenges conventional narratives and encourages individuals to take control of their own health and well-being.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: Today we have a fascinating guest with us, Health Warrior. He's an advocate for natural living, holistic healing, and critical thinking. He challenges conventional narratives and encourages individuals to take control of their own health and well-being.

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: Thanks for having me. It’s great to be here.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: We’ve been discussing a lot lately, especially around the pandemic. You’re quite vocal about your views on it. Can you tell us more about why you think the mainstream narrative is suspect?

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: Absolutely. The mainstream media and government often present information in a way that aligns with their agendas rather than what’s truly best for public health. For example, I’ve come across instances where they downplay natural immunity from things like vitamin D and sunlight while pushing vaccines as the only solution. That’s just one of many examples.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: You mentioned vaccine hesitancy. Can you elaborate on why you’re against mandatory vaccinations?

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: Mandatory vaccination policies can be coercive and undermine personal autonomy. They don’t take into account individual differences in immune responses, allergies, or other health conditions that might make vaccines harmful. Furthermore, the long-term effects of many vaccines are unknown, which is a huge risk for children who may not have the same robust immune systems as adults.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: That’s a compelling argument. You’ve also been critical of certain health and wellness products claiming to support immunity. Can you explain why?

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: Many companies promote their products as miracle cures without providing scientific evidence. They exploit people’s fears during uncertain times, which can be both unethical and dangerous. It’s important for consumers to verify the claims they see with reliable sources.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: That makes sense. You mentioned a divide between those who believe in the official story and alternative theories. How do you think this division is affecting society?

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: It’s creating a polarized environment where people are increasingly divided along political lines rather than sharing common values of health and safety. This divide can lead to conflict and even hostility, which isn’t conducive to finding solutions or maintaining peace.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: You mentioned the importance of critical thinking. Can you share some tips for how people can develop their own informed opinions?

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: Sure! Start by educating yourself from multiple sources, not just mainstream media. Look into peer-reviewed scientific studies and consult experts in various fields. Don’t be afraid to ask questions and challenge the status quo. And most importantly, prioritize your personal well-being.

transcript.speaker: Podcast Host
transcript.text: Those are great tips. For those who want to support your mission or learn more about what you’re doing, where can they find you?

transcript.speaker: Health Warrior
transcript.text: You can follow me on my website at [Website URL], and I also have social media accounts where I regularly share updates and resources. My goal is to empower individuals to take control of their health by providing accurate, evidence-based information.

summary: The podcast episode discusses a myth about basal metabolic rate (BMR) and calorie burn, specifically addressing whether people can eat unlimited amounts of certain foods while maintaining their weight due to higher BMRs. The host debunks this idea by explaining that the body's caloric needs are determined by factors like lean muscle mass, age, gender, and activity level rather than a person's ability to process specific foods. Additionally, the episode touches on the concept of thermic effect of food (TEF) and how it varies for different macronutrients, but overall, the core message is that no single type of food can magically allow one to eat unlimited amounts without consequences. The host also briefly mentions the impact of muscle mass on BMR, emphasizing that weight training is beneficial not just for building muscle but for increasing BMR as well.
key_points: BMR and calorie burn are determined by a combination of factors including lean muscle mass, age, gender, and activity level.
No single type of food allows unlimited consumption without affecting caloric balance; the body still processes all ingested calories.
Thermic effect of food (TEF) exists but its impact on overall calorie intake is minimal compared to total caloric expenditure.
Muscle mass significantly influences BMR, and weight training can help increase it.
Calorie intake should be balanced with activity levels for healthy weight management.

questions_answered.question: Can people who have a higher basal metabolic rate (BMR) eat unlimited amounts of specific foods without gaining weight?
questions_answered.answer: No, the host debunks this myth by explaining that BMR is influenced by factors like muscle mass and activity level. While certain foods may be metabolized differently, no single type of food allows for unlimited consumption without affecting overall caloric balance.

questions_answered.question: What is the thermic effect of food (TEF) and how does it affect calorie burn?
questions_answered.answer: Thermic effect of food refers to the energy used by the body to digest, absorb, transport, store, and use nutrients from consumed foods. While TEF can slightly increase caloric expenditure, its impact is minimal compared to total daily caloric needs.

episodeSummary.description: Jesse discusses how essentialism can help us reground ourselves, by focusing on what truly matters. He shares practical tips for identifying and prioritizing the most important aspects of our lives.

Summary:
This podcast discussion revolves around various experiences and insights gained from participating in online module training for group fitness instructors. The host, Lindsay, leads the conversation with several participants who share their thoughts on pre-module expectations, post-module feedback, and overall experience. Here’s a summary of key points discussed: 

### Pre-Module Expectations
- **Lindsay:** Expected a challenge but found the online format not difficult due to prior experience in webinars.
- **Jordan:** No specific concerns; enjoyed working online.
- **Carcelle:** Faced technical issues with video upload and resolved them by using YouTube links.
- **Terry:** Had mixed feelings but appreciated that feedback was constructive. 

### Module Experience
- **Lindsay:** Found the self-review process helpful, although it felt less immediate compared to face-to-face modules where second-day teaching sessions allow for quicker adjustments.
- **Jordan:** Enjoyed delivering the track despite some nervousness about how students would apply the information.
- **Carcelle:** Nervous initially but felt reassured when seeing others' performances align with taught content.

### Post-Module Feedback and Support
- **Lindsay:** Felt positive about the quality of connection and support provided during the online sessions. 
- **Jordan:** Appreciated that questions in chat boxes were sometimes answered by other participants, enhancing the flow of information.

### Overall Impressions
- **Terry:** Enjoyed the flexibility of online training over face-to-face modules.
- **Carcelle:** Felt it was a good experience overall but acknowledged potential challenges like technical issues and delayed feedback.

### Final Thoughts
- The participants generally felt that while there are some differences, online module training is effective and offers its own unique benefits. Feedback from the group was constructive and helpful.

The podcast concluded with an open invitation for listeners to reach out with any questions or comments via social media handles provided in the show notes.

Episode Title: Pump Up Your Fitness Journey with Fern Big Fern - Social Media, Dating & More
Description: In this episode of Pumped Peach, Fern shares her fitness journey, tips on social media management, and advice for dating. She talks about the importance of staying true to yourself in a competitive industry and how exercise has impacted her life both physically and mentally.

Key Takeaways.Content: Fern discusses her transition from being overweight to working out regularly, which helped boost her confidence and change the way people viewed her. She also mentions that even though she lost weight during high school due to football, it was more about becoming healthier and athletic.

Fern shares insights on how social media has impacted her career as a fitness influencer. She emphasizes the importance of authenticity, staying true to oneself, and building an engaged audience through consistent content and interaction with followers.

Fern discusses how her dating life changed after becoming more fit and confident. She mentions that she looks for partners who share similar interests in health and fitness but emphasizes that it's not necessary to be obsessed with the industry all the time. Working out together can also create a bond between couples.

Fern advises aspiring fitness influencers and gym-goers to focus on what works for them personally rather than trying to follow someone else's path. She recommends staying true to one's goals, being authentic, and finding joy in the process of working out.

To Woman Is No Man.Review: An intimate, matter-of-fact look at the struggles of Japanese women in early 20th century America. The book covers their experiences with immigration, factory work, and field labor, and how they adapted to a new culture while maintaining their own. It is both an important historical document and a powerful exploration of identity and assimilation.

The book challenges the reader to consider the impact of diversity on American culture. Themes include hope for change, the difficulties of assimilation, and the strength found in community.

To Woman Is No Man.Thoughts: The writing style is distinct, making the narrative easy to read despite some confusion with first-person plural perspective. The book provides a unique insight into a largely underrepresented group's experiences.

Introduction: Welcome to the Mill Unloaded podcast. I'm your host, [Host Name], and this is episode 26.
Today we're going to be sharing some insights about our recent self-care quiz results and discussing how they've influenced our approach to work-life balance.
Self-Care Quiz Results: After taking the self-help quiz from loveisrespect.org, I found that out of 60 questions, I only scored 34 right answers.
This highlighted several areas where I can improve in terms of self-care and stress management.
For example, I tend to eat too much, but otherwise, I do show my emotions, spend time with pets or in comfortable spaces, and spend time with people who care about me.
Challenges: I have a significant challenge when it comes to balancing work, family, relationships, and rest.
The start of the pandemic forced me to focus more on my business as people stayed home and couldn't leave for supplies.
While this increased workload was important in the beginning, it has led to overworking at the expense of personal time with my loved ones.
Overworking: I’ve been making so much jam that I’m in constant pain from sitting on a chair or standing up all day.
This has resulted in poor mental health and difficulty spending quality time with family, especially during speech events where I feel extremely fatigued.
Recognizing this imbalance led to the decision to create midweek weekends for myself.
Midweek Break: Starting Wednesdays and Thursdays off from my business is a step towards ensuring that I can rest properly and spend time with family, even if it means cooking easy meals or having smoothies.
The goal is to set boundaries and not be the 'jam and bread lady' all the time.
Setting Boundaries: Another challenge highlighted by the quiz was my tendency to take on too many customer requests that could disrupt my routine.
For instance, a customer's request for rhubarb cobbler was turned down because it wouldn't be practical or profitable in this context.
Daily Practices: To address these challenges and improve self-care, I’m focusing on daily affirmations, taking deep breaths when feeling overwhelmed, and setting better boundaries.
These practices are crucial for maintaining a healthier balance between personal and professional life.
Conclusion: Thank you for joining us today as we explore our journey towards better self-care and work-life balance.
If you’ve taken the quiz yourself or have thoughts on these topics, feel free to reach out via Instagram or email.

title: Robin Murray's Journey from PTSD to Motherhood and Entrepreneurship

transcript.text: John Doe: You're listening to 'The Parenting Podcast,' where we explore the joys, challenges, and everything in between of being a parent. I'm your host John Doe today, and joining me is Robin Murray, a mother, and advocate for veterans and mental health. Welcome to the show, Robin.
Robin Murray: Thank you so much for having me, John. I'm excited to be here.
John Doe: Let's dive right in. Can you tell us a bit about your background and how it led to becoming a mother and advocate for mental health?

Robin Murray: Sure, I served in the military for 15 years before retiring due to combat-related injuries. Unfortunately, during my time serving, I experienced military sexual trauma and was involved in a domestic violence incident that left me severely injured. After being medically retired, I struggled with PTSD and other mental health issues but eventually found solace through martial arts training.
John Doe: That's incredibly inspiring. How did you balance your personal struggles with advocating for others facing similar challenges?

Robin Murray: It was a challenging but rewarding journey. I founded 'Poster Girl' to share my story and help bring awareness to the issues faced by veterans and service members. Being part of organizations like this not only helps others but also provides me with a sense of purpose.
John Doe: Speaking of balancing, how did your journey as a mother differ from what you expected?

Robin Murray: Initially, I thought it would be smooth sailing. However, I quickly realized that parenthood comes with its own set of challenges, especially when dealing with mental health issues like PTSD. But being a mother has also brought immense joy and taught me to embrace imperfections.
John Doe: That's wonderful. Can you tell us more about your business ventures, particularly the jewelry line?

Robin Murray: Absolutely! I started making custom paracord bracelets and other outdoor gear-inspired items as a way to stay creative while balancing my entrepreneurial goals. It's been fulfilling, especially when I see people wearing something that means so much to me.
John Doe: That sounds amazing! Do you have any advice for parents out there who might be struggling with their mental health?

Robin Murray: Absolutely. First, don't be afraid to seek help and support. It's okay to ask for it. Second, remember that you're doing the best you can with what you have. Lastly, cherish every moment because parenthood is a rollercoaster of emotions.
John Doe: Wise words indeed. Thank you so much for sharing your story and inspiring others, Robin. Best of luck with all your endeavors!
Robin Murray: Thank you, John. It's been a pleasure talking to you.

introduction: Host introduces the topic of the episode and mentions the guest, Alex, and his technical knowledge.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What's your favorite game?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: My favorite game is The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. It’s an open world game with a lot to do, so it really keeps me engaged.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Where did you get your Switch from?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I got my Switch at launch, I think it was 2017 or 2018.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What's the most expensive thing you've ever spent on a game?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The most expensive thing I’ve ever spent on a game is probably the Super Rare Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild figurine.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Do you have any favorite board games?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: One of my favorite board games is Mario Party. The game's rules are so complex that they're almost like a mini-game themselves.

questionsAndAnswers.question: If you had to choose between video games and Disney ruling the world, which would you pick?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I think I’d have to go with the video games, as it’s something that has really shaped my life.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Have there been any games that you've had to stop playing due to addiction or just too much time spent on them?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes, there are several games I’ve played way too long in a row because of the game’s addictive algorithms, but one that sticks out is Pokémon GO.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Do you have any favorite games within genres that you normally wouldn’t enjoy?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I’m not typically into sports games, but Madden NFL is an exception. I find it really fun to play and strategize with others in a competitive environment.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Are you planning on getting either the Xbox Series X or PlayStation 5?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No, I have no plans for the PS5 because Second Sun hasn’t come out yet.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Do you think that backward compatibility with the PlayStation 4 will change your decision about whether to get a PlayStation 5?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It's not a little wishful thinking, but I would like to see more games available on it before making any decisions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Would you take a million dollars if you had to stop playing video games?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No, I'd rather keep playing the games that are important to me, even in quarantine.

There are suggestions that the pandemic could lead to increased mental health awareness, expression of feelings, and stronger community support networks. However, there is also recognition of potential negative social judgments and stigmatization based on past behavior during the pandemic.

Title: Back on Track: Getting Back Into Fitness After a Break

Transcript_Summary.Speaker: John Alva Seven
Content: We're going to talk about how to get back into fitness after a break. We'll discuss the challenges of adjusting to new circumstances and ways to maintain motivation.

Transcript_Summary.Speaker: Jordan Syak
Content: It's important to be realistic with your goals, especially if you've taken a break from working out.
If you're struggling to fit into your previous training routine, consider making adjustments. You can go down in frequency or intensity while still maintaining good habits.

Transcript_Summary.Speaker: Mike Nillis
Content: Maintaining consistency is key when getting back into fitness after a break.
Set realistic goals and expectations for yourself to avoid feeling overwhelmed.

Transcript_Summary.Speaker: John Alva Seven
Content: Sometimes, it's necessary to shift your focus from aesthetics to strength or other training goals that align better with your current situation.
Don't be too hard on yourself and allow for flexibility in your fitness routine.

Transcript_Summary.Speaker: Jordan Syak
Content: It's important to consider the changes in your life when adjusting your fitness routine, such as new family responsibilities or work commitments.
Don't feel like you have to go back to your previous level of intensity if it isn't sustainable.

Transcript_Summary.Speaker: John Alva Seven
Content: Remember that the goal is not just to look a certain way, but also to maintain overall health and well-being.
Listen to your body and make necessary adjustments as needed.

Flexibility is key in maintaining consistency, especially during challenging times.
Focus on overall health and well-being, not just aesthetics or performance metrics.

takeaways: Choosing the right weight is crucial for effective workouts and achieving desired results.
Consider muscle group, workout goal (hypertrophy vs strength), program recommendations, and personal fitness level when selecting weights.

Mix up rep ranges periodically to challenge different muscle fibers and prevent plateaus.

title: The Miraculous Journey to San Gimignano

main_points.point: The authors decided to visit a small town in Tuscany after considering giving up due to the difficult drive. They were led by their intuition, and ended up at San Gimignano - an ancient hilltop town with stunning views.
details: After driving through long distances, they found San Gimignano on a sign during their walk back to the B&B.
They walked past a mean dog but followed another dirt road that eventually led them to the correct path.
The town is characterized by narrow winding streets, ancient buildings, and flower-adorned windows.

main_points.point: At a restaurant in San Gimignano, they ordered their favorite food and were surprised to find an unexpected outdoor garden with a breathtaking view.
details: The outdoor area was not visible from the street, yet it offered the perfect view of the valley below.
They toasted to their creation after dinner, expressing gratitude for their lives.

main_points.point: Their journey back to Austria was seamless and perfect as they had asked for no traffic, open borders, sunny weather, and even free passage through a toll gate.
details: The day's events were an apparent proof of the power of intention and manifestation.
They felt relieved, secure, and grateful to each other.

author_insights.insight_1: The authors realized that their lives can be amazing if they stop controlling every aspect and allow spirit to create for them.
author_insights.insight_2: They were thankful for being together and seeing the magnificence of who and what they are.

lesson_learned: Following intuition, allowing spirit to guide us, and trusting in our intentions can lead to miraculous experiences and manifest positive outcomes.

This week, we have an incredibly deep and meaningful conversation with Christina, a dear friend who is also part of my family. The discussion delves into profound topics such as race and identity, the impact of the pandemic on mental health, and personal resilience. Here are some key highlights from our chat:

- **Race and Identity:** Christina discusses how racial stereotypes can influence behavior, particularly among black women. She mentions that even in professional settings like Ina Spirit, where she felt more accepted, people would still call her 'the angry black woman.' This experience highlights the persistent nature of such stereotypes.

- **Mental Health and Resilience:** The conversation touches on how to navigate social interactions during times of heightened stress. Christina suggests using simple tools like pre-written response cards for awkward situations, which can help maintain composure and avoid unnecessary conflicts.

- **Impact of the Pandemic:** We discuss the broader impact of the pandemic, including its effect on mental health and the lack of public acknowledgment of the grief associated with loss due to COVID. The conversation emphasizes the need to acknowledge and address the full range of emotions and impacts brought about by the pandemic.

- **Closing Thoughts:** Christina shares personal insights that only family members can provide, adding a layer of authenticity and intimacy to our discussion.

interview_transcript.text: This transcript contains a discussion on hiring practices, team dynamics and culture within the context of NASCAR pit crews. The interview revolves around identifying key traits in potential hires, such as work ethic, attitude, and leadership qualities.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: Could you describe the process for evaluating new tire changer candidates?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: We look at a combination of their background, personality traits like work ethic and positive attitude. We use spreadsheets to analyze past performance statistics and match them with successful teams. The goal is to find individuals who can contribute positively to the team dynamic.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: How long does it typically take for a new tire changer to settle into their role?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: Generally, less than four years or more than 12. It takes about a year or two before people can be confidently deemed reliable.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: What are some key characteristics you look for in new hires?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: We focus on individuals who bring positive energy and passion to the team. They should enjoy working with others, as they'll be spending a lot of time together. We also prioritize traits like reliability and teamwork.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: How important is cultural fit in hiring for your team?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: Cultural fit is very important. We want people who are willing to support their teammates, as well as those who can handle occasional disagreements and push each other to perform better.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: Can you share an example of how team dynamics play a crucial role in pit stops?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: Absolutely. Every member's role is critical, but it’s also about the overall teamwork. For instance, a tire changer must focus on their fundamental tasks, like hitting lug nuts correctly, while also anticipating where the hose might go. The team dynamics ensure that everyone works efficiently and effectively under pressure.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: What role does leadership play in your pit crew?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: Leadership is key, but it’s not always the official leader. There can be vocal leaders who inspire and quiet individuals whose contributions are just as valuable. We emphasize that every team member has a unique role to play.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: How do you ensure that new hires contribute positively to your team's culture?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: We focus on finding people who enjoy working with others, as they'll spend a lot of time together. We also prioritize reliability and teamwork. If a person can handle the pressure and bring positive energy, they will likely fit well into our culture.

interview_transcript.speaker: Interviewer
interview_transcript.text: What are some challenges you face in maintaining team cohesion during remote work or social distancing?

interview_transcript.speaker: User
interview_transcript.text: It's challenging because the relationships that build the culture can't be maintained as easily. We rely on in-person interactions, like helping each other move houses or attending happy hours and hotel rooms together. However, we make efforts to keep our team spirit strong through virtual meetings and maintaining open communication.
