transcript:
00:01:24 - 00:08:16
Welcome to Hopes and Dreams, a podcast about inclusion and the power of diversity.

The real beauty of Janelle is that we have so many beautiful souls who are bringing out the best in others. I'm the beard, and today my guest is Kevin Shafer. Kevin is a director at SIP, or Student Independence Project, which is an initiative with the California Department of Education to support students with intellectual disabilities to participate fully in their educational communities.

Kevin, thank you for being here on this podcast. Can you tell me about your background and how it led you to work with SIP?
00:08:16 - 00:12:55
Thank you for having me, the beard. I'm really excited to be here, and I think what we're doing through SIP is going to make a huge difference in students' lives.
My background started out of personal experience with my wife's cousin. She was born with Down syndrome, and growing up, she just had a normal life, but the teachers would pull her out because they felt it wasn't important for other kids to see them be successful. And so I saw this happen in my own community, which was really frustrating. And then I ended up working at the Department of Education on special education, and I got more and more frustrated with the system as we were doing what we thought was best for students but not really making an impact.

00:12:55 - 00:26:13
And so in my last role before joining SIP, which was a very senior leadership position at the department, I was leading a project called PACE, or Person-Centered Accountability and Evaluation. And through that experience, I saw there were a lot of people out there who are really committed to making sure students with intellectual disabilities have meaningful lives but not necessarily having the resources they need to do so. So we started to connect those individuals with grants, which is now what SIP does today.

We provide grant support and training for schools, and our goal is to make sure that students with intellectual disabilities are included in all aspects of their educational communities. We want them to participate fully, be self-advocates, have a voice at the table, so we train teachers, administrators, parents, students themselves, because it's about making sure everyone has an equal opportunity.

00:26:13 - 00:37:48
I started working with SIP in September of last year. And one thing that stood out to me was the individualized education plans or IEPs. We used to think that the goal for students with intellectual disabilities is simply to get a job, and we're now thinking about their whole lives. And so the student-led IEP is an approach where they take control of their own learning plan. They decide what matters most to them in life, whether it's education, work or relationships, and then we help them create goals around that. So instead of focusing on what someone else thinks a person with Down syndrome should be doing, we're really trying to center the student's voice.

The idea behind student-led IEPs is that students are at the forefront of their educational journey, and they have ideas about themselves that others might not see or understand. They can articulate their goals better than anyone else, and by making this shift in mindset, we're empowering them to take ownership of their lives.

00:37:48 - 00:52:16
The biggest challenge is just shifting the mindset from a traditional education system that may not be fully inclusive. We have to convince everyone involved that it's possible and beneficial for students with intellectual disabilities to participate in all aspects of their educational communities. The other piece, which I think is really interesting about SIP, is that we work at the state level. So what happens in one district or school might affect another. And so by working together, we're creating a ripple effect where more and more schools are adopting these practices.

We do see positive results from this approach, but it's not an easy task. For example, one of our grantees is trying to include students with intellectual disabilities in college classes, which can be challenging because the curriculum might not always align with their needs or goals. However, we believe that if we keep pushing and creating opportunities for them, they will thrive.

00:52:16 - 00:59:14
The overall message of SIP is to break down barriers and make sure everyone has the opportunity to participate fully in their educational communities. We want to create a culture where inclusion is not just seen as an add-on, but as something that's valued and celebrated. And we're seeing more and more parents and students advocating for themselves or others with intellectual disabilities.

We believe that by giving students like Janelle the tools to advocate for their own needs and goals, they can have a better life. We want them to be seen as valuable members of society who can contribute to their communities in meaningful ways. And through our work at SIP, we're striving to make this vision a reality.

00:59:14 - 01:06:23
In terms of what you've seen that has been huge or monumental steps towards success, I think the shift from focusing on just employment goals to recognizing the importance of all aspects of a person's life is one of them. Another is seeing more parents and students take an active role in advocating for themselves or others with intellectual disabilities.

What does full inclusion look like in practice? How do we create a school environment where everyone feels seen, heard, and valued?
01:06:23 - 01:19:57
Full inclusion is about creating an environment where all students are welcomed and given opportunities to participate fully. We want them to have meaningful interactions with their peers and be part of the school community. This means breaking down physical barriers, such as having inclusive classrooms or flexible scheduling that allows for students to move between different activities.

It's also about changing attitudes and beliefs around intellectual disabilities. We need to challenge stereotypes and biases, and encourage a culture where diversity is celebrated. This can be done through training teachers and staff on how to create an inclusive classroom environment, as well as involving students with intellectual disabilities in decision-making processes within the school.

One of the key things we do at SIP is provide resources and support for schools to adopt these practices. We also train teachers and parents to understand that inclusion isn't just about physical presence; it's about creating an emotional connection where every student feels a sense of belonging.

For example, in our IEP process, students are encouraged to share their goals and preferences with the team, which includes family members and educators. This helps build trust and ensures that everyone is working towards the same end goal. By involving all stakeholders, we're creating an environment where every student feels valued.

01:19:57 - 01:26:38
In terms of the social impact, I think there's a lot to be gained from creating inclusive schools. It helps break down barriers and promotes understanding among students without disabilities, as well as those with intellectual disabilities. By having more diverse groups in classrooms, we can challenge stereotypes and promote acceptance.

From my experience, full inclusion is not only beneficial for students but also for the entire school community. When everyone feels included, there's a sense of unity that fosters positive relationships and helps create a better learning environment. It's about creating an atmosphere where every student can thrive and contribute to their community in meaningful ways.

So, Kevin, thank you so much for your time today. And for our listeners at home, I encourage them to listen again or share this episode with someone who might benefit from the insights shared here. And on behalf of Janelle, I want to say thank you for everything that you do and continue doing.

01:26:38 - 01:27:47
Thank you for having me, the beard. I really appreciate it, and I'm excited to see what the future holds as we continue to make a difference in students' lives through SIP.
title: Kevin Shafer | Hopes & Dreams Part 1
topics: Inclusion and Diversity in Special Education

takeaways.1: Kevin Shafer is a director at SIP, an initiative with the California Department of Education to support students with intellectual disabilities.
takeaways.2: The traditional approach focused on employment goals for individuals with intellectual disabilities; now there's more emphasis on recognizing the importance of all aspects of their life.
takeaways.3: The shift from a traditional education system that may not be fully inclusive is challenging, but it creates a ripple effect where more and more schools adopt these practices.

key_points.1: SIP's mission: to make sure students with intellectual disabilities are included in all aspects of their educational communities.
key_points.2: Student-led IEPs empower students to take control of their own learning plan, centering on what matters most to them in life.
key_points.3: Full inclusion involves breaking down physical and attitudinal barriers, promoting diversity, and creating an environment where every student feels valued.

key_points.content: Ruth was instructed by Naomi to wash herself, put on a beautiful garment, and anoint herself with body lotion before going to meet Boaz. This act symbolized the need for spiritual preparation and discernment.

key_points.point: Spiritual Discernment
key_points.content: During trials, God uses various means to separate the wheat from the chaff in our lives. He removes those things that do not belong, allowing us to focus on what is truly valuable and important.

key_points.point: Waiting for Guidance
key_points.content: Ruth was instructed to wait until Boaz had finished eating and drinking before seeking guidance or instruction from him. This teaches us the importance of being patient and seeking God's timing in all things.

conclusion: In conclusion, personal preparation and positioning ourselves for harvest involves both spiritual and physical cleansing. It is during this process that we can truly discern what is valuable and important in our lives, allowing us to focus on what brings true joy and fulfillment. Remember to be patient and wait for God's guidance as He leads us through the trials of life.

Title: Finding Your Path with Inner Voice and Inspiration
Summary: The podcast episode focuses on finding one's path in life by following the inner voice and embracing inspiration. Craig shares his personal journey of trusting his instincts and taking small steps each day to find direction, while Jenny discusses a class called '50 Questions to Free Your Mind' which encourages self-reflection and awareness.

Craig emphasizes the importance of listening to one's intuition rather than relying solely on external information or advice. He reflects on how he overcame doubts and discouragement from others and learned to trust his inner voice, even if it led him in unexpected directions. Craig also highlights the value of taking small steps each day towards a more positive mindset.

Jenny introduces '50 Questions to Free Your Mind,' an Oasis class that aims to encourage brain fitness while addressing spiritual aspects through self-reflection and awareness. She quotes Johan Gottfried von Herder, emphasizing the need for inspiration in our lives to ignite our inner potential and bring our dreams to fruition. Jenny also discusses how emotions can influence our decision-making and suggests the importance of emotional intelligence.

Both speakers stress that it is crucial to reconnect with one's true self and core values during uncertain times. Craig encourages listeners to take small, positive steps daily while being mindful of their thoughts and feelings. Jenny invites participants to join an upcoming class on July 29th where they can engage in new ways of thinking about life through a series of thought-provoking questions.
Key Takeaways: Trust your inner voice over external advice.
Practice mindfulness by asking yourself 'where are you?' and 'what time is it?' each day.
Take small steps towards positive change and self-discovery.
Embrace inspiration to ignite one's potential and bring dreams to reality.
Cultivate emotional intelligence through understanding emotions, triggers, and responses.

podcast_summary.content: Daran discusses the pivotal role that leaders play in setting a strong culture within their organization. He stresses how leaders set the tone for employees, influence team dynamics, and ultimately determine whether an environment is positive or toxic.

This includes taking time to greet employees personally upon arrival, showing up during significant life events like births or funerals, and expressing care for the well-being of each team member.

podcast_summary.topic: Cultivating a Balance Between Order and Chaos
podcast_summary.content: Leaders need to maintain a balance between structure (order) and innovation (chaos) within their organizations. It's important not to be overly rigid, but also not to completely allow the environment to devolve into chaos without any form of management.

Creating a culture where employees feel heard and valued can lead to increased productivity and innovation. Leaders should encourage open communication channels and actively seek out input from all levels within the organization, fostering an environment that embraces creativity and collaboration.

Daran emphasizes that businesses have the potential to move past their current state and redefine themselves for the better. He reminds listeners of the opportunity they have to change their present situation or even future prospects by making thoughtful decisions today.

Daran offers his support and availability to assist businesses looking to improve their culture, leadership practices, or overall operations. He provides contact information for those interested in collaborating further on these initiatives.

.TRANSCRIPT:
You're listening to Nook's Tavern, the official podcast for Animal Crossing fans everywhere. Join us every week as we talk about all things related to this popular Nintendo franchise. I'm your host, Kurt.

Kurt: Welcome back to Nook's Tavern. We have a lot of exciting news and updates to share with you this episode. Let's dive right in!

First up, we wanted to take a moment to thank our friends at the Morning Stream Podcast for giving us a shoutout on their recent episode. If any new listeners are tuning in from the Morning Stream, welcome aboard! And be sure to check out their show as well.

Now let's get into some of the latest news and updates from the Animal Crossing world.

We have an interesting new discovery regarding airport colors. It seems that the color of your island's airport will determine the default colors of certain items in your game. There are four possible airport colors: blue, orange, green, and yellow. For example, if you have a blue airport, the vending machine will be gray by default. Similarly, with an orange airport, you'll get a brown monster to buy. Green gives you a blue monster, and yellow yields a black monster.

But that's not all! If you see other items of the same color in your game, it increases the likelihood that you'll receive similar items later on. For instance, if there are white lighthouses, it's more probable that you'll get a pure white satellite dish with a Nook logo on it.

There's an extensive infographic detailing these connections, and we've linked to it in the show notes. It's fascinating to see which items correspond to each other based on color. We highly recommend checking it out if you're interested in delving deeper into this aspect of the game.

Moving on, there has been a fix for duping issues that were present in recent updates. For those unfamiliar with duping, it refers to the process of creating multiple copies of an item or villager, which can be exploited in the game. The update has addressed these concerns, ensuring a fair and balanced gameplay experience.

Lastly, we have some intriguing information regarding the math behind how villagers decide whether to move out of your island. Previously, getting a villager to leave required at least six other villagers on the island. Now, with this new system, the probability is determined by the formula V * 5 + C, where V is the number of villagers and C is an additional factor that hasn't been explicitly defined yet.

There's also a five-day cooldown period after asking a villager to leave or stay, so you can't bombard them with requests too frequently. Additionally, friendship levels range from zero to 255, starting at 25, adding another layer of complexity to the formula. While we don't go into all the mathematical details in this episode, there's plenty to explore if you're interested in diving deep.

And now, for our Community Spotlight segment! We want to highlight a fan who recently shared an Easter Island Head remake of Parks and Recreation. It was shot-for-shot with hilarious results, especially when Ron Swanson pulls out a tooth during the scene. The creative use of Easter Island heads in this remake is impressive.

If you're part of our community and have something you'd like us to highlight on future episodes, please send us your projects or ideas. You can reach us at nooks.tavern.net@gmail.com.

That's all for today's episode of Nook's Tavern. We hope you found this information helpful and entertaining. Join us next time as we continue our journey through the world of Animal Crossing.

Changing negative thought patterns can lead to personal growth and freedom.

# ContraConcern Podcast

## Overview of the Show

In this episode, Joe covers a variety of topics including political commentary on current events, discussions about culture and society, as well as media critique. The show delves into several segments that highlight different issues, such as police reform in Washington State, the renaming of places like Columbus Day, and the public figures discussed include Senator John Kennedy and Tommy Lahren.

## Key Points:

1. **Police Reform Discussion** - Joe critiques Senator Kennedy's argument by suggesting he should give a crackhead a police uniform to show his support for reforming the police force instead of calling them when in trouble. This is presented as a humorous yet profound way to highlight the contradictions and flaws in the argument.

2. **Columbus Day Renaming** - Joe humorously suggests alternative names for the District of Columbia, such as 'District of Aragon' or 'DE, District of Farrington.' He also mocks the idea that Christopher Columbus did not mean any harm when he committed massacres during his voyages.

3. **Tommy Lahren Critique** - Joe strongly criticizes Tommy Lahren for her stance and rhetoric, describing her as one of the worst pundits due to her simplistic and often misleading arguments. He suggests that her arguments are outdated and rooted in a mentality from 2016, criticizing her for not having evolved with the times.

4. **Media Critique** - Joe mentions 'media matters' as a source that did not generate much interest or attention, highlighting how certain media outlets may go unnoticed by the public unless they are explicitly sought out.

## Key Figures:

- **Senator John Kennedy**: Criticized for his argument on police reform and his suggestion to call crackheads instead of police in case of trouble. Joe uses this as a humorous way to expose the flaws in the logic behind his statement.

- **Tommy Lahren**: Described by Joe as one of the worst pundits due to her simplistic arguments, particularly her stance that people who hate America still want to live there because they don't have the means or desire to leave. She is also criticized for her fixation on Donald Trump being their president.

## Humor and Tone:

Joe maintains a sarcastic and humorous tone throughout the episode, often using absurd scenarios (like calling a crackhead when in trouble) to illustrate his points. He frequently uses hyperbole and irony to make his arguments more impactful.

Joe humorously suggests alternative names for the District of Columbia and criticizes Christopher Columbus's actions during his voyages.

episode_title: Beneath the Waves: Matt Silver and Education's New Frontier
transcript:
Ralph Benke interviews Matt Silver about his Beneath the Waves initiative, its impact on education leadership, and how it can be applied globally.

[00:00:00] Ralph Benke: Welcome to another episode of The Bleeding Edge. I'm your host, Ralph Benke. Today we have a fantastic guest with us who is really making waves in the educational world. Matt Silver is the Headmaster of Shaftree High School and he's also the founder of Beneath the Waves, an initiative aimed at redefining leadership in education to foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

[00:00:26] Matt Silver: Thank you very much for having me. I'm really looking forward to discussing this work that we're doing.

[00:00:34] Ralph Benke: Absolutely. So tell us a bit about your background and how you came up with the idea of Beneath the Waves?

[00:00:41] Matt Silver: My career in education has been quite varied, starting as a teacher and moving on to senior leadership roles. I noticed that there was a gap between what we were doing on the surface level and what really mattered beneath the waves. This initiative came from a desire to address this imbalance by focusing on deeper aspects of leadership such as emotional intelligence, values alignment, and collective learning.

[00:01:08] Ralph Benke: That's fascinating. Can you explain more about these core components? How do they interconnect?

[00:01:15] Matt Silver: Absolutely. The core components are the I (individual) and the We (collective). The 'I' represents personal development, values alignment, emotional intelligence, and a clear sense of purpose. These elements help leaders understand their own strengths and weaknesses, align their actions with their values, and maintain a positive mindset for personal growth. On the other hand, the 'We' component focuses on collective learning, collaboration, innovation, and system-level thinking. By fostering an environment where individuals can learn from each other and work towards common goals, we create a more resilient and adaptable organization.

[00:01:48] Ralph Benke: It's clear that Beneath the Waves aims to transform not just individual leaders but entire organizations. How do you measure the success of this initiative?

[00:02:01] Matt Silver: We use a combination of qualitative and quantitative measures. On the qualitative side, we look at feedback from participants, changes in behavior and attitudes, and improvements in school culture. Quantitatively, we track metrics such as student performance, teacher satisfaction, and overall school success.

[00:02:21] Ralph Benke: That's very comprehensive. Now, let's talk about your webinar series. How has it been received by participants?

[00:02:30] Matt Silver: The response has been overwhelmingly positive. Participants have shared that they feel more empowered and motivated to drive change within their schools. They also report a greater sense of connection and collaboration among staff, which is crucial for long-term success.

[00:02:48] Ralph Benke: That's great to hear. What do you hope participants take away from these webinars?

[00:03:01] Matt Silver: I hope that they gain a deeper understanding of their own capabilities and the importance of working together as a team. They should leave with new strategies for fostering a growth mindset, improving communication, and creating an environment where innovation can thrive.

[00:03:24] Ralph Benke: And what are some key takeaways from your experiences leading Shaftree High School under this approach?

[00:03:31] Matt Silver: At Shaftree, we've seen a significant improvement in student engagement and academic performance. Teachers feel more supported and empowered to make meaningful changes in their classrooms. Overall, the school culture has become more positive and collaborative.

[00:04:02] Ralph Benke: That's impressive progress. You mentioned earlier that you're working on a research paper for peer review. Can you tell us more about it?

[00:04:12] Matt Silver: Yes, the paper focuses on the Beneath the Waves framework and its application in education leadership. It includes case studies and data from our own school and other institutions we've worked with. The goal is to provide evidence-based guidance for educators who want to implement similar approaches.

[00:04:30] Ralph Benke: That sounds like valuable work. How can listeners get involved or learn more about Beneath the Waves?

[00:04:38] Matt Silver: They can visit our website at Shaftree High School, follow us on Twitter @ShaftreeHS, and connect with me on LinkedIn. We're also planning to expand the initiative globally, so stay tuned for future developments.

[00:05:06] Ralph Benke: Excellent. Matt, thank you so much for sharing your insights today. Where can listeners find more information about your work?

[00:05:13] Matt Silver: They can check out our website and social media channels. I encourage everyone to explore the concept of Beneath the Waves and consider how it might impact their own leadership journey.

[00:05:27] Ralph Benke: Great advice, Matt. Thank you again for joining us on The Bleeding Edge.

[00:05:31] Matt Silver: Thanks, Ralph. It's been a pleasure to be here.

text: This message is part of a sermon on Psalm 23, which focuses on the imagery of God as a shepherd and provider. The speaker explains that while this passage primarily describes the comfort and provision of God for his people, it also applies to believers today. The main points include: 1) God's protection - He protects us from physical harm but more importantly our souls; 2) God's provision - He provides what we need, not always what we want, in ways that show His glory and enable us to accomplish His tasks; 3) Communion with God - The most glorious gift is being able to commune with Him through Christ. The speaker concludes by praying for comfort, guidance, rest, and the ability to share this message of hope with others during uncertain times.

podcast.title: Get Off My Lawn - Episode 31
podcast.transcript:
Hello and welcome to the latest episode of Get Off My Lawn, where I discuss various issues affecting society today. Today's episode will focus on the economic impact of the pandemic, the government's response, and how people are coping with restrictions. Let's get started.

Firstly, it's important to acknowledge that many people have been struggling financially during this time. The unemployment rate has reached unprecedented levels, and a significant number of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck. Some have received stimulus checks, but these can be insufficient in covering basic expenses such as rent or mortgage payments. There is currently an ongoing debate about the need for further stimulus packages.

Secondly, there seems to be a wide range of opinions on how long the pandemic will last and when we can return to our normal lives. Some people are eager to resume their pre-pandemic routines, while others remain cautious. As we navigate these differing perspectives, it's essential to balance personal freedom with public health concerns.

Lastly, there is a growing concern about the impact of prolonged restrictions on mental health and overall well-being. Many individuals are struggling with loneliness and anxiety due to isolation measures, which can have long-term consequences if not addressed properly.

title: Interview with Vishak Haque about Uptara and Spellbound
summary: In this episode, host Leyla Sanayi interviews Vishak Haque about her graphic storytelling debut 'Uptara' and the upcoming memoir 'Spellbound'. The conversation covers Haque's creative background as an architect before transitioning to comics, influences on her work, narrative techniques like stories within stories, and how Haque navigates virtual events during the pandemic. Sanayi also asks for Haque’s favorite book from They See Books collection.
topics: Influence of older comic artists on current work
Narrative techniques and stories within stories
keyPoints: Vishak Haque came to graphic storytelling after a background in architecture.
Architecture was healthy for her as an escape from frustration, allowing her to channel creative energy into drawing and comics.
Influences include older comic artists like Tintin, Beetal Byam, and Edward Gorey, who inspired vivid colors and storytelling techniques.
Haque prefers the short story form due to its ability to explore complex themes in a concentrated space, similar to Doris Lessing's and Margaret Atwood's works.
Her graphic storytelling focuses on themes of gender, body, and existential conformity, often exploring these through fantastical yet relatable narratives.
The format of 'Uptara' allows for multiple narrative layers, including stories within stories, which Haque finds compelling as seen in epic literature like Bejawada Gita.
During the pandemic, Haque has been actively promoting her work virtually and leveraging digital platforms to reach audiences.
quotes: It was healthy for me to channel that frustration into a creative way, so I started drawing again. And then eventually I got interested in comics, which is a different kind of storytelling.
I look up to older comic artists like Tintin, Beetal Byam, and Edward Gorey. They have a certain way of using color, which I think is really great.

    <section start="00:04:18.930" end="00:04:27.680">And then the other challenge is making sure that there's a good communication plan in place to keep participants informed about their 401(k) plan.</section>
    <section start="00:04:29.530" end="00:04:35.860">John: </section>
    <section start="00:04:36.350" end="00:04:44.870">Yeah, that's a good point because you want to make sure that the participants are engaged and understand what their options are.</section>
    <section start="00:04:46.190" end="00:05:03.020">Kevin: </section>

title: Episode with D Santana - Hiking and Personal Growth

transcript.text: Welcome to Just Trick's podcast. I'm your host, Justin, and today we have a special guest who will be sharing her journey with us. She is a hiker, adventurer, and personal growth advocate named D Santana.
D, can you tell our listeners a bit about yourself?
Sure! I'm a hiking enthusiast based in Los Angeles. Hiking has become an integral part of my life as it not only keeps me physically fit but also helps me find inner peace and connect with nature.
That's great to hear! How did you get into hiking?

I started hiking by accident. One day, I went for a walk in my neighborhood and stumbled upon a trail that eventually led me to the nearby mountains. It was exhilarating, and from there on, I fell in love with exploring different trails and heights.
That sounds like an amazing start! Can you share some of your favorite hiking spots in Los Angeles?
Absolutely! Some of my favorites include the Santa Monica Mountains, San Gabriel Mountains, and Baldwin Peak. Each one offers a unique experience with stunning views.
Those sound incredible! How does hiking help you in your personal growth journey?

Hiking helps me in many ways. It allows me to disconnect from the hustle and bustle of daily life, which helps me gain clarity and focus on my goals. Additionally, it teaches me about perseverance and resilience as I face challenges during the hike.
That's wonderful! Do you have any tips for someone who is just starting out with hiking?

Certainly! Start by choosing trails that are appropriate for your fitness level. Always check the weather conditions before heading out and wear comfortable, sturdy footwear. Most importantly, enjoy the journey and take it one step at a time.
Great advice! Can you tell us about any recent hiking adventures?
Recently, I completed a challenging hike to the top of Mount Baldy. It was incredibly rewarding, both physically and mentally.
That sounds like an impressive feat! Do you have any other outdoor activities or hobbies besides hiking?
Yes, I also enjoy kayaking and exploring national parks. These activities complement my love for nature and provide me with different perspectives on adventure.
That's awesome! You mentioned that hiking helps you find inner peace. Can you elaborate on that?

Certainly! Hiking in nature allows me to detach from the noise of everyday life and find a sense of calm and tranquility. It reminds me of the beauty and vastness of our world, which helps me feel more grounded.
That's beautiful! Do you have any favorite quotes or mantras that inspire you in your personal growth journey?
Yes, I love the quote by Jack Canfield: 'You can't do it all. But you can do something.' It reminds me to focus on small steps and progress rather than feeling overwhelmed by large goals.
That's a great reminder! Lastly, is there anything you would like to share with our listeners?
Yes, I encourage everyone to invest in themselves and take the time to understand their own needs. Self-reflection and personal growth are key to living a fulfilling life.

title: Deep Dive: Kubeflow Serving with David Wu
summary: In this episode, Matt and David discuss Kubeflow serving and how it can be used to deploy machine learning models. They cover the basics of Kubeflow serving, including what an endpoint is and why serverless hosting is beneficial for real-time applications. The hosts also touch on some of the challenges involved in deploying machine learning models using Kubeflow, such as setting up a cluster, and provide tips for overcoming those challenges.
key takeaways: Kubeflow serving allows data scientists to deploy their models in a production environment, making them available through an API endpoint. This can be beneficial for real-time applications that require low latency predictions.

Setting up a Kubeflow cluster is one of the biggest challenges when deploying machine learning models using this approach, but there are resources and community support available to help with this process.

Serverless hosting can be an effective solution for certain types of applications that don't need constant availability or high availability, as it reduces costs and allows for more efficient resource utilization.
discussion_points: The hosts discuss the benefits and limitations of Kubeflow serving compared to other deployment options, such as Kubernetes.
They also cover some of the best practices for deploying machine learning models using Kubeflow, including how to containerize your model and serve it with a web framework like Flask or Tornado.
The hosts share their personal experiences working with Kubeflow serving, highlighting both successes and challenges they've faced.

summary: The hosts continue their podcast by discussing pets and sharing stories about their experiences with them, referring to the pets as roommates. They share insights on why they might want a pet in the future, and the dynamics that can arise between humans and their animal companions. transcript:
[Hosts continue the podcast]

Mayor: So I was thinking we could go ahead and talk pets today. You know, like I said in the previous episodes, you all live with these animals. They're your roommates, so why don't you all just share a little bit about your pets? Because I think it would be interesting to hear that insight.

John: Sure, can I go first?

Mayor: Yeah, we'll go ahead and start with you.

John: Absolutely. My cat is the best roommate ever. She's super needy, but in a good way. She just wants attention all the time, and it's so funny because she kind of reminds me of my roommates who are always wanting something from me. So I think there's some parallels between us as roommates and her.

Mayor: That’s very interesting to hear that you make these comparisons with your cats in terms of their desires for attention and how they act similar to your human roommates. Do any of the other hosts have pets, or do they live with them?

Liam: I don't actually have a pet right now, but my parents are into dogs. They love going on walks and such, so it's interesting to hear you guys talk about it.

John: Yeah, same here. My dad is allergic to cats, so we can't get one. But my aunt has a dog that I sometimes visit, and she always talks about how much the neighbors' dogs annoy her while they're out for walks or skiing.

Mayor: That's funny. It’s like those animals are just interrupting their peaceful moments. In any case, it sounds like you all have mixed feelings on pets. But in the future, do you think you'll get one? Are there certain types of pets that appeal to you?

Liam: I definitely would love to have a dog eventually. Living with my parents right now, but yeah, once I move out, I'd love to have a dog and take care of it myself.

John: Same here! It's just that I gotta move out first, though.

Mayor: And then what about you, John? Do you want any specific type of pet?

John: Yeah, probably a cat. I like the idea of having a constant companion and someone who is always there to cuddle with.

Liam: That's funny because I was just thinking that cats often seem more like science experiments than dogs; they're just unpredictable, you know? They have their own little quirks and behaviors.

Mayor: Exactly. And it’s interesting to hear about these dynamics between humans and animals. It really does make you think about the companionship aspect of having a pet in your life. [laughs]

John: Yeah, I definitely agree with that. Moving on from pets, what would constitute a perfect day for you?

Mayor: Perfect day? Okay, so there are no expectations or responsibilities. Just doing whatever makes you happy.

Liam: So, waking up to beautiful birds chirping and making a perfect cup of coffee. I mean, I could probably wake up at 9 AM, and it's sunny outside. I would make my favorite pot of coffee and sip on that while sitting on the front porch enjoying the scenery. No expectations for anything else.

Mayor: Sounds good so far! And then after that, you said something about making some eggs and a little skillet thing, right?

Liam: Yeah, maybe I'll make an omelette or something like that. Then go downstairs to play some guitar and start working on writing. Maybe even jam out a bit.

Mayor: That’s great! After that, how about taking a paddle on the river? Find a new spot you haven't been before?

Liam: Absolutely, just experience something new. And then come back and play cards or Magic the Gathering. Then in the evening, maybe watch an improv show and play some video games with friends.

Mayor: That sounds like an amazing day! I can almost see us all having that kind of perfect day together sometime soon.

John: Yeah, it would be nice to just have that kind of freedom without any expectations. But the best part is waking up without setting an alarm. That's true freedom.

Mayor: Exactly! And it's funny how it feels like you've finally arrived when you can wake up whenever you want.

Liam: It’s so much better than being a prisoner to your own schedule, right?

Mayor: Absolutely. So thanks for listening everyone. We hope you enjoyed this episode and got to learn more about us through our pets and perfect days.

summary: Erin and Garen discuss the values, beliefs, and differences between political parties in the United States. They also reflect on the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on politics and the upcoming election process.
transcript:
Erin: Good evening, everyone! Welcome to another episode of Talk a Latte. I'm your host, Erin, and today we're going to dive into some political stuff, so please sit back, grab a cup of coffee or tea, and enjoy this conversation.

Garen: Yeah, that's right! And my name is Garen. We're talking about some different values and beliefs, the two parties in America, Republican Party and Democratic Party.

Erin: Yeah, so these are our two major political parties here in the United States. And today we're going to discuss their values and beliefs a bit more. So, Garen, can you give us a brief overview of each party's values and beliefs?

Garen: Sure! The Republican Party is generally known for its support of free market capitalism, smaller government, lower taxes, traditional family values, and limited immigration. They believe in individual liberties and are often associated with social conservatism.

Erin: And the Democratic Party? What about them?

Garen: The Democratic Party tends to support a larger role for government in society, higher taxes on the wealthy, greater access to healthcare and education, stronger environmental regulations, and more progressive social policies. They're often associated with diversity, equality, and human rights.

Erin: Yeah, so it's pretty clear that there are significant differences between these two parties in terms of their values and beliefs. And this can lead to a divided society at times. But why is it important for us as individuals to know about different political perspectives?

Garen: I think it's really important because, you know, we're all human, right? We have the same basic needs and desires. And yet, people can have such different values and beliefs that cause so much division between us as a society.

Erin: Yes, absolutely! And it's interesting to learn about these perspectives because it helps us understand why certain issues are important to different groups of people. For example, someone who leans Republican might prioritize individual liberties and limited government involvement, while someone who leans Democratic might focus on social justice and equality.

Garen: That's a great point! And by knowing about these differences, we can have more informed conversations with our friends and family. Instead of just taking sides or dismissing opposing viewpoints, we can engage in thoughtful discussions that lead to greater understanding and empathy.

Erin: Exactly! Informed citizens are better equipped to make decisions that align with their values. And when people understand each other's perspectives, it fosters a more inclusive and respectful society.

Garen: Agreed. And as we move forward in this conversation, I think we'll discuss the election process and how it might differ this year due to the coronavirus pandemic. But for now, let's go back to our political challenge for today: write a letter to someone you've never sent a letter to before.

Erin: That sounds like an interesting challenge! I think I'll start by sending a letter to my friend who works in healthcare. She's been on the front lines during this pandemic and I want to show my appreciation for her work.

Garen: Great idea! And thank you, Erin, for sharing that with us. Now, let's move on to our weekly challenge: hug your mom or take a selfie if you do that. Have you done this one yet?

Erin: I did that last week and it was fun! What about you, Garen?

Garen: Yeah, I did the same thing with my dad. It's nice to take a moment to appreciate those special people in our lives.

Erin: Absolutely! Now, what is next on the challenge list? Should we continue with last week's challenge or introduce something new?

transcript: [00:00:00] [Intro Music]

[00:00:18] Host: Welcome to Episode 56, the E2 Nutrition and Wellness Podcast. I'm your host, Dr. Eric R百慕大三角洲，很高兴能再次邀请到克里斯托弗·瓦尔博士（Dr. Christopher Wahl）做客我们的节目。今天我们将讨论一些有关酮类补充剂的问题，以及它们在提高运动表现方面的潜力。另外，我们还会聊一聊纤维素是否真的有效，还有关于清洁饮食的最新见解。所以请大家坐好，准备好笔和纸，让我们一起开始这段知识之旅吧！

keyPoints.content: 克里斯托弗·瓦尔博士讨论了酮类补充剂如何帮助运动员提高运动表现。他解释说，在运动过程中使用酮体作为燃料可以让运动员在锻炼时保持更长时间，因为它们比葡萄糖燃烧得慢一些。
我们讨论了不同的饮食方式，并强调了综合营养的重要性。克里斯托弗·瓦尔博士认为，无论你是素食主义者还是肉食爱好者，获取必要的营养素才是关键。他提到如果需要补充剂来满足这些需求，一定要确保选择信誉良好的公司提供的高质量产品。
我们讨论了纤维素在肠道健康中的作用。克里斯托弗·瓦尔博士指出，虽然不可溶性纤维（如芹菜）对促进消化是有益的，但过度摄入可能会导致消化不良或其他问题。
最后我们聊到了清洁饮食。克里斯托弗·瓦尔博士表示，尽管市场上充斥着各种不同的清肠产品和方式，但他认为人体自身的排毒能力是非常强大的。他建议人们通过均衡的饮食来获取所需的营养素，并补充高质量的补充剂（如果需要的话）。

S - Self-Discovery: Use journaling to uncover personal insights.

== Highlights =::
- **Young Frankenstein** is a classic comedy, reimagining Mary Shelley's _Frankenstein_ with comedic undertones and modern humor.
- The film stars Gene Wilder as Dr. Frederick Frankenstein, an descendant of Victor Frankenstein who inherits his grandfather's castle in Transylvania. 
- The cast includes young performers such as Marty Feldman, Madeline Kahn, andCloris Leachman. 
- Jean Cleary plays Inga, the love interest for Dr. Frederick Frankenstein.
- The film is known for its clever dialogue and memorable characters like Igor (Marty Feldman) and Frau Blucher (Cloris Leachman).
- Gene Wilder's portrayal of the Monster is notable, with a more sympathetic and comedic take on the character compared to earlier depictions. 
- Mel Brooks directed this film as part of his ongoing exploration of classic literature in comedic form.
- The movie balances comedy and horror elements, making it accessible for both adults and children (PG rating).
- The dialogue is sharp and witty, with memorable lines that have become pop culture references. 
- A standout scene involves Dr. Frederick Frankenstein's grandfather, played by Vincent Price, and his diary.
- The film received positive reviews upon release and has since become a beloved cult classic.
== Key Points =::
- **Gene Wilder**'s performance as the Monster in this version is notably different from previous depictions; it's more comedic and sympathetic. 
- **Mel Brooks** directed this adaptation, blending comedy with elements of horror to create a unique experience.
- The film maintains a PG rating while delivering both mature humor and scares, making it suitable for families.
- Jean Cleary portrays Inga, Dr. Frederick Frankenstein's love interest, adding depth to the romance in the story.
== Recommendations =::
- If you enjoy classic horror with a comedic twist, **Young Frankenstein** is highly recommended. 
- For fans of Mel Brooks and his work on reimagining literary classics, this film should be at the top of your list.
- This movie is perfect for family viewing but also offers enough mature humor to entertain adult audiences.
== Wrap-up =:: The episode discussed the comedic elements, characters, and overall appeal of **Young Frankenstein**. The hosts recommend it for both family entertainment and as a showcase of Mel Brooks' unique style in film.

Summary:
The speaker discusses the limitations and unreliability of first impressions, sharing personal anecdotes to illustrate her points. She emphasizes that people often misjudge others based solely on their initial interactions. Key takeaways include: 

1. First impressions are unreliable because they can be deceptive. One may present an image different from their true self.
2. Time and deeper interactions reveal the real person behind the first impression, leading to a more accurate understanding of one's character.
3. It is unwise to make judgments about someone based on a single interaction as people face various challenges that others might not fully understand or appreciate.
4. She advocates for giving individuals multiple opportunities to interact before forming any final opinions or making decisions regarding friendships, relationships, or further engagement.
5. The speaker encourages listeners to avoid basing their perception of someone solely on initial interactions and instead give them a chance to reveal their true nature through ongoing experiences and conversations.

title: Dare to Develop - Bizworthy Bash Stationers Cammy Monet & Eliza Calligraphy
summary: Joining Christina is a fun duo, Cammy and Elizabeth from Bizworthy Bash Stationery. They talk about launching their stationer's conference, the journey of working together as business partners, creating a community for stationers, and more.
transcript:
[The episode opens with background music]

Christina: Welcome back to Dare To Develop. I'm Christina Serrano. Today we have a special guest, Cammy Monet and Elizabeth Calligraphy from Bizworthy Bash Stationery.

[Cammy and Elizabeth introduce themselves briefly]

Christina: Can you tell us a bit about the conference and what it's all about?

Elizabeth: Absolutely! We launched Bizworthy Bash last year, which is our first stationer's conference. It was born from our desire to connect with other stationers and share resources. This year we're opening the doors again for people who maybe missed registration the first time or heard about it from someone else.

Cammy: Yes, exactly! We are not doing a brand new round of Bizworthy Bash until 2021 at the earliest, but this is a fantastic opportunity to join and get access to all that content. 

Christina: That's great. You both have been working together for quite some time now. Can you share more about how you two started your collaboration?

Elizabeth: Sure! Cammy and I first met through social media when we were both creating calligraphy. We discovered a shared passion, so we began collaborating on projects. Eventually, it became clear that we had complementary skills and could benefit from each other's strengths.

Cammy: That's right. It all started with us working together on a few projects, but as our partnership grew, we realized there was a need for a community specifically for stationers. So Bizworthy Bash was born!

Christina: And how has it been working as business partners?

Elizabeth: It can be challenging at times because everyone works differently. We have different approaches and ideas, but the key is to respect each other's input and work through any conflicts.

Cammy: Absolutely! We also make sure that we're both involved in every decision, so there are no surprises or unbalanced workload.

Christina: That sounds like a great system. You've created something unique together. What do you think sets Bizworthy Bash apart from other stationer's conferences?

Elizabeth: One of the things that makes us stand out is our focus on community and connections. We provide a platform for stationers to share resources, learn from each other, and build meaningful relationships.

Cammy: And we also have an online directory called The Bizworthy Bash Directory. It's essentially like yellow pages on steroids, with all the links in one place. 

Christina: That sounds incredibly useful! How do you think it has impacted your community?

Elizabeth: The community is engaged and supportive. People are more likely to use a resource if they've paid for it, so membership gives them an incentive to actively participate.

Cammy: Plus, our Facebook group is filled with helpful resources, where stationers can get advice on everything from ordering materials to troubleshooting issues with files.

Christina: That's awesome. For those who are interested in joining Bizworthy Bash or The Bizworthy Bash Directory, how do they go about it?

Elizabeth: You can visit bizbirthaybash.com for more information and to sign up for the conference. Cammy is also on Instagram at Cammy Monet.

Cammy: And I'm Eliza and Calligraphy on Instagram. 

Christina: Thank you so much, ladies! It's been a pleasure talking with you both about your journey as business partners and creators of Bizworthy Bash Stationery. 

Elizabeth & Cammy: Thank you for having us!

[Background music fades out]

summary:
The episode discusses the relationship between personal attachment to expectations of others and experiencing anger or conflict. Key points include: 

1. Personal attachments to having others think or feel a certain way can lead to frustration when those expectations are not met.
2. Expectations for specific behaviors in others, especially when they are demanded, increase the likelihood of conflict resolution struggles and resultant anger.
3. Attachment to these needs correlates directly with the amount of anger experienced.
4. Awareness and understanding that others may view their roles differently from us can help manage expectations better.
5. Setting aside one's ego is a lifelong process that requires effort but ultimately contributes to personal growth and improved emotional regulation.
takeaways: Recognize your own attachments to how others think, feel, or behave, and consider the impact they have on your emotions.
Acknowledge that people have different backgrounds, beliefs, and behaviors which may differ from yours.
Practice empathy and understanding by asking about someone's day before jumping to conclusions or expectations.
Work towards letting go of strict demands for behavior, focusing instead on cooperation and mutual respect.
View failure as an opportunity for growth rather than a setback, maintaining enthusiasm and motivation in the face of challenges.
audience: Individuals seeking personal growth and emotional intelligence
Managers and leaders who want to improve conflict resolution within their teams
Couples or partners working on communication and understanding each other better
next_steps: Identify one area where you have an attachment that may be causing frustration, and reflect on how it impacts your relationships.
Schedule a conversation with someone close to you about their experiences and feelings, rather than focusing solely on what they should do differently.
Write down three ways in which you can set aside your ego in specific situations at work or home.

title: A Fertility Journey: Emily's Experience with Secondary Infertility
description: Emily shares her experience with secondary infertility, the emotional rollercoaster of fertility treatments, and how she navigated challenges in her personal life. She offers advice for supportive friends and family members.
transcript:
Emily's journey with secondary infertility was challenging, but she found strength in sharing her story. She discusses the emotional aspects of fertility treatments and advises listeners on how to support loved ones going through similar experiences.

Despite having a successful first pregnancy, Emily and her husband faced difficulties conceiving again after four years. They struggled with unexplained secondary infertility, leading them to undergo various treatments without success. After four unsuccessful IVF cycles, they finally conceived via donor sperm, resulting in the birth of their daughter. Emily's journey was marked by disappointment, hope, and a strong support system from her partner.

Emily emphasizes the importance of being transparent about one's fertility struggles and shares advice for supportive friends and family members. She encourages people to listen without giving unsolicited advice or making insensitive comments. Emily also discusses her experiences as a public figure sharing her journey online, receiving messages of gratitude from others who feel less alone due to her transparency.

Throughout the interview, Emily reflects on how this experience has strengthened her relationships and provided opportunities to educate others about appropriate ways to support people going through similar challenges.
takeaways: Secondary infertility is a common issue affecting one in eight couples.
Being transparent and sharing personal experiences can provide comfort to others facing similar struggles.
Listening without giving unsolicited advice or making insensitive comments is crucial when supporting someone with fertility issues.

summary: The episode discusses systemic issues with policing, including funding, roles of police officers, and rethinking the purpose of law enforcement in public safety. The conversation also addresses how education funding can be improved by eliminating property taxes as a major source to break the cycle of poor educational outcomes in certain neighborhoods. The hosts use Maslow's hierarchy of needs to highlight that addressing policing first is crucial for creating an environment where people can focus on higher-level needs like education and employment. Additionally, they reference the Obama Foundation’s 2014 document outlining new approaches to public safety, emphasizing a redefinition of police roles towards more community-focused solutions. The discussion includes examples such as Camden, New Jersey, which completely scrapped its police department and saw significant reductions in crime rates after rethinking their approach. The hosts also mention the importance of targeting union strength to implement necessary reforms, including defunding certain aspects of current departments or restructuring them entirely. The episode concludes with a call for collective action against racism, likening it to addressing a pandemic, where listening to experts and changing behaviors is essential.

title: Victory Is Mine
transcript:
This podcast discusses themes of spiritual warfare, faith, and victory in Christ. The speaker emphasizes the importance of being strong in the Lord, protecting oneself through faith and the Word of God, and standing firm on one's ground in times of trial. Key points include:

1. **Being Strong in the Lord**: Encouraging listeners to stand strong in their faith.
2. **Protecting Oneself with Faith and the Word**: Urging believers to cover themselves with the blood of Jesus and the shield of faith, and to rely on the Word of God for guidance.
3. **Standing Your Ground**: Drawing an analogy from state laws like 'stand your ground' to the spiritual principles that guide believers in their battles against evil.
4. **Obedience vs. Freedom**: Cautioning listeners to use wisdom when following government orders, especially those that may conflict with God's will.
5. **Victory in Various Aspects of Life**: Highlighting that victory can be found in financial stability, health, family, and all areas of life through faith in Christ.

The speaker concludes by praying for listeners to find victory in their lives and expressing gratitude for the opportunity to share this message with them.
conclusion: The podcast encourages its audience to stand firm in their faith, protect themselves through the Word of God, and find victory in every aspect of life. It also includes a prayer for guidance and support.

Segments.Transcript: Maggie: Happy Mother's Day to all our listeners. This is Maggie Fong from ATXR, and today we're welcoming back the one and only Lola Davis. So how are you doing today, Lola? Lola: I'm doing really good. Thanks for having me, Maggie. Damon: I think there was a little bit of static in the beginning, but we got it taken care of, Maggie. So you know, Lola, this is your second episode with us, and on our first episode you were talking about how you're a busy mom and entrepreneur who owns a bar, Amber Collective, that's located in Los Angeles. But I wanted to start off by asking if you could give the listeners a quick rundown of what your business entails.

Lola: Yeah, absolutely. So Amber Collective is a bar that I own and run in Los Angeles. We specialize in handcrafted cocktails made with premium ingredients like fresh fruit, house-made syrups, and of course, spirits. We're kind of known for our unique cocktail menu, which features some really creative and delicious drinks. And we also offer food options to pair with those cocktails. So if you're looking for a place that's got great ambiance, good drinks, and tasty food, Amber Collective is definitely the spot.

Damon: That's awesome, Lola. And I think we talked a little bit about your personal experience as a mother and how it influenced your business. How did being a mom shape the way you run Amber Collective? Lola: Absolutely. Being a mom has definitely shaped my perspective in many ways. One of the things that really inspired me to start Amber Collective was just wanting to create a space where families could come together and enjoy themselves. I wanted to make sure that we had something for everyone, from moms like myself who are working hard to provide for their children, to kids who just want to have some fun with their parents. So it's really been about creating an inclusive atmosphere where people can relax, be themselves, and most importantly, bond as a family.

Maggie: That's such a wonderful idea, Lola. And I'm sure it must be challenging to balance being both a mom and an entrepreneur, especially with all the current challenges brought about by the pandemic. Can you tell us more about how you've been handling things during this time? Lola: Absolutely. It has definitely been a tough year for everyone, but I think one of the most important things is maintaining a good work-life balance. For me, that means making sure that I'm spending quality time with my family and friends, as well as taking care of myself both physically and mentally. I also try to stay connected with my team at Amber Collective through virtual meetings and check-ins so we can continue to support each other while working remotely.

Damon: That's great to hear, Lola. And we mentioned in our first episode that you're also a designer, specifically creating jewelry and other accessories for your Amber Collective bar. Can you tell us more about this side of your business? Lola: Sure thing! So I actually started out as a fashion designer before transitioning into running the bar. But I've always been passionate about jewelry design, so I decided to incorporate that into my current business model. We create unique, handcrafted pieces using high-quality materials and techniques. It's definitely a labor of love for me, and it allows me to express my creativity in a different way than managing the bar.

Maggie: That's really cool, Lola. And it sounds like you've been able to find a nice balance between your different roles. So before we wrap up, do you have any advice for other moms who are trying to juggle multiple responsibilities? Lola: Absolutely! My biggest piece of advice would be to prioritize self-care and seek support when needed. It's important to remember that it's okay to ask for help and delegate tasks when necessary. And most importantly, don't forget to celebrate your successes along the way, no matter how small they may seem.

Damon: That's great advice, Lola. And we're really grateful to have you back on the show today. So thank you for sharing your insights with us and our listeners. And I think we'll leave it there, but if anyone has any questions or wants more information about Amber Collective or your jewelry line, they can always reach out to you through social media or on your website.

Maggie: Absolutely, Lola. And as we wrap up today's episode, remember to tune in next Wednesday for our next ATXR podcast. We can't wait to feature another amazing artist on the show. And until then, happy Mother's Day to everyone out there and stay safe. Bye-bye!

episodeTitle: Silver Lining: The Great Barbecue Dilemma on Memorial Day Weekend
summary: Tom Saunders and Scott Blakeman explore the concept of finding silver linings during challenging times, using a hypothetical scenario where Tom can't have his preferred barbecue food (fish) on Memorial Day. They discuss how to deal with unfulfilled expectations and find joy in what is available.
transcript: {Tom Saunders} (TS): Welcome back to Saunders & Blakeman. I'm your co-host, Tom Saunders.

{Scott Blakeman} (SB): And I'm Scott Blakeman, and today we're here to explore the concept of finding silver linings during challenging times. This Memorial Day weekend, our listeners may be feeling the pinch of unfulfilled expectations, especially when it comes to barbecues. So let's dive in.
{TS}: Absolutely, Scotty. I can't have a barbecue this Memorial Day. I just smell my neighbor's delicious aromas and wish I could join them. How do we find the silver lining in this situation?

{SB}: Well, Tom, you're not alone. Many of us are feeling this way right now. The power of positive creativity is key. Let's imagine a scenario where the barbecue doesn't quite meet your expectations.
{TS}: That’s fair. So let's say I'm in my neighborhood and everyone is having a barbecue today. Chicken, burgers, sausages—no fish on the grill. How do I handle this without seeming rude?
{SB}: First of all, Tom, consider why you wanted to eat fish. Was it just because of the day, or are you really craving it? Sometimes our desires change with the moment.
{TS}: That's a good point. Maybe I was thinking about fish earlier but now it doesn't matter as much. How do I communicate that without being awkward?

{SB}: You could start by acknowledging their efforts and then gently steer the conversation away from what you're missing. For example, you might say, 'Wow, this looks delicious! Can you believe how good the weather is for a barbecue? Maybe we can share some of these recipes later.'
{TS}: That sounds reasonable. And if they offer me something to eat, I should just take whatever I like?
{SB}: Exactly. You don’t have to explain yourself or feel guilty about not having your preferred meal. Enjoy what you have and appreciate the companionship.
{TS}: So let's step back a bit. What is the silver lining of this situation? How do we find something positive in missing out on our ideal barbecue?

{SB}: The silver lining, Tom, lies in recognizing that you already have many wonderful things to enjoy today. You don't need fish or any specific dish. Instead, focus on the present moment and the good times with your neighbors.
{TS}: I like that idea, Scotty. Even though it's not what I wanted, I can still appreciate the day for what it is. Maybe it's a reminder to try something new or to enjoy simpler pleasures.
{SB}: Exactly! And this mindset can help us find joy even when things don't go exactly as planned. It’s all about positive imagination and gratitude.
{TS}: Absolutely, Scotty. This Memorial Day weekend, let's focus on finding the silver linings in our daily lives and celebrating what we have. Thanks for tuning in to Saunders & Blakeman.
{SB}: You're welcome, Tom. Until next time, keep finding those silver linings.

title: Key Messages and Steps for Addressing the Opioid Crisis
transcript_summary: This conversation revolves around the opioid crisis, focusing on personal experiences, challenges in treatment, and advice for those dealing with addiction or supporting loved ones. Key points include recognizing the importance of community support, staying informed about resources, avoiding stigmatization, and encouraging open communication.

main_points.point: Community Support is Vital
main_points.description: The speaker emphasizes the significance of surrounding oneself with a supportive network during recovery.

main_points.point: Avoid Stigma and Shame
main_points.description: It's crucial to avoid feeling ashamed or stigmatized, acknowledging that addiction is a disease and not a personal failing.

main_points.point: Stay Informed About Resources
main_points.description: Educating oneself about available treatment options, support groups, and recovery resources can be beneficial for both those in recovery and their supporters.

main_points.point: Open Communication is Essential
main_points.description: Encouraging honest dialogue can help prevent misunderstandings and build trust between family members or friends supporting someone with addiction.

main_points.point: Self-Awareness and Patience
main_points.description: Maintaining self-awareness, setting realistic expectations, and offering patience to those in recovery are important for effective support.

key_takeaways: Community plays a crucial role in supporting individuals through the opioid crisis.
Recovery is possible with proper resources and a supportive environment; avoid stigmatizing addiction as a personal weakness.
Stay informed about treatment options, support groups, and other resources to assist those struggling with addiction.
Open communication and empathy are vital for helping someone navigate their journey towards recovery.

title: Jacob Perry - Part 2
transcript: Welcome back to The Political Nomad, where we explore the unique paths that lead politicians and political operatives from one state to another, shaping our country's landscape. Today, we continue our conversation with Jacob Perry, a man whose journey took him from Indiana to Florida, navigating the intricacies of local politics in both states.

In this episode, Jacob shares his experiences working on the 2004 campaign for Mitch Daniels and discusses how that experience ultimately led him back to Florida. He also talks about some of the challenges he faced as a political operative, including ethical dilemmas and navigating party dynamics. We dive into his work with several campaigns in Florida, including helping to elect a current member of Congress, and discuss the impact of these experiences on his career.
Join us as we explore the twists and turns of Jacob's political journey and how it has shaped his understanding of American politics.

Josh Gillespie: Welcome back to The Political Nomad. Today, we continue our conversation with Jacob Perry, a man whose political journey took him from Indiana to Florida. Let’s pick up where we left off. After working on Mitch Daniels' 2004 campaign in Indiana, what led you back to Florida?

Jacob Perry: Well, as I mentioned earlier, the flight school thing didn't work out for me. My wife and I had been trying to have a child, and she finally got pregnant. We decided we would go the flight attendant route with her moving to Southwest Airlines in Indianapolis while I finished up my training. But when I found out that I was going to be a father, it just wasn't something that fit into my future plans anymore. I needed a job, and Andy Horning called me about working on his congressional campaign.

Josh Gillespie: That's interesting because you were involved in Mitch Daniels' campaign in Indiana, but then you ended up working for Andy Horning in Florida. Can you tell us more about that transition?

Jacob Perry: Sure. After the flight school debacle, I went back to politics and got a full-time job as a campaign manager on Andy's congressional campaign. It was my first paid political position. We worked hard and managed to get him elected in 2004. That experience taught me a lot about working within the Republican party structure and navigating various political landscapes.
Josh Gillespie: And what did you learn from that experience?

Jacob Perry: One of the biggest things I learned was the importance of ethical behavior, especially when working for elected officials. We faced some challenges with fundraising and media strategies, but ultimately, we had to adhere to certain principles. That helped shape my approach to future campaigns.
Josh Gillespie: Can you give us an example of a challenge you faced during that campaign?

Jacob Perry: Absolutely. One of the biggest ethical dilemmas we encountered was related to fundraising. We were working with limited resources and had to be creative in how we solicited donations without overstepping boundaries or compromising our integrity. It's all about finding that balance between staying true to your principles and meeting campaign goals.
Josh Gillespie: You mentioned Andy Horning. What was his approach to campaigning, and how did you collaborate with him?

Jacob Perry: Andy is a straight-talking, no-nonsense guy who has a clear vision for what he wants to achieve in Congress. He's very direct in his communication and works hard to connect with constituents. Our collaboration was based on mutual respect and shared goals. We worked closely together to develop strategies that resonated with the voters.
Josh Gillespie: After helping Andy Horning win, did you continue working in politics or did you pursue other opportunities?

Jacob Perry: I stayed involved in local politics after the campaign. I worked on several other campaigns and continued to contribute my expertise. One of the highlights was when we helped a Republican candidate for state senate win her race. It was a significant victory, and it really showed that with hard work and dedication, you can make a difference.
Josh Gillespie: And how did your experiences in Florida shape your understanding of American politics?

Jacob Perry: Living and working in different states gave me a broader perspective on the political landscape. In Indiana, I saw firsthand how local politics can be influenced by national trends, while in Florida, I experienced the unique dynamics of a state with diverse demographics. It taught me that there's no one-size-fits-all approach to politics; each state has its own challenges and opportunities.
Josh Gillespie: You've had a diverse career in politics, working on various campaigns across different states. Looking back, what are some of the most important lessons you've learned?

Jacob Perry: The most important lesson is that persistence pays off. I've faced many ups and downs in my political career, but each experience has taught me valuable lessons. Whether it's ethical behavior, effective communication, or strategic planning, every campaign offers new challenges that help shape my understanding of what it takes to succeed in politics.

Josh Gillespie: It's been fascinating to hear about your journey so far. Jacob, thank you for sharing these insights with us. We'll continue to follow your story and explore how your experiences have influenced the political landscape across multiple states.
Jacob Perry: Thanks, Josh. I'm looking forward to continuing our conversation in future episodes.

title: Toto's Musical Journey with Jakeah Perry
transcript:
JoshKolesby: Welcome to The Political Nomad. I'm your host, Josh Kolesby, and today we have a special guest with us who's not only a good friend but also someone whose musical tastes run deep—Jakeah Perry! We dive into the world of Toto, discussing their incredible journey as a band, from their iconic hit 'Africa' to the nuances of their other masterpieces. So sit back, relax, and get ready for a musical road trip with The Political Nomad!

JoshKolesby: Jakeah, welcome back to the show! Thanks so much for being here.
Jakeah Perry: Hey Josh, it's great to be here again. Thank you for having me.
JoshKolesby: Let's dive right into the music. Toto has had quite a journey over the years, but 'Africa' is undoubtedly their biggest hit. What do you think makes that song so special?
Jakeah Perry: Absolutely, 'Africa' is definitely one of my all-time favorite songs. I think what sets it apart is its timeless melody and the seamless blend of rock and pop elements. The vocals are incredible, and Steve Lukather's guitar work just adds an extra layer of brilliance. It's one of those tracks that can bring people together regardless of their age or background.
JoshKolesby: That's a great point. Now, Toto had several other albums that were critically acclaimed but perhaps not as commercially successful. Can you tell us about 'Toto IV' and its significance?
Jakeah Perry: Sure! 'Toto IV' is an absolute masterpiece. It was their first studio album with the legendary guitarist Steve Lukather, who really brought a new dimension to the band's sound. The production quality is top-notch, and each song feels like a mini-orchestra in itself. Tracks like 'Rosanna,' which you mentioned earlier, are particularly brilliant. It's an album that showcases Toto at their most polished and versatile.
JoshKolesby: You're right about 'Rosanna.' That track has such intricate layers and changes in tempo. It really is a standout. Now, let's talk about some of the band members who contributed to these albums. Steve Lukather's contributions are well-known, but what about Drummer Jeff Porcaro? How do you think his style influenced Toto's sound?
Jakeah Perry: Jeff Porcaro was an absolute genius behind the drums. His precision and timing were unparalleled. He had this incredible ability to make every drum beat count while still adding a human touch to the music. His presence on albums like 'Toto IV' really solidified Toto as one of the premier studio bands in the 80s.
JoshKolesby: Speaking of precision, let's talk about Bruce Hornsby. He played keyboards for Toto during their later years, and he brought a unique touch to the band's sound. Can you share your thoughts on his contributions?
Jakeah Perry: Definitely! Bruce Hornsby was an incredible addition. His piano work and vocals added a lot of depth to their late 80s and early 90s material. His presence on tracks like '99 Ways to Lie' from the movie Get Smart soundtrack, or even the live album with Toto, shows how versatile he is as a musician. He brought a different energy to the band that was both refreshing and exciting.
JoshKolesby: That's true. Bruce Hornsby definitely added a new layer of complexity to their sound. Now, let's turn our attention to more recent times. 'Toto 4' and their last studio album, 'Island,' are often seen as polarizing. What do you think is the key factor that sets these albums apart from their earlier work?
Jakeah Perry: I think what sets them apart is a combination of factors. On one hand, they were trying to keep up with changing musical trends while still maintaining their signature sound. On the other hand, there's an evolution in their songwriting and production techniques. 'Toto 4' especially has some fantastic tracks like 'The Lady Is Not For Sale,' which showcase a more mature approach to their music.
JoshKolesby: That's interesting. You mentioned a few live albums that you're particularly fond of. Can you tell us why these are your favorites?
Jakeah Perry: Absolutely! One of my absolute favorites is 'Live on Long Valley Road' because it captures the raw energy and spontaneity of their live performances. Bruce Hornsby's presence really brings out a different side of Toto, making every performance unique. It's like watching a jazz band where everything changes from one song to another.
JoshKolesby: That sounds amazing! For those who haven't had the chance to experience it firsthand, you should definitely check out these live performances. Now, before we wrap up, any last thoughts or recommendations for our listeners who might be new to Toto's music?
Jakeah Perry: I'd recommend starting with 'Africa' and then moving on to 'Toto IV.' After that, explore their earlier work like 'Island.' And if you can, try to catch them in concert. The live experience is truly special.
JoshKolesby: Excellent advice! Jakeah, thank you so much for joining us today. This was a lot of fun and I hope our listeners enjoy diving into the world of Toto with your insights.
Jakeah Perry: Thanks Josh, it's always great talking to you. I appreciate you having me on the show!
JoshKolesby: You're welcome. And don't forget to follow Jakeah on Twitter at @vjakeupharry and check out his social media for more insights and musings. Until next time, keep tuning in to The Political Nomad!

content:
[主持人]: 大家好，欢迎收听Pedal to the Metal Podcast。我是你们的主持人[主持人姓名]。在这期节目里，我们将分享一些最新的音乐新闻，并讨论即将到来的虚拟演唱会和其他活动。让我们开始吧！

首先，10年前的今天，2010年5月17日，我们庆祝了Def Leppard的新专辑《X》的发行。这张专辑取得了巨大成功，获得了多个奖项和好评。

然后是32年前的这一天，也就是1988年5月17日，Judas Priest发布了他们的经典专辑《Ram It Down》，这张专辑被认为是他们回归金属风格的重要作品之一。

接下来是关于Shadows Fall的消息。由于疫情的影响，乐队成员Brian Fair、Paul等正在努力安排一些演出和活动。之前主持人还分享了一个有趣的故事：有一次在商场偶遇了Brian Fair，差点误会了他的出现。这真是一次难忘的相遇！

Steel Panther也在准备进行一场虚拟演唱会，名为《Live from the Doom Saloon Volume 1》，将与Crowbar、Blacktop Mojo和Saul合作演出。这场虚拟演唱会将于5月27日举行，门票仅需9美元。

最后是关于Code Orange的讨论。他们在Twitch上进行了一个特别表演，演奏了低音吉他和鼓，并回答了一些观众的问题。主持人有机会向Joe Goldman提问，询问他们在录制新专辑时的主要差异。他们表示这次录音的时间更加充裕，给了乐队更多的创作空间。

总之，希望你享受这一期的Pedal to the Metal Podcast，我们下周同一时间再见！
